Baal@1Ch.8.30-=H1168B.short: Baal was a son of Abiel and a descendant of Benjamin.

Baal-hanan@1Ch.27.28=H1177H.brief: An overseer of olive and sycamore trees under David.
Baal-hanan@1Ch.27.28=H1177H.short: Baal-hanan the Gederite was in charge of the olive and sycamore trees in the lowlands under David's reign.

Baal-hanan@Gen.36.38-1Ch=H1177G.short: Baal-hanan was a king of Edom who reigned before Israel had kings.

Baalis@Jer.40.14=H1185.brief: King of the Ammonites during the Babylonian exile.
Baalis@Jer.40.14=H1185.short: Baalis, the king of the Ammonites, sent Ishmael to assassinate Gedaliah the governor.

Baal-zebub@2Ki.1.2-=H1176.brief: A Philistine god worshiped at Ekron.
Baal-zebub@2Ki.1.2-=H1176.short: Baal-zebub was the god of Ekron whom Ahaziah consulted about his illness.

Baana@1Ki.4.12=H1195G.brief: One of Solomon's twelve district governors.
Baana@1Ki.4.12=H1195G.short: Baana son of Ahilud was one of Solomon's twelve district governors.

Baanah@2Sa.23.29-1Ch=H1196H.short: Baanah the Netophathite was one of David's mighty warriors.

Baanah@Neh.10.27=H1196J.short: Baanah was one of the leaders who sealed the covenant during Nehemiah's time.

Baara@1Ch.8.8=H1199.brief: A wife of Shaharaim, a Benjamite.
Baara@1Ch.8.8=H1199.short: Baara was one of the wives of Shaharaim, a descendant of Benjamin.

Baaseiah@1Ch.6.40=H1202.short: Baaseiah was a Levite descended from Gershom, the son of Levi.

Bakbakkar@1Ch.9.15=H1230.short: Bakbakkar was a Levite who resided in Jerusalem.

Bakbuk@Ezr.2.51-Neh=H1227.short: Bakbuk was the ancestor of a family of temple servants who returned from exile.

Bakbukiah@Neh.11.17-=H1229.short: Bakbukiah was a Levite who held leadership roles in Jerusalem after the exile.

Balak@Num.22.2-Rev=H1111.short: Balak, son of Zippor, was the king of Moab who tried to curse Israel through Balaam.

Bani@1Ch.6.46=H1137H.short: Bani was a Levite who served as a musician during David's reign.

Bani@1Ch.9.4=H1137I.short: Bani, a descendant of Perez, was among those who settled in Jerusalem.

Bani@2Sa.23.36=H1137G.brief: One of David's mighty warriors from the tribe of Gad.
Bani@2Sa.23.36=H1137G.short: Bani the Gadite was one of David's mighty warriors.

Bani@Ezr.10.34=H1137J.short: Bani was one of the men who had married foreign women and agreed to put them away.

Bani@Neh.10.14=H1137N.short: Bani was one of the leaders who sealed the covenant during Nehemiah's time.

Bani@Neh.11.22=H1137O.short: Bani was a Levite who served as an overseer in Jerusalem.

Bani@Neh.3.17=H1137L.short: Bani, a Levite, made repairs to a section of Jerusalem's wall.

Gaddiel@Num.13.10=H1427.short: Gaddiel, the son of Sodi, was the representative of the tribe of Zebulun among the twelve spies sent to explore Canaan.

Gadi@2Ki.15.14-=H1424.brief: Father of Menahem, king of Israel.
Gadi@2Ki.15.14-=H1424.short: Gadi was the father of Menahem, who became king of Israel after assassinating Shallum.

Gaham@Gen.22.24=H1514.short: Gaham was one of the sons born to Nahor, Abraham's brother, and his concubine Reumah.

Gahar@Ezr.2.47-Neh=H1515.brief: Ancestor of temple servants who returned from Babylonian exile.
Gahar@Ezr.2.47-Neh=H1515.short: Gahar was an ancestor of a group of temple servants (Nethinim) who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile.

Gaius@3Jn.1.1=G1050J.brief: Recipient of John's third epistle; commended for his faithfulness.
Gaius@3Jn.1.1=G1050J.short: Gaius, the recipient of John's third epistle, was commended for his faithfulness to the truth and his hospitality to traveling missionaries.

Gaius@Act.19.29=G1050G.brief: Macedonian; Paul's traveling companion; caught in Ephesian riot.
Gaius@Act.19.29=G1050G.short: Gaius, a Macedonian and traveling companion of Paul, was seized along with Aristarchus during the riot in Ephesus.

Gaius@Act.20.4=G1050H.brief: Derbean; accompanied Paul on his journey to Jerusalem.
Gaius@Act.20.4=G1050H.short: Gaius of Derbe accompanied Paul on his journey from Greece to Jerusalem, along with several others.

Gaius@Rom.16.23-1Co=G1050I.brief: Corinthian believer; host to Paul and the church.
Gaius@Rom.16.23-1Co=G1050I.short: Gaius, a Corinthian believer baptized by Paul, hosted Paul and the whole church in his home.

Galal@1Ch.9.15=H1559G.brief: Levite musician; descendant of Asaph; lived in Jerusalem.
Galal@1Ch.9.15=H1559G.short: Galal, a Levite musician and descendant of Asaph, lived in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.

Galal@1Ch.9.16-Neh=H1559H.brief: Levite musician; descendant of Jeduthun; lived in Jerusalem.
Galal@1Ch.9.16-Neh=H1559H.short: Galal, a Levite musician and descendant of Jeduthun, lived in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile and assisted in the temple service.

Gallio@Act.18.12-=G1058.brief: Roman proconsul of Achaia; refused to judge Paul.
Gallio@Act.18.12-=G1058.short: Gallio, the Roman proconsul of Achaia, refused to judge Paul when the Jews brought charges against him in Corinth.

Gamaliel@Act.5.34-=G1059.brief: Pharisee; teacher of the law; Paul's mentor.
Gamaliel@Act.5.34-=G1059.short: Gamaliel, a respected Pharisee and teacher of the law, was Paul's mentor and advised the Sanhedrin to be cautious in their treatment of the apostles.

Gamaliel@Num.1.10-=H1583.brief: Leader of the tribe of Manasseh during the Exodus.
Gamaliel@Num.1.10-=H1583.short: Gamaliel, the son of Pedahzur, was the leader of the tribe of Manasseh during the Israelites' journey through the wilderness.

Gamul@1Ch.24.17=H1577.brief: Head of a priestly division in David's time.
Gamul@1Ch.24.17=H1577.short: Gamul was the head of the twenty-second priestly division organized during King David's reign.

Gareb@2Sa.23.38-1Ch=H1619G.brief: One of David's mighty warriors; an Ithrite.
Gareb@2Sa.23.38-1Ch=H1619G.short: Gareb the Ithrite was one of David's mighty warriors, known for his military prowess.

Garmites@1Ch.4.19=H1636.short: The Garmites, living in Keilah, were perhaps descendants of Gerem of Judah.

Gatam@Gen.36.11-1Ch=H1609.brief: Son of Eliphaz; grandson of Esau; Edomite chief.
Gatam@Gen.36.11-1Ch=H1609.short: Gatam was a son of Eliphaz, grandson of Esau, and one of the chiefs of Edom.

Gazez@1Ch.2.46a=H1495G.brief: Son of Caleb and his concubine Ephah.
Gazez@1Ch.2.46a=H1495G.short: Gazez was a son of Caleb and his concubine Ephah, born after Haran.

Gazez@1Ch.2.46b=H1495H.short: Gazez was a grandson of Caleb, born to Haran's son Gazez.

Gazzam@Ezr.2.48-Neh=H1502.brief: Ancestor of temple servants who returned from Babylonian exile.
Gazzam@Ezr.2.48-Neh=H1502.short: Gazzam was an ancestor of a group of temple servants (Nethinim) who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile.

Geber@1Ki.4.19=H1398.brief: Son of Uri; one of Solomon's twelve district governors.
Geber@1Ki.4.19=H1398.short: Geber, the son of Uri, was one of the twelve district governors appointed by King Solomon to provide food for the royal household.

Gedaliah@1Ch.25.3-=H1436I.brief: Son of Jeduthun; a temple musician during David's reign.
Gedaliah@1Ch.25.3-=H1436I.short: Gedaliah, a son of Jeduthun, was one of the temple musicians appointed by King David to prophesy with lyres, harps, and cymbals.

Gedaliah@2Ki.25.22-Jer=H1436B.brief: Appointed governor of Judah by Babylonians; assassinated by Ishmael.
Gedaliah@2Ki.25.22-Jer=H1436B.short: Gedaliah, appointed governor of Judah by the Babylonians after the fall of Jerusalem, was assassinated by Ishmael, leading to the flight of the remaining Jews to Egypt.

Gedaliah@Ezr.10.18=H1436A.brief: Priest who married a foreign woman during the Exile.
Gedaliah@Ezr.10.18=H1436A.short: Gedaliah, a priest, was among those who had married foreign women during the Babylonian exile and pledged to put them away.

Gedaliah@Jer.38.1=H1436J.brief: Son of Pashhur; an official during Zedekiah's reign.
Gedaliah@Jer.38.1=H1436J.short: Gedaliah, the son of Pashhur, was one of the officials who heard Jeremiah's message and urged King Zedekiah to put him to death.

Gedaliah@Zep.1.1=H1436H.short: Gedaliah was the grandfather of the prophet Zephaniah, who prophesied during the reign of King Josiah of Judah.

Gedor@1Ch.8.31-=H1446I.brief: Son of Abiel, the founder of Gibeon.
Gedor@1Ch.8.31-=H1446I.short: Gedor was a son of Abiel (or 'Jeiel'), the father (ie re-founder) of Gibeon, and an ancestor of King Saul.

Gehazi@2Ki.4.12-=H1522.brief: Elisha's servant; punished with leprosy for greed and deceit.
Gehazi@2Ki.4.12-=H1522.short: Gehazi, the servant of the prophet Elisha, was punished with leprosy for his greed and deceit in the matter of Naaman's healing.

Gemalli@Num.13.12=H1582.brief: Father of Ammiel, the spy from the tribe of Dan.
Gemalli@Num.13.12=H1582.short: Gemalli was the father of Ammiel, who represented the tribe of Dan as one of the twelve spies sent to explore Canaan.

Gemariah@Jer.29.3=H1587G.brief: Son of Hilkiah; messenger sent by Zedekiah to Nebuchadnezzar.
Gemariah@Jer.29.3=H1587G.short: Gemariah, the son of Hilkiah, was a messenger sent by King Zedekiah of Judah to deliver a letter to King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon.

Gemariah@Jer.36.10-=H1587H.brief: Son of Shaphan; official during Jehoiakim's reign; opposed burning scroll.
Gemariah@Jer.36.10-=H1587H.short: Gemariah, the son of Shaphan, was an official during King Jehoiakim's reign who opposed the burning of Jeremiah's scroll.

Genubath@1Ki.11.20=H1592.brief: Son of Hadad the Edomite; raised in Pharaoh's palace.
Genubath@1Ki.11.20=H1592.short: Genubath was the son of Hadad the Edomite and was raised in Pharaoh's palace alongside the Pharaoh's own children.

Gera@1Ch.8.3=H1617I.brief: Son of Bela, grandson of Benjamin.
Gera@1Ch.8.3=H1617I.short: Gera was a son of Bela and a grandson of Benjamin.

Gera@1Ch.8.7=H1617J.short: Gera (or Heglam) was a son of Ehud, a Benjamite, and was among those who were carried into exile.

Gera@2Sa.16.5-1Ki=H1617H.brief: Benjamite; cursed David during Absalom's rebellion; later sought forgiveness.
Gera@2Sa.16.5-1Ki=H1617H.short: Gera was a Benjamite who cursed David during Absalom's rebellion but later sought forgiveness when David returned to Jerusalem.

Gera@Gen.46.21-1Ch=H1617G.brief: Descendant of Benjamin; ancestor of Ehud, a judge of Israel.
Gera@Gen.46.21-1Ch=H1617G.short: Gera was a descendant of Benjamin and an ancestor of Ehud, a left-handed judge who delivered Israel from Moabite oppression.

Gershom@Exo.2.22-1Ch=H1647G.brief: Son of Moses; father of Jonathan, a renegade priest.
Gershom@Exo.2.22-1Ch=H1647G.short: Gershom was the firstborn son of Moses and Zipporah, and his descendant Jonathan served as a priest for the idolatrous Danites.

Gershom@Ezr.8.2=H1647I.brief: Descendant of Phinehas; returned to Jerusalem with Ezra.
Gershom@Ezr.8.2=H1647I.short: Gershom, a descendant of Phinehas, was among the men who returned to Jerusalem with Ezra after the Babylonian exile.

Gershon@Gen.46.11-2Ch=H1648.brief: Firstborn son of Levi; head of the Gershonite Levites.
Gershon@Gen.46.11-2Ch=H1648.short: Gershon was the firstborn son of Levi and the ancestor of the Gershonite Levites, who were responsible for the tabernacle curtains, coverings, and related duties.

Geshan@1Ch.2.47=H1529.brief: Son of Jahdai, a descendant of Caleb.
Geshan@1Ch.2.47=H1529.short: Geshan was a son of Jahdai, a wife of Caleb, from the tribe of Judah.

Geshem@Neh.2.19-=H1654.brief: Arab opponent of Nehemiah; tried to hinder wall rebuilding.
Geshem@Neh.2.19-=H1654.short: Geshem the Arab, along with Sanballat and Tobiah, opposed Nehemiah's efforts to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem and tried to intimidate and discourage him.

Gether@Gen.10.23-1Ch=H1666.brief: Son of Aram; grandson of Shem; part of Table of Nations.
Gether@Gen.10.23-1Ch=H1666.short: Gether was a son of Aram and a grandson of Shem, mentioned in the genealogies of the Table of Nations.

Geuel@Num.13.15=H1345.brief: Son of Machi; representative of Gad among the twelve spies.
Geuel@Num.13.15=H1345.short: Geuel, the son of Machi, was the representative of the tribe of Gad among the twelve spies sent by Moses to explore Canaan.

Gibea@1Ch.2.49=H1388.brief: With Machbenah, daughters or towns of Sheva.
Gibea@1Ch.2.49=H1388.short: Gibea, with Machbenah, daughters or cities founded by Sheva.

Giddalti@1Ch.25.4-=H1437.brief: Son of Heman; a temple musician during David's reign.
Giddalti@1Ch.25.4-=H1437.short: Giddalti was one of the sons of Heman, appointed by King David as a temple musician to prophesy with lyres, harps, and cymbals.

Giddel@Ezr.2.47-Neh=H1435G.brief: Ancestor of temple servants who returned from Babylonian exile.
Giddel@Ezr.2.47-Neh=H1435G.short: Giddel was an ancestor of a group of temple servants (Nethinim) who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile.

Giddel@Ezr.2.56-Neh=H1435H.brief: Ancestor of Solomon's servants who returned from Babylonian exile.
Giddel@Ezr.2.56-Neh=H1435H.short: Giddel was an ancestor of a group of Solomon's servants who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile.

Gideon@Jdg.6.11-Heb=H1439.brief: Judge of Israel; defeated Midianites; tested and reassured by God.
Gideon@Jdg.6.11-Heb=H1439.short: Gideon, also called Jerubbaal or Jerubbesheth, was a judge of Israel who, with God's help, defeated the Midianites and delivered Israel from oppression.

Gideoni@Num.1.11-=H1441.brief: Leader of the tribe of Benjamin during the Exodus.
Gideoni@Num.1.11-=H1441.short: Gideoni, the son of Abidan, was the leader of the tribe of Benjamin during the Israelites' journey through the wilderness.

Gilalai@Neh.12.36=H1562.brief: Priest and musician during the dedication of Jerusalem's wall.
Gilalai@Neh.12.36=H1562.short: Gilalai was a priest and musician who participated in the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem during Nehemiah's time.

Gilead@1Ch.5.14=H1568J.brief: Descendant of Manasseh; son of Michael; father of Jaroah.
Gilead@1Ch.5.14=H1568J.short: Gilead, a descendant of Manasseh, was the son of Michael and the father of Jaroah, as recorded in the genealogy of the tribe of Gad.

Gilead@Jdg.11.1-=H1568I.brief: Father of Jephthah, a judge of Israel.
Gilead@Jdg.11.1-=H1568I.short: Gilead was the father of Jephthah, a mighty warrior and judge of Israel who delivered the Israelites from the Ammonites.

Gilead@Num.26.29-1Ch=H1568H.brief: Son of Machir; grandson of Manasseh; father of six sons.
Gilead@Num.26.29-1Ch=H1568H.short: Gilead was the son of Machir, grandson of Manasseh, and father of six sons who became the heads of Gileadite clans.

Ginath@1Ki.16.21-=H1527.brief: Father of Tibni, who opposed Omri for kingship.
Ginath@1Ki.16.21-=H1527.short: Ginath was the father of Tibni, who contended with Omri for the throne of Israel.

Ginnethon@Neh.10.6-=H1599.brief: A priest who sealed the covenant during Nehemiah's time.
Ginnethon@Neh.10.6-=H1599.short: Ginnethon, a priest, was among those who sealed the covenant during Nehemiah's reforms.

Girgashites@Gen.10.16-Neh=H1622.brief: A Canaanite people group living in the Promised Land.
Girgashites@Gen.10.16-Neh=H1622.short: The Girgashites were one of the Canaanite groups inhabiting the land promised to Abraham's descendants.

Girzites@1Sa.27.8=H1511.brief: A people group David raided while living among the Philistines.
Girzites@1Sa.27.8=H1511.short: The Girzites were a people group David raided during his time living in Philistine territory.

Gishpa@Neh.11.21=H1658.brief: An overseer of the temple servants during Nehemiah's time.
Gishpa@Neh.11.21=H1658.short: Gishpa was an overseer of the temple servants (Nethinim) during Nehemiah's time.

Gizonites@1Ch.11.34=H1493.brief: A people group mentioned in the Old Testament.
Gizonites@1Ch.11.34=H1493.short: The Gizonites are mentioned in 1Ch.11.34 without any additional context.

Gog@1Ch.5.4=H1463G.brief: A descendant of Reuben, son of Joel.
Gog@1Ch.5.4=H1463G.short: Gog, a descendant of Reuben, is mentioned in the genealogy of Reuben in 1Ch.5.4.

Goiim@Gen.14.1-Jos=H1471B.brief: A king of Goyim who fought against Chedorlaomer.
Goiim@Gen.14.1-Jos=H1471B.short: Tidal, king of Goiim (nations), was one of the kings who fought against Chedorlaomer in Genesis 14.

Goliath@1Sa.17.4-1Ch=H1555.brief: A Philistine giant defeated by David.
Goliath@1Sa.17.4-1Ch=H1555.short: Goliath was the Philistine champion from Gath who was defeated by David in a battle.

Gomer@Gen.10.2-Ezk=H1586G.brief: Son of Japheth; father of Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
Gomer@Gen.10.2-Ezk=H1586G.short: Gomer, a son of Japheth, was the father of Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah, as listed in the Table of Nations.

Gomer@Hos.1.3=H1586H.short: Gomer, the daughter of Diblaim, was the wife of the prophet Hosea.

Guni@1Ch.5.15=H1476H.brief: A descendant of Gad; father of Abdiel.
Guni@1Ch.5.15=H1476H.short: Guni, a descendant of Gad, was the father of Abdiel, as mentioned in the genealogy of Gad.

Guni@Gen.46.24-1Ch=H1476G.brief: Son of Naphtali, grandson of Jacob.
Guni@Gen.46.24-1Ch=H1476G.short: Guni was a son of Naphtali and a grandson of Jacob, as listed in the genealogies of Genesis and Numbers.

Haahashtari@1Ch.4.6=H0326.brief: A descendant of Judah through Hezron.
Haahashtari@1Ch.4.6=H0326.short: Haahashtari was a descendant of Judah through Hezron, as listed in the genealogy in 1 Chronicles.

Habaiah@Ezr.2.61-Neh=H2252.brief: A priest whose descendants were unable to prove their lineage.
Habaiah@Ezr.2.61-Neh=H2252.short: Habaiah was a priest whose descendants were excluded from the priesthood due to insufficient genealogical records.

Habakkuk@Hab.1.1-=H2265.brief: A prophet who questioned God's justice.
Habakkuk@Hab.1.1-=H2265.short: Habakkuk, a prophet, wrote the book bearing his name, which records his dialogue with God about justice and faith.

Habazziniah@Jer.35.3=H2262.brief: Grandfather of Jaazaniah, a Rechabite leader.
Habazziniah@Jer.35.3=H2262.short: Habazziniah was the grandfather of Jaazaniah, a leader of the Rechabites during Jeremiah's time.

Hacaliah@Neh.1.1-=H2446.brief: Father of Nehemiah, the governor of Judah.
Hacaliah@Neh.1.1-=H2446.short: Hacaliah was the father of Nehemiah, who served as the governor of Judah during the Persian period.

Hachmoni@1Ch.27.32=H2453H.brief: Father of Jehiel, one of David's family servants.
Hachmoni@1Ch.27.32=H2453H.short: Hachmoni was the father of Jehiel who, with Jonathan attended King David's sons.

Hachmonites@2Sa.23.8-1Ch=H2453G.brief: A clan or family known for their mighty warriors.
Hachmonites@2Sa.23.8-1Ch=H2453G.short: The Hachmonites, also known as the Tahchemonites, were a clan or family that produced some of David's mighty warriors.

Hadad@1Ki.11.14-=H1908I.brief: An Edomite prince who opposed Solomon.
Hadad@1Ki.11.14-=H1908I.short: Hadad, an Edomite prince, fled to Egypt and later became an adversary to King Solomon.

Hadad@Gen.25.15-1Ch=H2301.brief: A son of Ishmael, Abraham's son.
Hadad@Gen.25.15-1Ch=H2301.short: Hadad was one of the twelve sons of Ishmael, Abraham's son.

Hadad@Gen.36.35-1Ch=H1908G.short: Hadad, son of Bedad, became king of Edom after Husham's death.

Hadad@Gen.36.39-1Ch=H1908H.brief: The last king of Edom before Israelite rule.
Hadad@Gen.36.39-1Ch=H1908H.short: Hadad, also known as Hadar, was the last king of Edom before the Israelites established their monarchy.

Hadadezer@2Sa.8.3-1Ch=H1909.brief: King of Zobah, defeated by David.
Hadadezer@2Sa.8.3-1Ch=H1909.short: Hadadezer, king of Zobah, was defeated by King David in battle, and his allies, the Arameans, became subject to Israel.

Hadlai@2Ch.28.12=H2311.brief: Father of Amasa, who opposed taking captives from Judah.
Hadlai@2Ch.28.12=H2311.short: Hadlai was the father of Amasa, who opposed taking captives from Judah during the reign of King Ahaz.

Hadoram@Gen.10.27-1Ch=H1913A.brief: Son of Joktan, a descendant of Shem.
Hadoram@Gen.10.27-1Ch=H1913A.short: Hadoram was a son of Joktan and a descendant of Shem, mentioned in the genealogies of Genesis and 1 Chronicles.

Hagab@Ezr.2.46=H2285.brief: A temple servant who returned from Babylonian exile.
Hagab@Ezr.2.46=H2285.short: Hagab was among the temple servants who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian captivity, as recorded in Ezra.

Hagabah@Ezr.2.45-Neh=H2286B.brief: A temple servant who returned from Babylonian exile.
Hagabah@Ezr.2.45-Neh=H2286B.short: Hagabah, also known as Hagaba, was among the temple servants who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian captivity.

Hagar@Gen.16.1-Gal=H1904.brief: Sarah's Egyptian maidservant; mother of Ishmael.
Hagar@Gen.16.1-Gal=H1904.short: Hagar, Sarah's Egyptian maidservant, bore Abraham a son named Ishmael and is also mentioned in Paul's allegory in Galatians.

Haggai@Ezr.5.1-Hag=H2292A.brief: A prophet who encouraged the rebuilding of the temple.
Haggai@Ezr.5.1-Hag=H2292A.short: Haggai, a prophet during the post-exilic period, urged the people to rebuild the temple in Jerusalem.

Haggedolim@Neh.11.14=H1419B.brief: A priest mentioned in Nehemiah's time.
Haggedolim@Neh.11.14=H1419B.short: Haggedolim was a priest during the time of Nehemiah, mentioned in the list of priests and Levites.

Haggi@Gen.46.16-Num=H2291.brief: Son of Gad, grandson of Jacob.
Haggi@Gen.46.16-Num=H2291.short: Haggi was a son of Gad and a grandson of Jacob, mentioned in the genealogies of Genesis and Numbers.

Haggiah@1Ch.6.30=H2293.short: Haggiah, a Levite descended from Merari, is mentioned in the genealogy of the Levites in 1 Chronicles.

Haggith@2Sa.3.4-1Ch=H2294.brief: One of David's wives; mother of Adonijah.
Haggith@2Sa.3.4-1Ch=H2294.short: Haggith was one of King David's wives and the mother of Adonijah, who attempted to claim the throne.

Hagri@1Ch.5.10-Psa=H1905.brief: A Gadite, father of Mibhar, one of David's mighty men.
Hagri@1Ch.5.10-Psa=H1905.short: Hagri was the father of Mibhar, one of David's mighty men from the tribe of Gad.

Hakkatan@Ezr.8.12=H6997.brief: Father of Johanan, a leader who returned from Babylon.
Hakkatan@Ezr.8.12=H6997.short: Hakkatan was the father of Johanan, a leader who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian exile.

Hakkoz@1Ch.24.10=H6976H.brief: A priest in the time of David.
Hakkoz@1Ch.24.10=H6976H.short: Hakkoz was a priest who served during the reign of King David, as mentioned in the priestly divisions.

Hakkoz@Ezr.2.61-Neh=H6976I.brief: A post-exilic priest whose descendants were excluded from the priesthood.
Hakkoz@Ezr.2.61-Neh=H6976I.short: Hakkoz was a priest whose descendants were unable to prove their priestly lineage after the Babylonian exile.

Hakkoz@Neh.3.4-=H6976J.brief: A priest who helped repair the wall of Jerusalem.
Hakkoz@Neh.3.4-=H6976J.short: Hakkoz, a priest, was involved in repairing sections of the wall of Jerusalem during Nehemiah's time.

Hakupha@Ezr.2.51-Neh=H2709.brief: A temple servant who returned from Babylonian exile.
Hakupha@Ezr.2.51-Neh=H2709.short: Hakupha was among the temple servants who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian captivity.

Hallohesh@Neh.3.12-=H3873.brief: Father of Shallum, a leader who helped repair Jerusalem's wall.
Hallohesh@Neh.3.12-=H3873.short: Hallohesh was the father of Shallum, a leader who helped repair the wall of Jerusalem during Nehemiah's time.

Ham@Gen.5.32-1Ch=H2526G.brief: One of Noah's three sons, father of Canaan.
Ham@Gen.5.32-1Ch=H2526G.short: Ham, one of Noah's three sons, was the father of Canaan and the ancestor of various nations.

Haman@Est.3.1-=H2001.brief: A Persian official who plotted to destroy the Jews.
Haman@Est.3.1-=H2001.short: Haman, a high-ranking Persian official, conspired to kill all the Jews in the empire but was ultimately thwarted by Queen Esther and Mordecai.

Hamathites@Gen.10.18-1Ch=H2577.brief: A Canaanite people group descended from Canaan.
Hamathites@Gen.10.18-1Ch=H2577.short: The Hamathites were a Canaanite people group descended from Canaan, son of Ham.

Hammath@1Ch.2.55=H2575B.brief: A Kenite clan, descendants of Salma.
Hammath@1Ch.2.55=H2575B.short: Hammath was a Kenite clan, listed among the descendants of Salma, the father (ie founder) of Bethlehem.

Hammedatha@Est.3.1-=H4099.brief: The father of Haman, the enemy of the Jews.
Hammedatha@Est.3.1-=H4099.short: Hammedatha was the father of Haman, the Persian official who plotted to destroy the Jews in the book of Esther.

Hammelech@Jer.36.26-=H4428H.brief: Father of Jerahmeel and Malchijah (or 'Malchiah'), officials during Jeremiah's time.
Hammelech@Jer.36.26-=H4428H.short: Hammelech, meaning "the king," was the father of Jerahmeel and Malchijah (or 'Malchiah'), officials mentioned in the book of Jeremiah.

Hammolecheth@1Ch.7.18=H4447G.brief: Sister of Gilead; mother of Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah.
Hammolecheth@1Ch.7.18=H4447G.short: Hammolecheth, the sister of Gilead, was the mother of Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah.

Hammuel@1Ch.4.26=H2536.brief: Son of Mishma, a descendant of Simeon.
Hammuel@1Ch.4.26=H2536.short: Hammuel, a descendant of Simeon, was the son of Mishma.

Iddo@1Ch.27.21=H3035G.short: Iddo, the son of Zechariah, was a leader of the half-tribe of Manasseh during King David's reign.

Iddo@1Ch.6.21-=H5714H.brief: A Levite in the genealogy of temple singers
Iddo@1Ch.6.21-=H5714H.short: Iddo (or Adaiah), a Levite in the genealogy of the temple singers.

Iddo@1Ki.4.14=H5714G.brief: Abinadab's son, an official under King Solomon
Iddo@1Ki.4.14=H5714G.short: Iddo, the son of Abinadab, was an official in Mahanaim during King Solomon's reign.

Iddo@2Ch.9.29-=H5714I.brief: A seer and prophet during the divided monarchy
Iddo@2Ch.9.29-=H5714I.short: Iddo, a seer and prophet who recorded the events of the reigns of Solomon, Rehoboam, and Abijah.

Iddo@Ezr.5.1-Zec=H5714J.brief: Zechariah's grandfather, a priest and prophet in post-exilic Judah
Iddo@Ezr.5.1-Zec=H5714J.short: Iddo, the grandfather of the prophet Zechariah, was a priest and prophet in post-exilic Judah.

Iddo@Ezr.8.17=H0112.brief: A prophet in Casiphia during Ezra's time.
Iddo@Ezr.8.17=H0112.short: Iddo was a prophet in Casiphia to whom Ezra sent a message requesting Levites to assist in the temple service.

Iddo@Neh.12.4-=H5714K.brief: A priest during the time of Zerubbabel.
Iddo@Neh.12.4-=H5714K.short: Iddo, also known as Adaia, was a priest who returned to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel and was head of a priestly family during the time of Joiakim.

Igal@1Ch.3.22=H3008I.short: Igal was a descendant of King David, mentioned in the genealogy of David's descendants through his son Jeconiah.

Igal@2Sa.23.36=H3008H.short: Igal son of Nathan of Zobah was listed among David's mighty warriors known for their military prowess and bravery.

Igal@Num.13.7=H3008G.brief: A scout from the tribe of Issachar.
Igal@Num.13.7=H3008G.short: Igal son of Joseph, from the tribe of Issachar, was one of the twelve scouts sent by Moses to explore Canaan.

Igdaliah@Jer.35.4=H3012.brief: A man of God during Jeremiah's time.
Igdaliah@Jer.35.4=H3012.short: Igdaliah, a man of God, was associated with a chamber in the house of the Lord during the time of the prophet Jeremiah.

Ikkesh@2Sa.23.26-1Ch=H6142.brief: Father of Ira, one of David's mighty warriors.
Ikkesh@2Sa.23.26-1Ch=H6142.short: Ikkesh the Tekoite was the father of Ira, one of King David's mighty warriors and a leader in his army.

Imlah@1Ki.22.8-2Ch=H3229.short: Imlah was the father of Micaiah, a prophet who spoke the truth to King Ahab of Israel, despite the king's displeasure.

Immer@1Ch.24.14-Jer=H0564H.brief: A priestly division and its descendants.
Immer@1Ch.24.14-Jer=H0564H.short: Immer was the name of a priestly division during the time of David, and his descendants served as priests in the post-exilic period.

Immer@1Ch.9.12-Neh=H0564G.brief: A priestly family in post-exilic Jerusalem.
Immer@1Ch.9.12-Neh=H0564G.short: The descendants of Immer were a priestly family who lived in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile, as recorded in 1 Chronicles and Nehemiah.

Immer@Neh.3.29=H0564J.brief: Man who repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall
Immer@Neh.3.29=H0564J.short: Immer was one of the people who helped repair the wall of Jerusalem during Nehemiah's time.

Imna@1Ch.7.35=H3234.short: Imna was a descendant of Asher, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher in 1 Chronicles.

Imnah@2Ch.31.14=H3232H.short: Imnah, a Levite, was appointed as an overseer of the freewill offerings during the religious reforms of King Hezekiah.

Imnah@Gen.46.17-1Ch=H3232G.brief: A son of Asher and ancestor of the Imnites.
Imnah@Gen.46.17-1Ch=H3232G.short: Imnah was a son of Asher and the ancestor of the Imnite clan within the tribe of Asher.

Imrah@1Ch.7.36=H3236.short: Imrah was a descendant of Asher, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher in 1 Chronicles.

Imri@1Ch.9.4=H0566G.brief: A descendant of Judah who lived in Jerusalem.
Imri@1Ch.9.4=H0566G.short: Imri, a descendant of Perez from the tribe of Judah, was among those who settled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.

Imri@Neh.3.2=H0566H.brief: Father of Zaccur, helped rebuild Jerusalem's wall.
Imri@Neh.3.2=H0566H.short: Imri was the father of Zaccur, who helped rebuild the wall of Jerusalem.

Iphdeiah@1Ch.8.25=H3301.short: Iphdeiah was a descendant of Benjamin through Shashak.

Ir@1Ch.7.12=H5893G.brief: Son of Bela, descendant of Benjamin.
Ir@1Ch.7.12=H5893G.short: Ir was a son of Bela and descendant of Benjamin.

Ira@2Sa.20.26=H5896G.short: Ira the Jairite was a priest under King David.

Ira@2Sa.23.26-1Ch=H5896H.brief: One of David's Thirty warriors, from Tekoa.
Ira@2Sa.23.26-1Ch=H5896H.short: Ira the Tekoite was one of King David's Thirty mighty warriors.

Ira@2Sa.23.38-1Ch=H5896I.brief: One of David's Thirty warriors, an Ithrite.
Ira@2Sa.23.38-1Ch=H5896I.short: Ira the Ithrite was one of King David's Thirty mighty warriors.

Irad@Gen.4.18=H5897.brief: Descendant of Cain; father of Mehujael.
Irad@Gen.4.18=H5897.short: Irad was a descendant of Cain and the father of Mehujael.

Iram@Gen.36.43-1Ch=H5902.short: Iram was an Edomite chief, a descendant of Esau.

Iri@1Ch.7.7=H5901.brief: Son of Bela, grandson of Benjamin.
Iri@1Ch.7.7=H5901.short: Iri was a son of Bela and grandson of Benjamin.

Irijah@Jer.37.13-=H3376.brief: Captain who arrested Jeremiah for desertion.
Irijah@Jer.37.13-=H3376.short: Irijah, a captain, arrested Jeremiah on suspicion of desertion to the Babylonians.

Iru@1Ch.4.15=H5900.brief: Son of Caleb, brother of Elah and Naam.
Iru@1Ch.4.15=H5900.short: Iru was a son of Caleb, along with his brothers Elah and Naam.

Isaac@Gen.17.19-Jas=H3327.brief: Son of Abraham; father of Jacob and Esau.
Isaac@Gen.17.19-Jas=H3327.short: Isaac was the son of Abraham and Sarah, and the father of Jacob and Esau. God made a covenant with him, renewing the promises given to Abraham.

Isaiah@2Ki.19.2-Rom=H3470A.brief: Prophet during reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, Hezekiah.
Isaiah@2Ki.19.2-Rom=H3470A.short: Isaiah was a prophet in Judah during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah. His prophecies are recorded in the biblical book bearing his name.

Iscah@Gen.11.29=H3252.brief: Daughter of Haran, Milcah's sister, Lot's sister.
Iscah@Gen.11.29=H3252.short: Iscah was the daughter of Haran and sister of Milcah and Lot.

Ishbah@1Ch.4.17=H3431.brief: Son of Mered in the genealogy of Judah
Ishbah@1Ch.4.17=H3431.short: Ishbah's sons were the father (ie founder) of Eshtemoa and Keilah, mentioned in the genealogy of Judah..

Ishbak@Gen.25.2-1Ch=H3435.short: Ishbak was a son of Abraham and his concubine Keturah.

Ishbi-benob@2Sa.21.16=H3430.brief: Philistine giant who fought against David's men.
Ishbi-benob@2Sa.21.16=H3430.short: Ishbi-benob, a Philistine giant, was killed by David's warrior Abishai when he threatened David's life.

Ish-bosheth@2Sa.2.8-1Ch=H0378.brief: Son of Saul, king over Israel.
Ish-bosheth@2Sa.2.8-1Ch=H0378.short: Ish-bosheth (also called Eshbaal), Saul's son, was made king over Israel by Abner but was ultimately assassinated, leading to David's rule over all Israel.

Ishhod@1Ch.7.18=H0379.short: Ishhod was the son of Hammoleketh, who was the sister of Manasseh.

Ishi@1Ch.2.31=H3469G.brief: Son of Appaim, descendant of Judah.
Ishi@1Ch.2.31=H3469G.short: Ishi was a descendant of Judah through Appaim.

Ishi@1Ch.4.20=H3469H.brief: Son of Shimon, descendant of Judah.
Ishi@1Ch.4.20=H3469H.short: Ishi was a son of Shimon, a descendant of Judah.

Ishi@1Ch.4.42=H3469I.brief: Leader of Simeonites who attacked Hamites in Gedor.
Ishi@1Ch.4.42=H3469I.short: Ishi was one of the leaders of the Simeonites who attacked the Hamites in Gedor during the days of Hezekiah.

Ishi@1Ch.5.24=H3469J.brief: Head of a father's house in Manasseh.
Ishi@1Ch.5.24=H3469J.short: Ishi was a head of a father's house in the half-tribe of Manasseh.

Ishma@1Ch.4.3=H3457.brief: Son of Hur, descendant of Judah.
Ishma@1Ch.4.3=H3457.short: Ishma was a son of Hur, a descendant of Judah.

Ishmael@1Ch.8.38-=H3458I.brief: Descendant of Benjamin through Saul's line.
Ishmael@1Ch.8.38-=H3458I.short: Ishmael was a descendant of Benjamin through King Saul's line.

Ishmael@2Ch.19.11=H3458J.short: Ishmael son of Jehohanan was a leader in Judah during King Jehoshaphat's reign.

Ishmael@2Ch.23.1=H3458K.brief: Son of Jehohanan; supported Joash as king.
Ishmael@2Ch.23.1=H3458K.short: Ishmael was the son of Jehohanan, who supported Jehoiada in making Joash king.

Ishmael@2Ki.25.23-Jer=H3458H.brief: Assassinated Gedaliah the governor; led captives to Ammon.
Ishmael@2Ki.25.23-Jer=H3458H.short: Ishmael, son of Nethaniah, assassinated Gedaliah the governor and led captives to Ammon before being pursued by Johanan.

Ishmael@Ezr.10.22=H3458L.brief: Priest who married a foreign woman during Ezra's time.
Ishmael@Ezr.10.22=H3458L.short: Ishmael was a priest who had married a foreign woman and pledged to put her away during Ezra's reforms.

Ishmael@Gen.16.11-Psa=H3458G.brief: Son of Abraham and Hagar; father of Arab tribes.
Ishmael@Gen.16.11-Psa=H3458G.short: Ishmael, the son of Abraham and Hagar, was the ancestor of various Arab tribes. Though not the chosen heir, he was still blessed by God.

Ishmaiah@1Ch.12.4=H3460G.brief: Gibeonite warrior who joined David at Ziklag.
Ishmaiah@1Ch.12.4=H3460G.short: Ishmaiah the Gibeonite was a mighty warrior among the Thirty who joined David at Ziklag.

Ishmaiah@1Ch.27.19=H3460H.brief: Leader of the tribe of Zebulun under David.
Ishmaiah@1Ch.27.19=H3460H.short: Ishmaiah son of Obadiah was the leader of the tribe of Zebulun during King David's reign.

Ishmerai@1Ch.8.18=H3461.short: Ishmerai was a descendant of Benjamin through Elpaal.

Ishpah@1Ch.8.16=H3472.short: Ishpah was a descendant of Benjamin through Beriah.

Ishpan@1Ch.8.22=H3473.short: Ishpan was a descendant of Benjamin through Shashak.

Ishvah@Gen.46.17-1Ch=H3438.brief: Son of Asher, grandson of Jacob.
Ishvah@Gen.46.17-1Ch=H3438.short: Ishvah was a son of Asher and grandson of Jacob.

Ishvi@Gen.46.17-1Ch=H3440G.brief: Son of Asher, grandson of Jacob.
Ishvi@Gen.46.17-1Ch=H3440G.short: Ishvi (or Isui) was a son of Asher and grandson of Jacob.

Ismachiah@2Ch.31.13=H3253.brief: Overseer under King Hezekiah during temple restoration.
Ismachiah@2Ch.31.13=H3253.short: Ismachiah was one of the overseers appointed by King Hezekiah during the restoration of the temple and its services.

Israel@Gen.25.26-Rev=H3478.brief: Patriarch, son of Isaac, father of twelve tribes
Israel@Gen.25.26-Rev=H3478.short: Israel, also named Jacob, was the son of Isaac, the father of the twelve tribes of Israel, and a key patriarch of the Jewish people.

Issachar@1Ch.26.5=H3485H.brief: Son of Obed-Edom, a gatekeeper in David's time.
Issachar@1Ch.26.5=H3485H.short: Issachar was a son of Obed-Edom, a gatekeeper in the time of King David.

Issachar@Gen.30.18-Rev=H3485G.brief: Son of Jacob and Leah, forefather of tribe
Issachar@Gen.30.18-Rev=H3485G.short: Issachar was the ninth son of Jacob and fifth by Leah, and he became the forefather of the Israelite tribe of Issachar.

Isshiah@1Ch.12.6=H3449H.brief: Korahite warrior who joined David at Ziklag.
Isshiah@1Ch.12.6=H3449H.short: Isshiah the Korahite was one of the warriors who joined David at Ziklag.

Isshiah@1Ch.23.20-=H3449I.brief: Levite, grandson of Rehabiah during David's reign.
Isshiah@1Ch.23.20-=H3449I.short: Isshiah was a Levite, the son of Rehabiah and grandson of Moses, who served during King David's reign.

Isshiah@1Ch.24.21-=H3449J.brief: Levite, descendant of Rehabiah during David's reign.
Isshiah@1Ch.24.21-=H3449J.short: Isshiah (or Jeshaiah) was a Levite, a descendant of Rehabiah, who served during King David's reign.

Isshiah@1Ch.7.3=H3449G.brief: Son of Izrahiah, descendant of Issachar.
Isshiah@1Ch.7.3=H3449G.short: Isshiah was a son of Izrahiah and a descendant of Issachar.

Isshijah@Ezr.10.31=H3449K.brief: Descendant of Harim; agreed to put away foreign wife.
Isshijah@Ezr.10.31=H3449K.short: Isshijah, a descendant of Harim, was among those who agreed to put away their foreign wives during Ezra's reforms.

Ithamar@Exo.6.23-Ezr=H0385.brief: Youngest son of Aaron; served as priest.
Ithamar@Exo.6.23-Ezr=H0385.short: Ithamar was the fourth and youngest son of Aaron, who served as a priest alongside his brothers Nadab, Abihu, and Eleazar.

Ithiel@Neh.11.7=H0384G.brief: Descendant of Benjamin living in Jerusalem.
Ithiel@Neh.11.7=H0384G.short: Ithiel, a descendant of Benjamin, was among those who settled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.

Ithiel@Pro.30.1=H0384H.brief: Mentioned in Agur's sayings; meaning uncertain.
Ithiel@Pro.30.1=H0384H.short: Ithiel is mentioned twice in Proverbs 30:1, but the meaning and context of the name are uncertain.

Ithmah@1Ch.11.46=H3495.short: Ithmah the Moabite was one of the mighty warriors in David's army.

Ithran@1Ch.7.37-=H3506H.brief: Descendant of Asher, son of Zophah.
Ithran@1Ch.7.37-=H3506H.short: Ithran (or Jether) was a descendant of Asher, the son of Zophah.

Ithran@Gen.36.26-1Ch=H3506G.brief: Descendant of Esau, son of Dishon the Horite.
Ithran@Gen.36.26-1Ch=H3506G.short: Ithran was a descendant of Esau and son of Dishon the Horite.

Ithream@2Sa.3.5-1Ch=H3507.brief: Son of David, born in Hebron to Eglah.
Ithream@2Sa.3.5-1Ch=H3507.short: Ithream was a son of David, born to him in Hebron by his wife Eglah.

Ithrites@2Sa.23.38-1Ch=H3505.brief: Clan descended from Kiriath-jearim; two of David's warriors.
Ithrites@2Sa.23.38-1Ch=H3505.short: The Ithrites were a clan descended from Kiriath-jearim (1Ch.2.53), and two of David's mighty warriors, Ira and Gareb, were Ithrites.

Ittai@2Sa.15.19-=H0863G.brief: Gittite commander who remained loyal to David.
Ittai@2Sa.15.19-=H0863G.short: Ittai the Gittite was a commander who remained loyal to David during Absalom's rebellion.

Ittai@2Sa.23.29-1Ch=H0863H.short: Ittai, one of King David's mighty men, was from Gibeah of Benjamin.

Izhar@1Ch.4.7=H3328.brief: Son of Asher listed in the genealogy in Chronicles
Izhar@1Ch.4.7=H3328.short: Izhar was a descendant of Asher mentioned among the genealogies of the twelve tribes of Israel.

Izhar@Exo.6.18-1Ch=H3324.brief: Son of Kohath, grandson of Levi; father of Korah.
Izhar@Exo.6.18-1Ch=H3324.short: Izhar (or Amminadab), son of Kohath and father of Korah, was a Levite.

Izliah@1Ch.8.18=H3152.short: Izliah was a Benjamite, one of the sons of Elpaal.

Izrahiah@1Ch.7.3=H3156G.short: Izrahiah, a son of Uzzi, was a descendant of Issachar and a clan head.

Izziah@Ezr.10.25=H3150.brief: Descendant of Parosh; agreed to put away foreign wife.
Izziah@Ezr.10.25=H3150.short: Izziah, a descendant of Parosh, was among those who agreed to put away their foreign wives during Ezra's reforms.

Jaakobah@1Ch.4.36=H3291.short: Jaakobah was a leader from the tribe of Simeon during the reign of King Hezekiah.

Jaalah@Ezr.2.56-Neh=H3279.brief: Returned exile; descendant of Solomon's servants.
Jaalah@Ezr.2.56-Neh=H3279.short: Jaalah was among the descendants of Solomon's servants who returned to Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.

Jaare-oregim@2Sa.21.19-1Ch=H3296.brief: Father of Elhanan, who killed Goliath's brother.
Jaare-oregim@2Sa.21.19-1Ch=H3296.short: Jaare-oregim (or Jair) was the father of Elhanan, who killed Lahmi, the brother of Goliath the Gittite.

Jaareshiah@1Ch.8.27=H3298.short: Jaareshiah was a descendant of Benjamin through Jeroham.

Jaasiel@1Ch.11.47=H3300G.brief: One of David's mighty warriors, the son of Abner.
Jaasiel@1Ch.11.47=H3300G.short: Jaasiel, the son of Abner, was one of David's mighty warriors.

Jaasiel@1Ch.27.21=H3300H.brief: Leader of the half-tribe of Manasseh during David's reign.
Jaasiel@1Ch.27.21=H3300H.short: Jaasiel, the son of Abner, was the leader of the half-tribe of Manasseh during King David's reign.

Jaasu@Ezr.10.37=H3299.brief: Descendant of Bani; agreed to put away foreign wife.
Jaasu@Ezr.10.37=H3299.short: Jaasu, a descendant of Bani, was among those who agreed to put away their foreign wives during Ezra's reforms.

Jaazaniah@Ezk.11.1=H2970I.brief: Leader among the twenty-five men in Ezekiel's vision.
Jaazaniah@Ezk.11.1=H2970I.short: Jaazaniah, the son of Azzur, was one of the twenty-five men in Ezekiel's vision who were devising iniquity and giving wicked counsel.

Jaazaniah@Ezk.8.11=H2970H.brief: Israelite elder; participated in idolatry in the temple.
Jaazaniah@Ezk.8.11=H2970H.short: Jaazaniah, the son of Shaphan, was one of the seventy elders of Israel who participated in idolatrous practices in the temple, as seen in Ezekiel's vision.

Jaazaniah@Jer.35.3=H2970G.brief: Son of Jeremiah; a Rechabite during Jeremiah's time.
Jaazaniah@Jer.35.3=H2970G.short: Jaazaniah, the son of Jeremiah, was a Rechabite who was tested by the prophet Jeremiah for his obedience to his ancestor's commands.

Jaaziah@1Ch.24.26-=H3269.brief: Levite, descendant of Merari during David's reign.
Jaaziah@1Ch.24.26-=H3269.short: Jaaziah was a Levite, a descendant of Merari through his son Beno, who served during King David's reign.

Jaaziel@1Ch.15.18-=H3268.short: Jaaziel (or Aziel or Jeiel) was a Levite appointed as a musician to play the bronze cymbals during the bringing of the ark to Jerusalem in David's reign.

Jabal@Gen.4.20=H2989.brief: Son of Lamech; father of nomadic herdsmen.
Jabal@Gen.4.20=H2989.short: Jabal, the son of Lamech and Adah, was the ancestor of those who dwell in tents and have livestock.

Jabesh@2Ki.15.10-=H3003H.brief: Assassinated Zechariah; reigned as king of Israel for a month.
Jabesh@2Ki.15.10-=H3003H.short: Jabesh, the son of Shallum, conspired against and assassinated Zechariah, becoming king of Israel, but reigned for only one month before being killed by Menahem.

Jabez@1Ch.4.9-=H3258H.brief: More honorable than his brothers; God granted his prayer.
Jabez@1Ch.4.9-=H3258H.short: Jabez, who was more honorable than his brothers, cried out to God, who granted his request to enlarge his territory and keep him from harm.

Jabin@Jdg.4.2-Psa=H2985H.brief: Canaanite king who oppressed Israel; defeated by Deborah and Barak.
Jabin@Jdg.4.2-Psa=H2985H.short: Jabin, a Canaanite king of Hazor, oppressed Israel for twenty years until he was defeated by Deborah and Barak.

Jabin@Jos.11.1=H2985G.brief: King of Hazor; led Canaanite coalition against Joshua.
Jabin@Jos.11.1=H2985G.short: Jabin, king of Hazor, formed an alliance with other Canaanite kings to fight against Joshua and the Israelites.

Jacan@1Ch.5.13=H3275.brief: Gadite leader during the reign of Jotham.
Jacan@1Ch.5.13=H3275.short: Jacan was a leader from the tribe of Gad during the reign of Jotham, king of Judah.

Jachin@1Ch.24.17=H3199J.brief: Head of a priestly division during David's reign.
Jachin@1Ch.24.17=H3199J.short: Jachin was the head of the twenty-first priestly division organized by King David.

Jachin@1Ch.9.10-Neh=H3199I.brief: Priest who lived in Jerusalem after the exile.
Jachin@1Ch.9.10-Neh=H3199I.short: Jachin was a priest who resided in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.

Jachin@Gen.46.10-1Ch=H3199G.brief: Son of Simeon; founder of the Jachinites clan.
Jachin@Gen.46.10-1Ch=H3199G.short: Jachin (or Jarib), a son of Simeon, was the founder of the Jachinites clan within the tribe of Simeon.

Jacob@Mat.1.15-=G2384G.brief: Father of Joseph, the husband of Mary.
Jacob@Mat.1.15-=G2384G.short: Jacob was the father of Joseph, the husband of Mary, the mother of Jesus.

Jada@1Ch.2.28-=H3047.brief: Son of Onam and brother of Shammai.
Jada@1Ch.2.28-=H3047.short: Jada was the son of Onam and the brother of Shammai, from the tribe of Judah.

Jaddai@Ezr.10.43=H3035H.brief: Israelite who agreed to put away his foreign wife.
Jaddai@Ezr.10.43=H3035H.short: Jaddai was among the Israelites who agreed to put away their foreign wives during Ezra's reforms.

Jaddua@Neh.10.21=H3037G.brief: One of the leaders who sealed Nehemiah's covenant.
Jaddua@Neh.10.21=H3037G.short: Jaddua was one of the leaders who sealed the covenant made by the people of Israel during Nehemiah's time.

Jaddua@Neh.12.11-=H3037H.brief: High priest during the time of Alexander the Great.
Jaddua@Neh.12.11-=H3037H.short: Jaddua served as the high priest during the reign of Darius the Persian and was contemporary with Alexander the Great.

Jadon@Neh.3.7=H3036.brief: Meronothite who helped repair Jerusalem's walls under Nehemiah.
Jadon@Neh.3.7=H3036.short: Jadon the Meronothite was one of the people who helped repair the walls of Jerusalem during Nehemiah's time.

Jael@Jdg.4.17-=H3278.brief: Wife of Heber; killed Sisera, the Canaanite commander.
Jael@Jdg.4.17-=H3278.short: Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite, killed Sisera, the commander of the Canaanite army, by driving a tent peg through his temple.

Jahath@1Ch.23.10-=H3189H.brief: Levite, descendant of Shimei, son of Gershon.
Jahath@1Ch.23.10-=H3189H.short: Jahath was a Levite, a descendant of Shimei, and a grandson of Gershon.

Jahath@1Ch.24.22=H3189J.brief: Levite, son of Shelomoth, descendant of Izhar.
Jahath@1Ch.24.22=H3189J.short: Jahath was a Levite, the son of Shelomoth, and a descendant of Izhar.

Jahath@1Ch.4.2=H3189G.brief: Son of Reaiah, descendant of Judah through Shobal.
Jahath@1Ch.4.2=H3189G.short: Jahath was the son of Reaiah and a descendant of Judah through Shobal.

Michael@1Ch.5.14=H4317I.brief: A Gadite chief, descendant of Abihail.
Michael@1Ch.5.14=H4317I.short: Michael, a descendant of Abihail, was one of the Gadite chiefs mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Gad.

Michael@1Ch.6.40=H4317J.brief: A Levite musician, son of Baaseiah.
Michael@1Ch.6.40=H4317J.short: Michael, a Levite and descendant of Merari, was the son of Baaseiah and is mentioned in the genealogy of the Levitical musicians.

Michael@1Ch.7.3=H4317K.brief: Son of Uzzi, a descendant of Issachar.
Michael@1Ch.7.3=H4317K.short: Michael, a descendant of Issachar, was one of the sons of Uzzi.

Michael@1Ch.8.16=H4317L.short: Michael, a Benjamite, was one of the sons of Beriah mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin.

Michael@2Ch.21.2=H4317O.brief: A son of King Jehoshaphat of Judah.
Michael@2Ch.21.2=H4317O.short: Michael was one of the sons of King Jehoshaphat of Judah.

Michael@Dan.10.13-Rev=H4317Q.brief: An archangel who fights for God's people.
Michael@Dan.10.13-Rev=H4317Q.short: Michael, the archangel, is mentioned in the Bible as a heavenly being who fights for God's people and contends with evil forces.

Michael@Ezr.8.8=H4317P.brief: A descendant of Shephatiah who returned with Ezra.
Michael@Ezr.8.8=H4317P.short: Michael, a descendant of Shephatiah, was among those who returned to Jerusalem with Ezra.

Michael@Num.13.13=H4317G.brief: A spy from the tribe of Asher.
Michael@Num.13.13=H4317G.short: Michael, from the tribe of Asher, was one of the twelve spies sent by Moses to scout out the land of Canaan.

Michal@1Sa.14.49-1Ch=H4324G.brief: Daughter of Saul; wife of David.
Michal@1Sa.14.49-1Ch=H4324G.short: Michal, the younger daughter of King Saul, became David's wife and helped him escape from Saul's attempts to kill him.

Michri@1Ch.9.8=H4381.brief: A Benjamite who lived in Jerusalem.
Michri@1Ch.9.8=H4381.short: Michri, a Benjamite, is mentioned in the list of the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

Midian@Gen.25.2-1Ch=H4080G.brief: Son of Abraham and Keturah; father of the Midianites.
Midian@Gen.25.2-1Ch=H4080G.short: Midian, a son of Abraham and Keturah, was the ancestor of the Midianite people.

Mijamin@1Ch.24.9=H4326G.brief: A priest in the time of David.
Mijamin@1Ch.24.9=H4326G.short: Mijamin, a priest, was the head of the sixth division of the priestly order during the reign of David.

Mijamin@Ezr.10.25=H4326H.brief: An Israelite who married a foreign woman.
Mijamin@Ezr.10.25=H4326H.short: Mijamin, an Israelite, was among those who had married foreign women during the time of Ezra.

Mijamin@Neh.10.7-=H4326I.brief: A priest who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah.
Mijamin@Neh.10.7-=H4326I.short: Mijamin (or Miniamin), a priest, was among those who sealed the covenant during the time of Nehemiah and served as a leader of the priestly division.

Mikloth@1Ch.27.4=H4732H.brief: A military commander during David's reign.
Mikloth@1Ch.27.4=H4732H.short: Mikloth was the leader of the second division of David's army, serving during the second month of each year.

Mikloth@1Ch.8.32-=H4732G.short: Mikloth, a Benjamite, was the son of Eshek and lived in Jerusalem.

Mikneiah@1Ch.15.18-=H4737.brief: A Levite musician during David's reign.
Mikneiah@1Ch.15.18-=H4737.short: Mikneiah, a Levite, was one of the musicians appointed by David to play the harp during the procession of the ark to Jerusalem.

Milalai@Neh.12.36=H4450.brief: A priest who participated in the dedication of Jerusalem's wall.
Milalai@Neh.12.36=H4450.short: Milalai, a priest, was among the musicians who participated in the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem during the time of Nehemiah.

Milcah@Gen.11.29-=H4435G.short: Milcah, the daughter of Haran and wife of Nahor, was the mother of Bethuel and the grandmother of Rebekah.

Milcah@Num.26.33-Jos=H4435H.brief: Daughter of Zelophehad, a descendant of Manasseh.
Milcah@Num.26.33-Jos=H4435H.short: Milcah, one of the five daughters of Zelophehad, was part of a significant case regarding inheritance rights for women in Israel.

Miniamin@2Ch.31.15=H4509G.short: Miniamin, a Levite, assisted in distributing the offerings and tithes to his fellow Levites during the reign of King Hezekiah.

Miniamin@Neh.12.41=H4509H.brief: A priest who played a trumpet in Nehemiah's time.
Miniamin@Neh.12.41=H4509H.short: Miniamin, a priest, was among those who played trumpets at the dedication of Jerusalem's wall during Nehemiah's time.

Miriam@1Ch.4.17=H4813H.brief: A descendant of Judah, mentioned in a genealogy.
Miriam@1Ch.4.17=H4813H.short: Miriam, a descendant of Judah, is mentioned in the genealogy of Ezrah.

Miriam@Exo.15.20-Mic=H4813G.brief: Moses' sister, a prophetess who led women in worship.
Miriam@Exo.15.20-Mic=H4813G.short: Miriam, the sister of Moses and Aaron, was a prophetess who played a significant role in the Exodus and the Israelites' journey through the wilderness.

Mirmah@1Ch.8.10=H4821.brief: A Benjamite mentioned in a genealogy.
Mirmah@1Ch.8.10=H4821.short: Mirmah, a Benjamite, is listed in the genealogy of Shaharaim.

Mishael@Dan.1.6-=H4332I.brief: A Jewish exile in Babylon, friend of Daniel.
Mishael@Dan.1.6-=H4332I.short: Mishael, also known as Meshach, was one of the four young Jewish men chosen to serve in Nebuchadnezzar's court and was a companion of Daniel during the Babylonian exile.

Mishael@Exo.6.22-Lev=H4332G.brief: A Levite who helped remove the bodies of Nadab and Abihu.
Mishael@Exo.6.22-Lev=H4332G.short: Mishael, a Levite and cousin of Aaron, assisted in removing the bodies of Nadab and Abihu after they offered unauthorized fire before the Lord.

Mishael@Neh.8.4=H4332H.brief: A Levite who stood beside Ezra during the reading of the Law.
Mishael@Neh.8.4=H4332H.short: Mishael, a Levite, was one of those who stood beside Ezra as he read the Book of the Law to the people.

Misham@1Ch.8.12=H4936.short: Misham, a Benjamite, was one of the sons of Elpaal mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin.

Mishma@1Ch.4.25-=H4927H.short: Mishma, a descendant of Simeon, was the son of Mibsam and the father of Hammuel.

Mishma@Gen.25.14-1Ch=H4927G.brief: A son of Ishmael, Abraham's son.
Mishma@Gen.25.14-1Ch=H4927G.short: Mishma was one of the twelve sons of Ishmael, Abraham's son by Hagar, and is listed among the chiefs of the Ishmaelite tribes.

Mishmannah@1Ch.12.10=H4925.brief: A Gadite warrior who joined David at Ziklag.
Mishmannah@1Ch.12.10=H4925.short: Mishmannah, a Gadite, was one of the warriors who joined David at Ziklag when he was fleeing from Saul.

Mishraites@1Ch.2.53=H4954.brief: A clan descended from Shobal, of the tribe of Judah.
Mishraites@1Ch.2.53=H4954.short: The Mishraites were a clan descended from Shobal, who was a descendant of Judah through Caleb.

Mispar@Ezr.2.2-Neh=H4558.brief: One of the returnees from Babylonian exile.
Mispar@Ezr.2.2-Neh=H4558.short: Mispar, also known as Mispereth, was among the first group of exiles who returned to Jerusalem from Babylon under the leadership of Zerubbabel.

Mithnites@1Ch.11.43=H4981.brief: The people of an unknown place or family.
Mithnites@1Ch.11.43=H4981.short: The Mithnites are mentioned in the context of Joshaphat the Mithnite, one of David's mighty warriors, but no further information about them is provided.

Mithredath@Ezr.1.8=H4990G.brief: The treasurer of King Cyrus of Persia.
Mithredath@Ezr.1.8=H4990G.short: Mithredath, the treasurer of King Cyrus of Persia, was responsible for overseeing the return of the temple articles to Sheshbazzar, the prince of Judah.

Mithredath@Ezr.4.7=H4990H.brief: A Persian official who opposed the rebuilding of Jerusalem.
Mithredath@Ezr.4.7=H4990H.short: Mithredath was one of the Persian officials who wrote a letter to King Artaxerxes, accusing the Jews of rebuilding Jerusalem's walls.

Mizzah@Gen.36.13-1Ch=H4199.brief: A grandson of Esau and a chief of Edom.
Mizzah@Gen.36.13-1Ch=H4199.short: Mizzah was a grandson of Esau and one of the chiefs of Edom listed in the genealogies of Genesis and 1 Chronicles.

Mnason@Act.21.16=G3416.brief: A Cypriot disciple who hosted Paul in Jerusalem.
Mnason@Act.21.16=G3416.short: Mnason, an early disciple from Cyprus, provided lodging for Paul and his companions when they arrived in Jerusalem.

Moab@Gen.19.37a=H4124H.brief: Son of Lot, born from an incestuous relationship.
Moab@Gen.19.37a=H4124H.short: Moab, the son of Lot by his eldest daughter, was the ancestor of the Moabite people.

Molid@1Ch.2.29=H4140.brief: Son of Abisur, of the tribe of Judah.
Molid@1Ch.2.29=H4140.short: Molid was the son of Abisur and Abihail, mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.

Mordecai@Est.2.5-=H4782H.brief: Esther's cousin, a Jewish leader in the Persian court.
Mordecai@Est.2.5-=H4782H.short: Mordecai, Esther's cousin and guardian, played a crucial role in saving the Jews from Haman's plot during the reign of King Ahasuerus (Xerxes) of Persia.

Mordecai@Ezr.2.2-Neh=H4782G.brief: A leader who returned from Babylonian exile.
Mordecai@Ezr.2.2-Neh=H4782G.short: Mordecai was one of the leaders who returned with Zerubbabel from Babylonian captivity to Jerusalem.

Moses@Exo.2.10-Rev=H4872.brief: Prophet who led Israel out of Egypt
Moses@Exo.2.10-Rev=H4872.short: Moses was a prophet whom God used to lead Israel out of slavery in Egypt and give them the law.

Moza@1Ch.2.46=H4162G.brief: Son of Caleb by his concubine Ephah
Moza@1Ch.2.46=H4162G.short: Moza was a son of Caleb, the renowned spy, by his concubine Ephah.

Moza@1Ch.8.36-=H4162H.brief: Son of Zimri, descendant of King Saul
Moza@1Ch.8.36-=H4162H.short: Moza, a Benjamite, was a descendant of King Saul.

Muppim@Gen.46.21-1Ch=H4649.short: Muppim, also known as Shephupham, Shephuphan, or Shuphamite, was a son of Benjamin mentioned in the genealogies of Genesis, Numbers, and 1 Chronicles.

Mushi@Exo.6.19-1Ch=H4187.brief: A Levite, son of Merari, and head of a clan.
Mushi@Exo.6.19-1Ch=H4187.short: Mushi was a son of Merari and a grandson of Levi, who became the head of the Mushite clan within the Levitical tribe.

Naam@1Ch.4.15=H5277.brief: Son of Caleb, from the tribe of Judah.
Naam@1Ch.4.15=H5277.short: Naam was a son of Caleb, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah in 1 Chronicles.

Naamah@1Ki.14.21-2Ch=H5279A.brief: An Ammonite; mother of King Rehoboam of Judah.
Naamah@1Ki.14.21-2Ch=H5279A.short: Naamah, an Ammonite woman, was the mother of Rehoboam, who succeeded his father Solomon as king of Judah.

Naamah@Gen.4.22=H5279G.brief: Daughter of Lamech and Zillah, sister of Tubal-cain.
Naamah@Gen.4.22=H5279G.short: Naamah was the daughter of Lamech and Zillah, and the sister of Tubal-cain, mentioned in the genealogy of Cain.

Naaman@1Ch.8.7=H5283J.brief: A descendant of Benjamin, son of Ehud.
Naaman@1Ch.8.7=H5283J.short: Naaman, a descendant of Benjamin, was one of the sons of Ehud mentioned in the genealogy of 1 Chronicles.

Naaman@2Ki.5.1-Luk=H5283I.brief: Aramean commander healed of leprosy by Elisha.
Naaman@2Ki.5.1-Luk=H5283I.short: Naaman, a commander of the Aramean army, was healed of his leprosy by the prophet Elisha, demonstrating God's power and compassion.

Naaman@Gen.46.21-1Ch=H5283G.short: Naaman, also known as Nohah, was one of the sons of Benjamin mentioned in the genealogies of Genesis and 1 Chronicles.

Naaman@Num.26.40-1Ch=H5283H.brief: Grandson of Benjamin, head of the Naamite clan.
Naaman@Num.26.40-1Ch=H5283H.short: Naaman, a grandson of Benjamin through Bela, was the head of the Naamite clan within the tribe of Benjamin.

Naamathites@Job.2.11-=H5284.brief: The people group of Zophar, Job's friend.
Naamathites@Job.2.11-=H5284.short: The Naamathites were the people group to which Zophar, one of Job's three friends, belonged.

Naarah@1Ch.4.5-=H5292B.brief: Wife of Ashhur, the founder of Tekoa.
Naarah@1Ch.4.5-=H5292B.short: Naarah was one of the two wives of Ashhur, the father (ie founder) of Tekoa, mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.

Naarai@1Ch.11.37=H5293.brief: One of David's mighty warriors, son of Ezbai.
Naarai@1Ch.11.37=H5293.short: Naarai, the son of Ezbai, was one of the mighty warriors who fought alongside King David.

Nabal@1Sa.25.3-2Sa=H5037.brief: Wealthy Carmelite; husband of Abigail. He was known for foolishness.
Nabal@1Sa.25.3-2Sa=H5037.short: Nabal, a wealthy man from Carmel, was known for his foolishness and mistreatment of David, which nearly led to his demise.

Naboth@1Ki.21.1-2Ki=H5022.brief: Jezreelite vineyard owner, unjustly killed by Ahab and Jezebel.
Naboth@1Ki.21.1-2Ki=H5022.short: Naboth, a Jezreelite, was unjustly killed by King Ahab and Queen Jezebel for refusing to sell his ancestral vineyard.

Nacon@2Sa.6.6-1Ch=H5225.brief: Threshing floor where Uzzah touched the ark.
Nacon@2Sa.6.6-1Ch=H5225.short: Nacon, also known as Chidon, was the owner of the threshing floor where Uzzah touched the ark of God and was struck down.

Nadab@1Ch.2.28-=H5070I.brief: Son of Shammai, from the tribe of Judah.
Nadab@1Ch.2.28-=H5070I.short: Nadab was a son of Shammai, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah.

Nadab@1Ch.8.30-=H5070J.brief: Son of Abiel, from the tribe of Benjamin.
Nadab@1Ch.8.30-=H5070J.short: Nadab was a son of Abiel, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin.

Nadab@1Ki.14.20-=H5070H.brief: King of Israel, son of Jeroboam I, reigned briefly.
Nadab@1Ki.14.20-=H5070H.short: Nadab, the son of Jeroboam I, reigned as king of Israel for two years before being assassinated by Baasha.

Nadab@Exo.6.23-1Ch=H5070G.brief: Son of Aaron, consumed by fire for offering incense.
Nadab@Exo.6.23-1Ch=H5070G.short: Nadab, the eldest son of Aaron, was consumed by fire from the Lord for offering unauthorized incense.

Naggai@Luk.3.25=G3477.short: Naggai is mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus Christ as recorded in the Gospel of Luke.

Naham@1Ch.4.19=H5163.brief: Brother of Hodiah who married Ishbar.
Naham@1Ch.4.19=H5163.short: Naham, the brother of Hodiah whose son founded Keilah the Garmite city.

Nahamani@Neh.7.7=H5167.brief: One who returned from Babylonian exile with Zerubbabel.
Nahamani@Neh.7.7=H5167.short: Nahamani was among those who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian captivity with Zerubbabel.

Naharai@2Sa.23.37-1Ch=H5171.brief: One of David's mighty men, Joab's armor-bearer.
Naharai@2Sa.23.37-1Ch=H5171.short: Naharai the Beerothite, Joab's armor-bearer, was one of David's mighty men.

Nahash@1Sa.11.1-=H5176G.brief: Ammonite king who besieged Jabesh Gilead.
Nahash@1Sa.11.1-=H5176G.short: Nahash, the king of the Ammonites, besieged Jabesh Gilead and threatened to gouge out the right eyes of its inhabitants.

Nahash@2Sa.10.2-1Ch=H5176H.brief: Ammonite king, father of Hanun, showed kindness to David.
Nahash@2Sa.10.2-1Ch=H5176H.short: Nahash, the king of the Ammonites and father of Hanun, had shown kindness to David, prompting David to send envoys to console Hanun after Nahash's death.

Nahash@2Sa.17.25=H5176I.brief: Mother of Abigail and Zeruiah, David's sisters.
Nahash@2Sa.17.25=H5176I.short: Nahash, the mother of David and his sisters Abigail and Zeruiah, is mentioned in the context of Amasa's lineage.

Nahash@2Sa.17.27=H5176J.brief: King of the Ammonites, provided supplies to David.
Nahash@2Sa.17.27=H5176J.short: Nahash, the king of the Ammonites, provided supplies to David and his men during their time in Mahanaim.

Nahath@2Ch.31.13=H5184H.brief: A Levite during the reign of King Hezekiah.
Nahath@2Ch.31.13=H5184H.short: Nahath was one of the Levites appointed by King Hezekiah to oversee the distribution of offerings and tithes.

Nahath@Gen.36.13-1Ch=H5184G.brief: A descendant of Esau, a chief of Edom.
Nahath@Gen.36.13-1Ch=H5184G.short: Nahath, a descendant of Esau, was one of the chiefs of Edom.

Nahbi@Num.13.14=H5147.brief: The spy from the tribe of Naphtali.
Nahbi@Num.13.14=H5147.short: Nahbi, the son of Vophsi, was the representative from the tribe of Naphtali among the twelve spies sent to explore Canaan.

Nahor@Gen.11.22-Luk=H5152G.brief: Son of Serug; father of Terah, Abraham's father.
Nahor@Gen.11.22-Luk=H5152G.short: Nahor, the son of Serug and father of Terah, was Abraham's grandfather.

Nahor@Gen.11.26-=H5152H.brief: Son of Terah, Abraham's brother; father of Bethuel.
Nahor@Gen.11.26-=H5152H.short: Nahor, the son of Terah and brother of Abraham, was the father of Bethuel and the grandfather of Rebekah.

Nahshon@Exo.6.23-Luk=H5177.brief: Son of Amminadab, leader of Judah, ancestor of David.
Nahshon@Exo.6.23-Luk=H5177.short: Nahshon, the son of Amminadab, was a leader of the tribe of Judah during the Exodus and an ancestor of King David and Jesus Christ.

Nahum@Luk.3.25=G3486.short: Nahum is mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus Christ as recorded in the Gospel of Luke.

Nahum@Nam.1.1=H5151.brief: Old Testament prophet, author of the Book of Nahum.
Nahum@Nam.1.1=H5151.short: Nahum, identified as the Elkoshite, was a prophet of God who delivered a message of judgment against the Assyrian city of Nineveh.

Naomi@Rut.1.2-=H5281.short: Naomi, also known as Mara, was an Israelite woman who, after losing her husband and sons, returned from Moab to Bethlehem with her daughter-in-law Ruth.

Naphish@Gen.25.15-1Ch=H5305.brief: Son of Ishmael, defeated by Reubenites, Gadites, and Manassites.
Naphish@Gen.25.15-1Ch=H5305.short: Naphish, a son of Ishmael, was among the Hagrite tribes defeated by the Reubenites, Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.

Naphtali@Gen.30.8-Rev=H5321G.brief: Son of Jacob, founder of the tribe of Naphtali.
Naphtali@Gen.30.8-Rev=H5321G.short: Naphtali, the sixth son of Jacob and second son of Bilhah, was the founder of the Israelite tribe that bore his name.

Naphtuhim@Gen.10.13-1Ch=H5320.brief: Descendants of Mizraim, son of Ham
Naphtuhim@Gen.10.13-1Ch=H5320.short: The Naphtuhim were descendants of Mizraim, son of Ham, who settled in northern Egypt.

Narcissus@Rom.16.11=G3488.brief: Christian in Rome with a household
Narcissus@Rom.16.11=G3488.short: Narcissus was likely a wealthy Christian in Rome with a household of believers.

Nathan@1Ch.2.36=H5416J.brief: Son of Attai, from the tribe of Judah.
Nathan@1Ch.2.36=H5416J.short: Nathan, the son of Attai, is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah.

Nathan@2Sa.23.36-1Ch=H5416I.brief: One of David's mighty men, brother of Joel.
Nathan@2Sa.23.36-1Ch=H5416I.short: Nathan, the brother of Joel, was one of David's mighty men.

Nathan@2Sa.5.14-Luk=H5416G.brief: Son of David and Bathsheba, ancestor of Jesus.
Nathan@2Sa.5.14-Luk=H5416G.short: Nathan, a son of David and Bathsheba, is mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus Christ.

Nathan@2Sa.7.2-Psa=H5416H.brief: Prophet during the reigns of David and Solomon.
Nathan@2Sa.7.2-Psa=H5416H.short: Nathan, a prophet of God, served during the reigns of David and Solomon, offering guidance, confronting David's sin, and supporting Solomon's accession to the throne.

Nathan@Ezr.10.39=H5416L.brief: An Israelite who married a foreign woman during the Exile.
Nathan@Ezr.10.39=H5416L.short: Nathan is listed among the Israelites who had married foreign women during the Exile and pledged to put them away.

Nathan@Ezr.8.16=H5416K.brief: A leader summoned by Ezra to help teach the Law.
Nathan@Ezr.8.16=H5416K.short: Nathan, along with other leaders, was summoned by Ezra to assist in teaching the Law to the people.

Nathanael@Jhn.1.45-=G3482.brief: Disciple of Jesus, from Cana in Galilee.
Nathanael@Jhn.1.45-=G3482.short: Nathanael, also known as Bartholomew, was one of Jesus' twelve disciples, who was initially skeptical but later confessed Jesus as the Son of God.

Nathan-melech@2Ki.23.11=H5419.brief: A court official during King Josiah's reign.
Nathan-melech@2Ki.23.11=H5419.short: Nathan-melech was a court official who had living quarters near the entrance of the temple during King Josiah's reign.

Neariah@1Ch.3.22-=H5294G.brief: Descendant of David, son of Shemaiah.
Neariah@1Ch.3.22-=H5294G.short: Neariah, a descendant of King David, was the son of Shemaiah and had three sons: Elioenai, Hizkiah, and Azrikam.

Neariah@1Ch.4.42=H5294H.brief: A Simeonite leader who defeated the Amalekites.
Neariah@1Ch.4.42=H5294H.short: Neariah, along with other Simeonite leaders, defeated the remaining Amalekites during the reign of King Hezekiah.

Nebai@Neh.10.19=H5109.brief: A leader who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah.
Nebai@Neh.10.19=H5109.short: Nebai was one of the leaders who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah to follow God's law.

Nebaioth@Gen.25.13-Isa=H5032.brief: Firstborn son of Ishmael; father of a tribe.
Nebaioth@Gen.25.13-Isa=H5032.short: Nebaioth, the firstborn son of Ishmael, was the ancestor of a tribe known for their flocks and mentioned in Isaiah's prophecy of future blessing.

Nebat@1Ki.11.26-2Ch=H5028.brief: Father of Jeroboam, the first king of Israel.
Nebat@1Ki.11.26-2Ch=H5028.short: Nebat was the father of Jeroboam I, who became the first king of the northern kingdom of Israel after the division of the monarchy.

Nebuchadnezzar@2Ki.24.1-Dan=H5019.brief: Emperor of Babylon who conquered Judah
Nebuchadnezzar@2Ki.24.1-Dan=H5019.short: Nebuchadnezzar II was the powerful Emperor of Babylon who destroyed Jerusalem and exiled the Jews.

Nebu-sar-sekim@Jer.39.3=H8310.short: Nebu-sar-sekim was a high official in Nebuchadnezzar's army when Jerusalem fell.

Nebushazban@Jer.39.13=H5021.brief: Babylonian official during the fall of Jerusalem.
Nebushazban@Jer.39.13=H5021.short: Nebushazban, a Babylonian official, was among those who took charge of Jeremiah after the fall of Jerusalem.

Nebuzaradan@2Ki.25.8-Jer=H5018.brief: Babylonian captain of the guard during Jerusalem's fall.
Nebuzaradan@2Ki.25.8-Jer=H5018.short: Nebuzaradan, the captain of the Babylonian guard, oversaw the destruction of Jerusalem, the exile of its inhabitants, and the release of Jeremiah.

Neco@2Ki.23.29-Jer=H5224G.brief: Egyptian Pharaoh during the reigns of Josiah and Jehoiakim.
Neco@2Ki.23.29-Jer=H5224G.short: Pharaoh Neco II, the ruler of Egypt, opposed King Josiah of Judah, installed Jehoiakim as a vassal king, and was later defeated by Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon.

Nedabiah@1Ch.3.18=H5072.brief: Descendant of King Jeconiah of Judah
