Remaliah@2Ki.15.25-Isa=H7425.short: Remaliah was the father of Pekah, who became king of Israel and reigned for 20 years.

Rephael@1Ch.26.7=H7501.brief: A gatekeeper of the temple during David's reign
Rephael@1Ch.26.7=H7501.short: Rephael was one of the gatekeepers of the temple during the reign of King David.

Rephah@1Ch.7.25=H7506.brief: Son of Beriah, of the tribe of Asher
Rephah@1Ch.7.25=H7506.short: Rephah was a son of Beriah, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher.

Rephaiah@1Ch.3.21=H7509G.short: Rephaiah was a descendant of King David, mentioned in the genealogy of David's descendants.

Rephaiah@1Ch.4.42=H7509H.brief: A Simeonite leader who attacked the Amalekites
Rephaiah@1Ch.4.42=H7509H.short: Rephaiah was a Simeonite leader who led an attack against the Amalekites during the time of Hezekiah.

Rephaiah@1Ch.7.2=H7509I.brief: Son of Tola, of the tribe of Issachar
Rephaiah@1Ch.7.2=H7509I.short: Rephaiah was a son of Tola, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Issachar.

Rephaiah@Neh.3.9=H7509J.brief: Son of Hur, who helped repair Jerusalem's wall
Rephaiah@Neh.3.9=H7509J.short: Rephaiah was the son of Hur and ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, who helped repair a section of the city wall.

Rephaim@Gen.14.5-Jos=H7497B.brief: A race of giants who inhabited Canaan
Rephaim@Gen.14.5-Jos=H7497B.short: The Rephaim, also known as Zamzummin, were a race of giants who inhabited parts of Canaan before the Israelite conquest.

Resheph@1Ch.7.25=H7566.brief: Son of Beriah, of the tribe of Asher
Resheph@1Ch.7.25=H7566.short: Resheph was a son of Beriah, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher.

Reu@Gen.11.18-Luk=H7466.brief: Son of Peleg, ancestor of Abraham
Reu@Gen.11.18-Luk=H7466.short: Reu was the son of Peleg and an ancestor of Abraham, living to the age of 239 years.

Reuben@Gen.29.32-Rev=H7205.brief: Firstborn son of Jacob and Leah
Reuben@Gen.29.32-Rev=H7205.short: Reuben was the firstborn son of Jacob and Leah, and his descendants formed one of the twelve tribes of Israel.

Reuel@1Ch.9.8=H7467H.short: Reuel was a Benjamite mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin.

Reuel@Gen.36.4-1Ch=H7467G.brief: Son of Esau and Basemath, a chief of Edom
Reuel@Gen.36.4-1Ch=H7467G.short: Reuel was a son of Esau and Basemath, and he became a chief in the land of Edom.

Reumah@Gen.22.24=H7208.short: Reumah was the concubine of Nahor, Abraham's brother, and she bore him four sons.

Rezin@2Ki.15.37-Isa=H7526G.brief: King of Aram (Syria) during the reign of Ahaz
Rezin@2Ki.15.37-Isa=H7526G.short: Rezin was the king of Aram (Syria) who allied with Pekah, king of Israel, against Ahaz, king of Judah.

Rezin@Ezr.2.48-Neh=H7526H.brief: Ancestor of a family of temple servants (Nethinim)
Rezin@Ezr.2.48-Neh=H7526H.short: Rezin was the ancestor of a family of temple servants (Nethinim) who returned from the Babylonian exile.

Rezon@1Ki.11.23=H7331.brief: Son of Eliada, adversary of Solomon
Rezon@1Ki.11.23=H7331.short: Rezon, son of Eliada, was an adversary of Solomon who reigned over Aram (Syria) in Damascus.

Rhesa@Luk.3.27=G4488.brief: Son of Zerubbabel, ancestor of Jesus
Rhesa@Luk.3.27=G4488.short: Rhesa was the son of Zerubbabel and an ancestor of Jesus Christ, according to Luke's genealogy.

Rhoda@Act.12.13=G4498.brief: Servant girl in the house of Mary
Rhoda@Act.12.13=G4498.short: Rhoda was a servant girl in the house of Mary, the mother of John Mark, who recognized Peter's voice at the door.

Ribai@2Sa.23.29-1Ch=H7380.brief: Father of Ittai, one of David's mighty men
Ribai@2Sa.23.29-1Ch=H7380.short: Ribai was the father of Ittai the Gibeathite, one of David's mighty men.

Rimmon@2Sa.4.2-=H7417B.brief: Father of Baanah and Rechab, murderers of Ish-bosheth
Rimmon@2Sa.4.2-=H7417B.short: Rimmon was a Beerothite and the father of Rechab and Baanah, who murdered Ish-bosheth, Saul's son.

Rinnah@1Ch.4.20=H7441.brief: Son of Shimon, of the tribe of Judah
Rinnah@1Ch.4.20=H7441.short: Rinnah was a son of Shimon, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah.

Riphath@Gen.10.3-1Ch=H7384B.brief: Son of Gomer, grandson of Japheth
Riphath@Gen.10.3-1Ch=H7384B.short: Riphath was a son of Gomer and grandson of Japheth, mentioned in the Table of Nations.

Rizia@1Ch.7.39=H7525.brief: Son of Ulla, of the tribe of Asher
Rizia@1Ch.7.39=H7525.short: Rizia was a son of Ulla, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher.

Rizpah@2Sa.3.7-=H7532.brief: Concubine of Saul; mother of Armoni and Mephibosheth
Rizpah@2Sa.3.7-=H7532.short: Rizpah was a concubine of King Saul and the mother of Armoni and Mephibosheth, who were executed by the Gibeonites.

Rohgah@1Ch.7.34=H7303.brief: Son of Shomer, of the tribe of Asher
Rohgah@1Ch.7.34=H7303.short: Rohgah was a son of Shomer (or 'Shamer'), mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher.

Romamti-ezer@1Ch.25.4-=H7320.brief: Son of Heman, a Levitical singer
Romamti-ezer@1Ch.25.4-=H7320.short: Romamti-ezer was a son of Heman and a Levitical singer during the reign of King David.

Rosh@Gen.46.21-1Ch=H7220.brief: Son of Benjamin, grandson of Jacob
Rosh@Gen.46.21-1Ch=H7220.short: Rosh (or Rapha) was a son of Benjamin and grandson of Jacob, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin.

Rufus@Mrk.15.21=G4504G.brief: Son of Simon of Cyrene, who carried Jesus' cross
Rufus@Mrk.15.21=G4504G.short: Rufus was the son of Simon of Cyrene, who was compelled to carry Jesus' cross on the way to His crucifixion.

Rufus@Rom.16.13=G4504H.brief: Believer in Rome, son of Paul's "mother"
Rufus@Rom.16.13=G4504H.short: Rufus was a believer in Rome, chosen in the Lord, whose mother had also been a mother figure to Paul.

Ruth@Rut.1.4-Mat=H7327.brief: Moabite woman, ancestor of David and Jesus
Ruth@Rut.1.4-Mat=H7327.short: Ruth was a Moabite woman who married Boaz and became an ancestor of King David and Jesus Christ.

Sabtah@Gen.10.7-1Ch=H5454.brief: Son of Cush, grandson of Ham
Sabtah@Gen.10.7-1Ch=H5454.short: Sabtah (or Sabta) was a son of Cush and a grandson of Ham, mentioned in the Table of Nations.

Sabteca@Gen.10.7-1Ch=H5455.brief: Son of Cush, grandson of Ham
Sabteca@Gen.10.7-1Ch=H5455.short: Sabteca was a son of Cush and a grandson of Ham, mentioned in the Table of Nations.

Sachar@1Ch.26.4=H7940G.brief: Son of Obed-edom, a Levitical gatekeeper
Sachar@1Ch.26.4=H7940G.short: Sachar was a son of Obed-edom and a Levitical gatekeeper during the reign of King David.

Sachia@1Ch.8.10=H7634.short: Sachia was a son of Shaharaim, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin.

Sallai@Neh.11.8=H5543A.brief: Benjamite who settled in Jerusalem after the exile
Sallai@Neh.11.8=H5543A.short: Sallai was a Benjamite who settled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile, as recorded in Nehemiah 11.

Sallu@1Ch.9.7=H5543D.short: Sallu was a Benjamite who lived in Jerusalem, as recorded in the genealogy of 1Chronicles 9.

Sallu@Neh.11.7=H5543G.brief: Benjamite who settled in Jerusalem after the exile
Sallu@Neh.11.7=H5543G.short: Sallu was a Benjamite leader who settled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile, as recorded in Nehemiah 11.

Sallu@Neh.12.7-=H5543B.brief: Priest who returned from Babylonian exile with Zerubbabel
Sallu@Neh.12.7-=H5543B.short: Sallu (or Sallai) was a priest who returned from the Babylonian exile with Zerubbabel and later signed the covenant under Nehemiah.

Salma@1Ch.2.51-=H8007H.brief: Son of Hur, founder of Bethlehem
Salma@1Ch.2.51-=H8007H.short: Salma was the son of Hur and the father (ie founder) of Bethlehem, as mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.

Salmon@Rut.4.20-Luk=H8007G.brief: Son of Nahshon; husband of Rahab; ancestor of David
Salmon@Rut.4.20-Luk=H8007G.short: Salmon (or Sala) was the son of Nahshon and husband of Rahab - an ancestor of King David and Jesus Christ.

Salome@Mat.14.6=G2266H.brief: Danced for Herod, requested John the Baptist's execution
Salome@Mat.14.6=G2266H.short: Salome, the daughter of Herodias, danced before Herod and requested the execution of John the Baptist.

Salome@Mat.20.20-Mrk=G4539.brief: Witness of Jesus' crucifixion and resurrection
Salome@Mat.20.20-Mrk=G4539.short: Salome was one of the women who witnessed Jesus' crucifixion and resurrection. She was perhaps the wife of Zebedee.

Salu@Num.25.14=H5543C.brief: Father of Zimri, a Simeonite prince
Salu@Num.25.14=H5543C.short: Salu was the father of Zimri, a Simeonite prince who was killed by Phinehas for his involvement with a Midianite woman.

Samgar@Jer.39.3=H5562.brief: Babylonian official present at the fall of Jerusalem
Samgar@Jer.39.3=H5562.short: Samgar was a Babylonian official present at the fall of Jerusalem, as recorded in the book of Jeremiah.

Samlah@Gen.36.36-1Ch=H8072.brief: King of Edom before Israel had kings
Samlah@Gen.36.36-1Ch=H8072.short: Samlah was a king of Edom who reigned before Israel had kings, as mentioned in the genealogies of Esau.

Samson@Jdg.13.24-Heb=H8123.brief: Israelite judge with great strength from God
Samson@Jdg.13.24-Heb=H8123.short: Samson was an Israelite judge known for his God-given strength, which he used to fight against the Philistines.

Samuel@1Sa.1.20-Heb=H8050G.brief: Prophet and last judge of Israel before the kings
Samuel@1Sa.1.20-Heb=H8050G.short: Samuel was a prophet and the last judge of Israel before the establishment of the monarchy, who anointed both Saul and David as kings.

Sanballat@Neh.2.10-=H5571G.brief: Governor of Samaria, opposed Nehemiah's rebuilding of Jerusalem
Sanballat@Neh.2.10-=H5571G.short: Sanballat was the governor of Samaria who opposed Nehemiah's efforts to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem.

Saph@2Sa.21.18-1Ch=H5593.brief: Philistine giant killed by Sibbechai the Hushathite
Saph@2Sa.21.18-1Ch=H5593.short: Saph (or Sippai) was a Philistine giant who was killed by Sibbechai the Hushathite during a battle with the Philistines.

Sapphira@Act.5.1=G4551.brief: Wife of Ananias, lied to the apostles, died
Sapphira@Act.5.1=G4551.short: Sapphira, along with her husband Ananias, lied to the apostles about the proceeds from a property sale and died as a result.

Sarah@Gen.11.29-1Pe=H8283.brief: Wife of Abraham; mother of Isaac
Sarah@Gen.11.29-1Pe=H8283.short: Sarah (or Sarai) was the wife of Abraham and the mother of Isaac, through whom God fulfilled His promise to make Abraham a great nation.

Saraph@1Ch.4.22=H8315.brief: Son of Shelah, descendant of Judah
Saraph@1Ch.4.22=H8315.short: Saraph was a son of Shelah and a descendant of Judah, mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.

Saul@1Sa.9.2-Act=H7586G.brief: First king of Israel, anointed by Samuel
Saul@1Sa.9.2-Act=H7586G.short: Saul was the first king of Israel, anointed by the prophet Samuel, who initially followed God but later disobeyed and was rejected as king.

Sceva@Act.19.14=G4630.brief: Jewish chief priest whose seven sons attempted to exorcise demons
Sceva@Act.19.14=G4630.short: Sceva was a Jewish chief priest whose seven sons attempted to exorcise demons in the name of Jesus, as mentioned in the book of Acts.

Scythians@Col.3.11=G4658.brief: Nomadic people group mentioned by Paul
Scythians@Col.3.11=G4658.short: The Scythians were a nomadic people group known for their barbaric reputation.

Seba@Gen.10.7-1Ch=H5434G.brief: Son of Cush, brother of Raamah
Seba@Gen.10.7-1Ch=H5434G.short: Seba was a son of Cush and brother of Raamah.

Secundus@Act.20.4=G4580.short: Secundus was a Thessalonian believer who accompanied Paul on his journey.

Segub@1Ch.2.21-=H7687H.brief: Son of Hezron; father of Jair
Segub@1Ch.2.21-=H7687H.short: Segub, son of Hezron, was the father of Jair, who had twenty-three cities in Gilead.

Segub@1Ki.16.34=H7687G.short: Segub was the son of Hiel, who rebuilt Jericho during Ahab's reign.

Seir@Gen.36.20-1Ch=H8165B.brief: Horite chief, ancestor of the Horites of Seir
Seir@Gen.36.20-1Ch=H8165B.short: Seir was a Horite chief and an ancestor of the Horites who inhabited the land of Seir.

Seled@1Ch.2.30=H5540.brief: Son of Nadab, died without children
Seled@1Ch.2.30=H5540.short: Seled, a son of Nadab, died without having any children.

Semachiah@1Ch.26.7=H5565.brief: Son of Shemaiah, gatekeeper of the temple
Semachiah@1Ch.26.7=H5565.short: Semachiah, a son of Shemaiah, served as a gatekeeper in the temple during the time of David.

Semein@Luk.3.26=G4584.short: Semein is mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus Christ, as recorded in Luke's Gospel.

Sennacherib@2Ki.18.13-Isa=H5576.short: Sennacherib and Sargon were Assyrian kings who led military campaigns against Judah during the reigns of King Hezekiah and King Ahaz, respectively.

Seorim@1Ch.24.8=H8188.brief: Priest during David's reign, head of the fourth division
Seorim@1Ch.24.8=H8188.short: Seorim was a priest who served during David's reign and was the head of the fourth priestly division.

Serah@Gen.46.17-1Ch=H8294.brief: Daughter of Asher, sister of Asher's sons
Serah@Gen.46.17-1Ch=H8294.short: Serah was the daughter of Asher and the sister of Asher's sons, as mentioned in the genealogies of the tribe of Asher.

Seraiah@1Ch.4.13-=H8304J.brief: Son of Kenaz; father of Joab
Seraiah@1Ch.4.13-=H8304J.short: Seraiah, the son of Kenaz, was the father of Joab, who was the father of the Valley of Craftsmen.

Seraiah@1Ch.4.35=H8304K.brief: Son of Asiel, descendant of Simeon
Seraiah@1Ch.4.35=H8304K.short: Seraiah, the son of Asiel, was a descendant of Simeon mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Simeon.

Seraiah@2Ki.25.18-Jer=H8304H.brief: High priest during the reign of Zedekiah
Seraiah@2Ki.25.18-Jer=H8304H.short: Seraiah served as the high priest during the reign of King Zedekiah and was executed by the Babylonians after the fall of Jerusalem.

Seraiah@2Ki.25.23-Jer=H8304I.brief: Officer under Gedaliah, son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite
Seraiah@2Ki.25.23-Jer=H8304I.short: Seraiah, the son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, was one of the officers who served under Gedaliah, the governor appointed by the Babylonians after the fall of Jerusalem.

Seraiah@2Sa.8.17-1Ch=H8304G.brief: David's scribe, also known as Shavsha, Sheva, Sheya, or Shisha
Seraiah@2Sa.8.17-1Ch=H8304G.short: Seraiah, also known as Shavsha, Sheva, Sheya, or Shisha, served as David's scribe during his reign.

Seraiah@Ezr.2.2-Neh=H8304L.brief: Priest who returned from Babylonian exile
Seraiah@Ezr.2.2-Neh=H8304L.short: Seraiah was a priest who returned from the Babylonian exile and is mentioned in the lists of returning exiles and priests.

Seraiah@Jer.36.26=H8304M.brief: Son of Azriel, sent to capture Jeremiah and Baruch
Seraiah@Jer.36.26=H8304M.short: Seraiah, the son of Azriel, was one of the men sent by King Jehoiakim to capture Jeremiah and Baruch.

Seraiah@Jer.51.59-=H8304N.brief: Neriah's son, Baruch's brother, accompanied Zedekiah to Babylon
Seraiah@Jer.51.59-=H8304N.short: Seraiah, the son of Neriah and brother of Baruch, accompanied King Zedekiah to Babylon and carried a message from Jeremiah.

Sered@Gen.46.14-Num=H5624.brief: Son of Zebulun, ancestor of the Seredites
Sered@Gen.46.14-Num=H5624.short: Sered was a son of Zebulun and the ancestor of the Seredite clan.

Sergius_Paulus@Act.13.7=G4588.brief: Proconsul of Cyprus, converted under Paul's ministry
Sergius_Paulus@Act.13.7=G4588.short: Sergius Paulus, the proconsul of Cyprus, was an intelligent man who sought to hear the word of God and believed after witnessing Paul's confrontation with Elymas the sorcerer.

Serug@Gen.11.20-Luk=H8286.brief: Son of Reu; father of Nahor, ancestor of Abraham
Serug@Gen.11.20-Luk=H8286.short: Serug was the son of Reu, the father of Nahor, and an ancestor of Abraham, living to the age of 230 years.

Seth@Gen.4.25-Luk=H8352.brief: Third son of Adam and Eve, ancestor of righteous line
Seth@Gen.4.25-Luk=H8352.short: Seth was the third son of Adam and Eve, born after the death of Abel, and became the ancestor of the righteous line of humanity.

Sethur@Num.13.13=H5639.brief: Son of Michael, spy from the tribe of Asher
Sethur@Num.13.13=H5639.short: Sethur, the son of Michael, was one of the twelve spies sent by Moses to scout out the land of Canaan, representing the tribe of Asher.

Shaaph@1Ch.2.47=H8174G.short: Shaaph, a son of Jahdai, was a descendant of Caleb.

Shaaph@1Ch.2.49=H8174H.short: Shaaph, a son of Caleb's concubine Maacah, was the father of Madmannah.

Shaashgaz@Est.2.14=H8190.brief: Eunuch in charge of King Ahasuerus' concubines
Shaashgaz@Est.2.14=H8190.short: Shaashgaz was the eunuch appointed by King Ahasuerus to be in charge of the concubines in the royal harem.

Shabbethai@Ezr.10.15=H7678G.brief: Levite who opposed Ezra's marriage reforms
Shabbethai@Ezr.10.15=H7678G.short: Shabbethai, a Levite, opposed Ezra's efforts to address the issue of intermarriage among the returned exiles.

Shabbethai@Neh.11.16=H7678I.brief: Levite in charge of external affairs in Jerusalem
Shabbethai@Neh.11.16=H7678I.short: Shabbethai, a Levite, was responsible for overseeing external affairs in Jerusalem during the time of Nehemiah.

Shabbethai@Neh.8.7=H7678H.brief: Levite who helped explain the Law to the people
Shabbethai@Neh.8.7=H7678H.short: Shabbethai, a Levite, assisted in explaining the Law to the people during the public reading led by Ezra.

Shaharaim@1Ch.8.8=H7842.brief: Benjamite who had wives Hushim and Baara
Shaharaim@1Ch.8.8=H7842.short: Shaharaim, a Benjamite, had two wives, Hushim and Baara, and he sent them away.

Shallum@1Ch.2.40-=H7967I.brief: Son of Sismai, descendant of Judah
Shallum@1Ch.2.40-=H7967I.short: Shallum, the son of Sismai, was a descendant of Judah through the line of Jerahmeel.

Shallum@1Ch.3.15=H7967J.brief: Son of Josiah, king of Judah
Shallum@1Ch.3.15=H7967J.short: Shallum was a son of Josiah, king of Judah, and the brother of Jehoiakim and Zedekiah.

Shallum@1Ch.4.25=H7967K.brief: Son of Shaul, descendant of Simeon
Shallum@1Ch.4.25=H7967K.short: Shallum was the son of Shaul and a descendant of Simeon.

Shallum@1Ch.6.12-Neh=H7967L.brief: High priest, son of Zadok and father of Hilkiah
Shallum@1Ch.6.12-Neh=H7967L.short: Shallum, also known as Meshullam, was a high priest during the time of the kings of Judah, serving as the son of Zadok and the father of Hilkiah.

Shallum@1Ch.9.17-Neh=H7967M.brief: Gatekeeper of the tabernacle during David's reign
Shallum@1Ch.9.17-Neh=H7967M.short: Shallum was a gatekeeper of the tabernacle during the reign of David, and his descendants continued to serve as gatekeepers in the temple.

Shallum@2Ch.28.12=H7967N.brief: Ephraimite leader who opposed taking captives from Judah
Shallum@2Ch.28.12=H7967N.short: Shallum, along with other leaders from Ephraim, opposed the army of Israel taking captives from Judah during the reign of King Ahaz.

Shallum@2Ki.15.10-=H7967G.brief: King of Israel who conspired against Zechariah
Shallum@2Ki.15.10-=H7967G.short: Shallum, son of Jabesh, conspired against Zechariah, king of Israel, assassinated him, and succeeded him as king, reigning for one month.

Shallum@2Ki.22.14-2Ch=H7967H.short: Shallum, the husband of Huldah the prophetess, was the keeper of the wardrobe during the reign of King Josiah.

Shallum@Ezr.10.24=H7967O.brief: Singer who married a foreign woman during Ezra's time
Shallum@Ezr.10.24=H7967O.short: Shallum was one of the singers who had married a foreign woman and agreed to put her away during Ezra's reforms.

Shallum@Ezr.10.42=H7967P.brief: Israelite who married a foreign woman during Ezra's time
Shallum@Ezr.10.42=H7967P.short: Shallum was one of the Israelites who had married a foreign woman and pledged to put her away during Ezra's reforms.

Shallum@Jer.32.7=H7967R.short: Shallum was the uncle of Jeremiah the prophet and the father of Hanamel, who sold a field to Jeremiah.

Shallum@Jer.35.4=H7967S.brief: Father of Maaseiah, keeper of the threshold
Shallum@Jer.35.4=H7967S.short: Shallum was the father of Maaseiah, who was a keeper of the threshold during the time of Jeremiah the prophet.

Shallum@Neh.3.12=H7967Q.brief: Son of Hallohesh, repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall
Shallum@Neh.3.12=H7967Q.short: Shallum, the son of Hallohesh and ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, repaired a section of the city wall along with his daughters.

Shallum@Neh.3.15=H7968.brief: Son of Col-hozeh, repaired the Fountain Gate
Shallum@Neh.3.15=H7968.short: Shallum, the son of Col-hozeh and ruler of the district of Mizpah, repaired the Fountain Gate and the wall of the Pool of Shelah during Nehemiah's rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls.

Shalmai@Ezr.2.46-Neh=H8014.brief: Nethinim ancestor whose descendants returned from Babylonian exile
Shalmai@Ezr.2.46-Neh=H8014.short: Shalmai (or Shamlai) was an ancestor of the Nethinim, and his descendants were among those who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile.

Shalmaneser@2Ki.17.3-Hos=H8022.brief: Assyrian king who conquered Samaria and exiled Israelites
Shalmaneser@2Ki.17.3-Hos=H8022.short: Shalmaneser, king of Assyria, besieged Samaria and conquered the northern kingdom of Israel, exiling its inhabitants and ending the kingdom's existence.

Shama@1Ch.11.44=H8091.brief: Mighty man in David's army, a Harodite
Shama@1Ch.11.44=H8091.short: Shama, the son of Hotham the Aroerite, was one of the mighty men in David's army.

Shamgar@Jdg.3.31-=H8044.brief: Judge of Israel who killed 600 Philistines
Shamgar@Jdg.3.31-=H8044.short: Shamgar, the son of Anath, was a judge of Israel who delivered the nation by killing 600 Philistines with an oxgoad.

Shamhuth@1Ch.27.8=H8049.brief: Fifth division commander in David's army
Shamhuth@1Ch.27.8=H8049.short: Shamhuth the Izrahite was the commander of the fifth division in David's army, serving during the fifth month.

Shamir@1Ch.24.24=H8069I.short: Shamir (or Shamur) was a Levite descended from Uzziel, the son of Kohath.

Shamma@1Ch.7.37=H8037H.brief: Son of Zophah, descendant of Asher
Shamma@1Ch.7.37=H8037H.short: Shamma was a son of Zophah and a descendant of Asher.

Shammah@2Sa.23.11=H8037G.brief: Mighty man in David's army, defended a lentil field

Stephanas@1Co.1.16-=G4734.short: Stephanas was a believer from Corinth who, along with his household, was baptized by Paul and later visited Paul to provide support and encouragement.

Stephen@Act.6.5-=G4736.brief: One of seven deacons, full of faith, performed miracles, martyred.
Stephen@Act.6.5-=G4736.short: Stephen, one of the seven deacons chosen by the early church, was full of faith and the Holy Spirit, performed miracles, and became the first Christian martyr after his powerful testimony before the Sanhedrin.

Suah@1Ch.7.36=H5477.brief: Son of Zophah, from the tribe of Asher
Suah@1Ch.7.36=H5477.short: Suah, a descendant of Asher mentioned in a genealogy.

Sukkiim@2Ch.12.3=H5525.brief: African people who invaded Judah under Shishak
Sukkiim@2Ch.12.3=H5525.short: The Sukkiim were an African people who joined Shishak's invasion of Judah.

Susanna@Luk.8.3=G4677.brief: Woman who helped support Jesus and his disciples
Susanna@Luk.8.3=G4677.short: Susanna was one of the women who provided for Jesus out of her resources.

Susi@Num.13.11=H5485.brief: Father of the Manassite spy Gaddi
Susi@Num.13.11=H5485.short: Susi was the father of Gaddi, the spy from the tribe of Manasseh.

Syntyche@Php.4.2=G4941.brief: Woman in the Philippian church whom Paul exhorted
Syntyche@Php.4.2=G4941.short: Syntyche was a prominent woman in Philippi whom Paul urged to reconcile with Euodia.

Tabbaoth@Ezr.2.43-Neh=H2884.brief: Family of temple servants who returned from exile
Tabbaoth@Ezr.2.43-Neh=H2884.short: The Tabbaoth were a family of temple servants who returned to Judah from Babylonian exile.

Tabeal@Isa.7.6=H2870B.brief: Man whom Syria and Ephraim wanted to make king of Judah
Tabeal@Isa.7.6=H2870B.short: Tabeal was the man Syria and Ephraim conspired to make king of Judah in place of Ahaz.

Tabeel@Ezr.4.7=H2870A.brief: Persian official involved in accusing the Jews to Artaxerxes
Tabeel@Ezr.4.7=H2870A.short: Tabeel was a Persian official who joined in writing an accusation against the Jews to Artaxerxes.

Tabitha@Act.9.36-=G5000.brief: Charitable woman in Joppa whom Peter raised from the dead
Tabitha@Act.9.36-=G5000.short: Tabitha, also called Dorcas, was a beloved disciple in Joppa known for her charitable works, whom Peter raised from the dead.

Tabrimmon@1Ki.15.18=H2886.brief: Father of Ben-hadad I, king of Syria
Tabrimmon@1Ki.15.18=H2886.short: Tabrimmon was the father of Ben-hadad I, the king of Syria who was an ally of Asa king of Judah.

Tahan@1Ch.7.25=H8465H.brief: Son of Telah, from the tribe of Ephraim
Tahan@1Ch.7.25=H8465H.short: Tahan was a descendant of Ephraim, the son of Telah and father of Ladan.

Tahan@Num.26.35=H8465G.brief: Son of Ephraim, ancestor of the Tahanites clan
Tahan@Num.26.35=H8465G.short: Tahan was a son of Ephraim and the ancestor of the Tahanites clan.

Tahash@Gen.22.24=H8477.short: Tahash was a son of Abraham's brother Nahor and his concubine Reumah.

Tahath@1Ch.6.24-=H8480H.brief: Levite of the Kohathite clan, son of Assir
Tahath@1Ch.6.24-=H8480H.short: Tahath was a Levite of the Kohathite clan, the son of Assir and father of Uriel.

Tahath@1Ch.7.20a=H8480I.short: Tahath, a descendant of Ephraim mentioned in the genealogy.

Tahath@1Ch.7.20b=H8480J.short: Tahath, another descendant of Ephraim mentioned in the genealogy.

Tahpenes@1Ki.11.19-=H8472G.brief: Egyptian queen who raised Hadad the Edomite
Tahpenes@1Ki.11.19-=H8472G.short: Tahpenes was the queen of Egypt who gave her sister in marriage to Hadad the Edomite.

Talmai@2Sa.3.3-1Ch=H8526H.brief: King of Geshur; father of David's wife Maacah
Talmai@2Sa.3.3-1Ch=H8526H.short: Talmai was the king of Geshur and father of Maacah, one of David's wives and mother of Absalom.

Talmai@Num.13.22-Jdg=H8526G.brief: Anakim king of Hebron, defeated by Judah
Talmai@Num.13.22-Jdg=H8526G.short: Talmai was one of the Anakim kings of Hebron defeated by Caleb and the men of Judah.

Talmon@1Ch.9.17-Neh=H2929.brief: Levite gatekeeper who returned from Babylonian exile
Talmon@1Ch.9.17-Neh=H2929.short: Talmon was a Levite gatekeeper who returned from Babylon and served at the temple.

Tamar@2Sa.13.1-1Ch=H8559H.brief: David's daughter, raped by her half-brother Amnon
Tamar@2Sa.13.1-1Ch=H8559H.short: Tamar was David's daughter who was raped by her half-brother Amnon, leading to tragic consequences.

Tamar@2Sa.14.27=H8559I.short: Tamar was the beautiful daughter of Absalom, named after his tragic sister.

Tamar@Gen.38.6-Mat=H8559G.brief: Judah's daughter-in-law who bore Perez and Zerah
Tamar@Gen.38.6-Mat=H8559G.short: Tamar was Judah's daughter-in-law who, after being wronged by him, bore twin sons Perez and Zerah.

Tanhumeth@2Ki.25.23-Jer=H8576.brief: Supporter of Gedaliah after Jerusalem's fall
Tanhumeth@2Ki.25.23-Jer=H8576.short: Tanhumeth the Netophathite was one of the leaders who supported Gedaliah's governorship after Jerusalem's fall.

Taphath@1Ki.4.11=H2955.brief: Daughter of Solomon; wife of Ben-abinadab
Taphath@1Ki.4.11=H2955.short: Taphath was a daughter of Solomon who married Ben-abinadab, one of Solomon's district governors.

Tappuah@1Ch.2.43=H8599A.brief: Son of Hebron from the tribe of Judah
Tappuah@1Ch.2.43=H8599A.short: Tappuah was a son of Hebron, a descendant of Judah.

Tarea@1Ch.8.35-=H8390.brief: Son of Micah and grandson of Mephibosheth
Tarea@1Ch.8.35-=H8390.short: Tarea, also called Tahrea, was a son of Micah and grandson of Mephibosheth.

Tarshish@1Ch.7.10=H8659I.brief: Son of Bilhan from the tribe of Benjamin
Tarshish@1Ch.7.10=H8659I.short: Tarshish was a son of Bilhan, a descendant of Benjamin.

Tarshish@Est.1.14=H8659J.brief: One of the seven princes of Persia and Media
Tarshish@Est.1.14=H8659J.short: Tarshish was one of the seven princes of Persia and Media who had access to King Ahasuerus's presence and held the highest positions in the kingdom.

Tarshish@Gen.10.4-1Ch=H8659G.brief: Son of Javan, great-grandson of Noah
Tarshish@Gen.10.4-1Ch=H8659G.short: Tarshish was a son of Javan and great-grandson of Noah, associated with the ancient city of Tarshish.

Tartan@2Ki.18.17-Isa=H8661.brief: Title of an Assyrian military commander
Tartan@2Ki.18.17-Isa=H8661.short: The Tartan was a high-ranking Assyrian military commander who led campaigns against Ashdod and Jerusalem.

Tattenai@Ezr.5.3-=H8674.brief: Persian governor who questioned the Jews' authority to rebuild
Tattenai@Ezr.5.3-=H8674.short: Tattenai was the Persian governor of the province Beyond the River who questioned the Jews' authority to rebuild the temple.

Tebah@Gen.22.24=H2875.short: Tebah was a son of Abraham's brother Nahor and his concubine Reumah.

Tebaliah@1Ch.26.11=H2882.short: Tebaliah was a Levite gatekeeper, the third son of Hosah.

Tehinnah@1Ch.4.12=H8468.brief: Father of Ir-nahash from the tribe of Judah
Tehinnah@1Ch.4.12=H8468.short: Tehinnah was the father of Ir-nahash and a descendant of Chelub from the tribe of Judah.

Telah@1Ch.7.25=H8520.brief: Son of Resheph from the tribe of Ephraim
Telah@1Ch.7.25=H8520.short: Telah was a descendant of Ephraim, the son of Resheph and father of Tahan.

Telem@Ezr.10.24=H2928H.brief: Temple servant who married a foreign wife
Telem@Ezr.10.24=H2928H.short: Telem was a temple servant who married a foreign wife during the Exile and later divorced her.

Tema@Gen.25.15-1Ch=H8485G.brief: Son of Ishmael, associated with an Arabian city
Tema@Gen.25.15-1Ch=H8485G.short: Tema was a son of Ishmael and is associated with the ancient Arabian city of Tema.

Temah@Ezr.2.53-Neh=H8547.brief: Ancestor of a family of temple servants
Temah@Ezr.2.53-Neh=H8547.short: Temah was the ancestor of a family of temple servants who returned from the Babylonian exile.

Teman@Gen.36.11-Job=H8487G.brief: Grandson of Esau, associated with an Edomite clan
Teman@Gen.36.11-Job=H8487G.short: Teman was a grandson of Esau and is associated with an important Edomite clan known for its wisdom.

Temeni@1Ch.4.6=H8488.brief: Son of Ashhur (or 'Ashur') from the tribe of Judah
Temeni@1Ch.4.6=H8488.short: Temeni was a son of Ashhur (or 'Ashur') and a descendant of Judah.

Terah@Gen.11.24-Luk=H8646G.brief: Abraham's father who settled in Haran
Terah@Gen.11.24-Luk=H8646G.short: Terah was the father of Abraham, Nahor, and Haran, who left Ur to settle in Haran.

Teresh@Est.2.21-=H8657.brief: Persian official who plotted against King Ahasuerus
Teresh@Est.2.21-=H8657.short: Teresh was one of two Persian officials who plotted to assassinate King Ahasuerus but were discovered by Mordecai.

Tertius@Rom.16.22=G5060.brief: Paul's scribe who wrote the Epistle to the Romans
Tertius@Rom.16.22=G5060.short: Tertius served as Paul's scribe, writing down the Epistle to the Romans.

Tertullus@Act.24.1-=G5061.brief: Lawyer who accused Paul before Governor Felix
Tertullus@Act.24.1-=G5061.short: Tertullus was a lawyer hired by the Jewish authorities to accuse Paul before the Roman governor Felix.

Theophilus@Luk.1.3-Act=G2321.brief: Recipient of Luke's Gospel and Acts
Theophilus@Luk.1.3-Act=G2321.short: Theophilus was the recipient of Luke's Gospel and the Book of Acts, likely a Christian of high social standing.

Theudas@Act.5.36=G2333.brief: Jewish rebel leader killed by Roman authorities
Theudas@Act.5.36=G2333.short: Theudas was a Jewish rebel leader who was killed, and his followers scattered, by the Roman authorities.

Thomas@Mat.10.3-Act=G2381.brief: One of Jesus' twelve disciples, known for doubting
Thomas@Mat.10.3-Act=G2381.short: Thomas, also called Didymus, was one of Jesus' twelve disciples, known for doubting Jesus' resurrection until he saw him in person.

Tiberius@Mat.22.17-Jhn=G5086.brief: Roman emperor during Jesus' ministry and death
Tiberius@Mat.22.17-Jhn=G5086.short: Tiberius was the Roman emperor during Jesus' ministry and crucifixion, mentioned in several Gospel accounts.

Tibni@1Ki.16.21-=H8402.brief: Rival to Omri for the throne of Israel
Tibni@1Ki.16.21-=H8402.short: Tibni was a rival to Omri for the throne of Israel, leading to a divided kingdom until his death.

Tidal@Gen.14.1-=H8413.brief: King of Goiim, ally of Chedorlaomer
Tidal@Gen.14.1-=H8413.short: Tidal, king of Goiim, was one of the four kings allied with Chedorlaomer in the battle against the five kings of the plain.

Tiglath-pileser@2Ki.15.19-Hos=H8407.brief: Assyrian king who conquered parts of Israel
Tiglath-pileser@2Ki.15.19-Hos=H8407.short: Tiglath-pileser, also known as Pul, was an Assyrian king who conquered parts of Israel and received tribute from King Menahem.

Tikvah@2Ki.22.14-2Ch=H8616G.brief: Father of Shallum, husband of Huldah the prophetess
Tikvah@2Ki.22.14-2Ch=H8616G.short: Tikvah, also known as Tokhath, was the father of Shallum and the father-in-law of Huldah the prophetess.

Tikvah@Ezr.10.15=H8616H.brief: Opposed Ezra's reforms regarding foreign wives
Tikvah@Ezr.10.15=H8616H.short: Tikvah was one of two men who opposed Ezra's reforms requiring Jewish men to divorce their foreign wives.

Tilon@1Ch.4.20=H8436.brief: Son of Shimon from the tribe of Judah
Tilon@1Ch.4.20=H8436.short: Tilon was a son of Shimon, a descendant of Judah.

Timaeus@Mrk.10.46=G5090.brief: Father of Bartimaeus, a blind man healed by Jesus
Timaeus@Mrk.10.46=G5090.short: Timaeus was the father of Bartimaeus, a blind beggar who was healed by Jesus near Jericho.

Timna@Gen.36.12-1Ch=H8555.brief: Concubine of Eliphaz; mother of Amalek
Timna@Gen.36.12-1Ch=H8555.short: Timna was a concubine of Eliphaz, son of Esau, and the mother of Amalek.

Timon@Act.6.5=G5096.brief: One of the seven chosen to serve the church
Timon@Act.6.5=G5096.short: Timon was one of the seven men chosen by the apostles to oversee the daily distribution of food to widows in the early church.

Timothy@Act.16.1-Heb=G5095G.short: Timothy was a young disciple and co-worker of Paul, who accompanied him on his missionary journeys and later served as a pastor.

Tiras@Gen.10.2-1Ch=H8494.brief: Son of Japheth, grandson of Noah
Tiras@Gen.10.2-1Ch=H8494.short: Tiras was a son of Japheth and grandson of Noah, listed among the nations descended from Noah after the flood.

Tirhakah@2Ki.19.9-Isa=H8640.brief: King of Cush (Ethiopia) who opposed Sennacherib
Tirhakah@2Ki.19.9-Isa=H8640.short: Tirhakah, the king of Cush (Ethiopia), opposed Sennacherib's invasion of Judah during the reign of King Hezekiah.

Tirhanah@1Ch.2.48=H8647.brief: Son of Caleb by his concubine Maacah
Tirhanah@1Ch.2.48=H8647.short: Tirhanah was a son of Caleb by his concubine Maacah, mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.

Tiria@1Ch.4.16=H8493.brief: Son of Jehallelel from the tribe of Judah
Tiria@1Ch.4.16=H8493.short: Tiria was a son of Jehallelel, a descendant of Judah, mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.

Tirzah@Num.26.33-Jos=H8656G.brief: Daughter of Zelophehad, granted inheritance rights
Tirzah@Num.26.33-Jos=H8656G.short: Tirzah was one of the five daughters of Zelophehad who were granted inheritance rights in the absence of male heirs.

Titus@2Co.2.13-Tit=G5103.brief: Gentile convert and companion of Paul
Titus@2Co.2.13-Tit=G5103.short: Titus was a Gentile convert and a trusted companion of Paul, who accompanied him on missionary journeys and served as his delegate to the church in Corinth.

Tizites@1Ch.11.45=H8491.brief: Clan from the tribe of Manasseh
Tizites@1Ch.11.45=H8491.short: The Tizites were a clan from the tribe of Manasseh, mentioned among the mighty warriors who joined David at Ziklag.

Tobadonijah@2Ch.17.8=H2899.brief: Levite sent by Jehoshaphat to teach the Law
Tobadonijah@2Ch.17.8=H2899.short: Tobadonijah was a Levite sent by King Jehoshaphat to teach the Book of the Law in the cities of Judah.

Tobiah@Ezr.2.60-Neh=H2900H.brief: Ancestor of returned exiles unable to prove lineage
Tobiah@Ezr.2.60-Neh=H2900H.short: Tobiah was an ancestor of some returned exiles who were unable to prove their Israelite lineage and were excluded from the priesthood.

Tobiah@Neh.2.10-=H2900I.brief: Ammonite official who opposed Nehemiah's rebuilding efforts
Tobiah@Neh.2.10-=H2900I.short: Tobiah was an Ammonite official who, along with Sanballat the Horonite, opposed Nehemiah's efforts to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem.

Tobijah@2Ch.17.8=H2900G.brief: Levite sent by Jehoshaphat to teach the Law
Tobijah@2Ch.17.8=H2900G.short: Tobijah was a Levite sent by King Jehoshaphat to teach the Book of the Law in the cities of Judah.

Tobijah@Zec.6.10-=H2900J.brief: Postexilic Jew who provided silver and gold for crowns
Tobijah@Zec.6.10-=H2900J.short: Tobijah was a postexilic Jew who, along with others, provided silver and gold to make crowns for Joshua the high priest.

Togarmah@Gen.10.3-1Ch=H8425G.brief: Son of Gomer, grandson of Japheth
Togarmah@Gen.10.3-1Ch=H8425G.short: Togarmah was a son of Gomer and grandson of Japheth, mentioned in the Table of Nations.

Tohu@1Sa.1.1-1Ch=H8459.short: Tohu, also known as Nahath or Toah, was an ancestor of the prophet Samuel, mentioned in his genealogy.

Toi@2Sa.8.9-1Ch=H8583.brief: King of Hamath who sent his son to David
Toi@2Sa.8.9-1Ch=H8583.short: Toi, also known as Tou, was the king of Hamath who sent his son Joram to congratulate David on his victory over Hadadezer.

Tola@Gen.46.13-1Ch=H8439G.brief: Son of Issachar, ancestor of the Tolaites
Tola@Gen.46.13-1Ch=H8439G.short: Tola was a son of Issachar and the ancestor of the Tolaite clan.

Tola@Jdg.10.1=H8439H.brief: Judge of Israel who succeeded Abimelech
Tola@Jdg.10.1=H8439H.short: Tola, the son of Puah, was a judge of Israel who ruled for 23 years after Abimelech's death.

Trophimus@Act.20.4-2Ti=G5161.brief: Gentile Christian from Ephesus, companion of Paul
Trophimus@Act.20.4-2Ti=G5161.short: Trophimus was a Gentile Christian from Ephesus who accompanied Paul on his missionary journeys and was falsely accused of defiling the temple in Jerusalem.

Tryphaena@Rom.16.12=G5170.brief: Christian woman in Rome greeted by Paul
Tryphaena@Rom.16.12=G5170.short: Tryphaena was a Christian woman in Rome to whom Paul sent greetings in his letter to the Romans.

Tryphosa@Rom.16.12=G5173.brief: Christian woman in Rome greeted by Paul
Tryphosa@Rom.16.12=G5173.short: Tryphosa was a Christian woman in Rome to whom Paul sent greetings in his letter to the Romans.

Tubal@Gen.10.2-1Ch=H8422G.brief: Son of Japheth, grandson of Noah
Tubal@Gen.10.2-1Ch=H8422G.short: Tubal was a son of Japheth and grandson of Noah, mentioned in the Table of Nations.

Tubal-cain@Gen.4.22=H8423.short: Tubal-cain, a descendant of Cain, was the first metalworker mentioned in the Bible, forging tools out of bronze and iron.

Tychicus@Act.20.4-Tit=G5190.brief: Faithful companion and messenger of Paul
Tychicus@Act.20.4-Tit=G5190.short: Tychicus was a faithful companion of Paul who served as his messenger to the churches in Asia Minor.

Tyrannus@Act.19.9=G5181.brief: Ephesian teacher who hosted Paul's discussions
Tyrannus@Act.19.9=G5181.short: Tyrannus was a teacher in Ephesus who allowed Paul to use his lecture hall for daily discussions about the gospel.

Ucal@Pro.30.1=H0401.brief: Recipient of Agur's wisdom in Proverbs 30
Ucal@Pro.30.1=H0401.short: Ucal is mentioned in Proverbs 30:1 as one of the recipients of the wise sayings of Agur son of Jakeh.

Uel@Ezr.10.34=H0177.brief: Israelite who agreed to put away his foreign wife
Uel@Ezr.10.34=H0177.short: Uel was one of the Israelites who agreed to put away his foreign wife during the time of Ezra's reforms.

Ulam@1Ch.7.16-=H0198G.brief: Son of Sheresh, great-grandson of Manasseh
Ulam@1Ch.7.16-=H0198G.short: Ulam was a son of Sheresh and great-grandson of Manasseh, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Manasseh.

Ulam@1Ch.8.39-=H0198H.brief: Descendant of Benjamin, known for his numerous descendants
Ulam@1Ch.8.39-=H0198H.short: Ulam was a descendant of Benjamin known for his numerous descendants, including many skilled archers.

Unni@1Ch.15.18-=H6042G.short: Unni was a Levite musician who played the harp and participated in the procession when the ark was brought to Jerusalem during David's reign.

Unni@Neh.12.9=H6042H.brief: Postexilic Levite who assisted in the temple
Unni@Neh.12.9=H6042H.short: Unni was a postexilic Levite who assisted in the temple during the time of Nehemiah.

Ur@1Ch.11.35=H0218A.brief: Father of one of David's mighty men
Ur@1Ch.11.35=H0218A.short: Ur was the father of Eliphal, one of David's mighty men.

Urbanus@Rom.16.9=G3773.brief: Christian in Rome greeted by Paul
Urbanus@Rom.16.9=G3773.short: Urbanus was a Christian in Rome whom Paul called a fellow worker in Christ and to whom he sent greetings.

Uri@1Ki.4.19=H0221H.brief: Father of Geber, one of Solomon's officers
Uri@1Ki.4.19=H0221H.short: Uri was the father of Geber, one of the twelve officers appointed by Solomon to provide for the king and his household.

Uri@Exo.31.2-2Ch=H0221G.brief: Father of Bezalel, the skilled craftsman
Uri@Exo.31.2-2Ch=H0221G.short: Uri was the father of Bezalel, the skilled craftsman chosen by God to construct the tabernacle and its furnishings.

Uri@Ezr.10.24=H0221I.brief: Postexilic Israelite who agreed to put away his foreign wife
Uri@Ezr.10.24=H0221I.short: Uri was one of the postexilic Israelites who agreed to put away his foreign wife during the time of Ezra's reforms.

Uriah@2Ki.16.10-Isa=H0223G.brief: Priest during the reign of King Ahaz
Uriah@2Ki.16.10-Isa=H0223G.short: Uriah was a priest during the reign of King Ahaz who followed the king's instructions in building a new altar based on a pagan model from Damascus.

Uriah@2Sa.11.3-Mat=H0223A.short: Uriah was a Hittite soldier in David's army, the husband of Bathsheba, who was killed in battle as part of David's plan to cover up his adultery with Bathsheba.

Uriah@Ezr.8.33-Neh=H0223H.brief: Postexilic priest involved in rebuilding the wall
Uriah@Ezr.8.33-Neh=H0223H.short: Uriah was a postexilic priest who participated in rebuilding the wall of Jerusalem and was entrusted with the temple treasures.

Uriah@Jer.26.20-=H0223B.brief: Prophet from Kiriath-jearim who prophesied against Jerusalem
Uriah@Jer.26.20-=H0223B.short: Uriah was a prophet from Kiriath-jearim who prophesied against Jerusalem and Judah during the reign of King Jehoiakim, and was killed for his message.

Uriah@Neh.8.4=H0223I.brief: Priest who assisted Ezra in reading the Law
Uriah@Neh.8.4=H0223I.short: Uriah was one of the priests who assisted Ezra in reading the Law to the people during the religious revival in Jerusalem.

Uriel@1Ch.15.5-=H0222H.brief: Kohathite leader who helped bring the ark to Jerusalem
Uriel@1Ch.15.5-=H0222H.short: Uriel, a Kohathite leader, assisted in bringing the ark to Jerusalem.

Uriel@1Ch.6.24-=H0222G.brief: Kohathite Levite, ancestor of the prophet Samuel
Uriel@1Ch.6.24-=H0222G.short: Uriel, also known as Zephaniah, was a Kohathite Levite and an ancestor of the prophet Samuel.

Uriel@2Ch.13.2=H0222I.brief: Father of mother of Abijah, king of Judah
Uriel@2Ch.13.2=H0222I.short: Uriel was the father of the mother of Abijah, king of Judah.

Uthai@1Ch.9.4=H5793G.brief: Judahite who resettled in Jerusalem after the exile
Uthai@1Ch.9.4=H5793G.short: Uthai, a descendant of Perez, resettled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.

Uthai@Ezr.8.14=H5793H.brief: Exile who returned to Jerusalem with Ezra
Uthai@Ezr.8.14=H5793H.short: Uthai, along with Zabbud, led a group returning to Jerusalem with Ezra.

Uz@Gen.10.23-1Ch=H5780G.brief: Son of Aram, grandson of Shem
Uz@Gen.10.23-1Ch=H5780G.short: Uz, son of Aram and grandson of Shem, was an early Semitic patriarch.

Uz@Gen.22.21=H5780H.short: Uz, son of Nahor and nephew of Abraham, was an Aramean.

Uz@Gen.36.28-1Ch=H5780I.brief: Son of Dishan, a Horite chief
Uz@Gen.36.28-1Ch=H5780I.short: Uz, a Horite, was the son of Dishan, a chief in Seir.

Uzai@Neh.3.25=H0186.brief: Father of Palal, who repaired Jerusalem's wall
Uzai@Neh.3.25=H0186.short: Uzai was the father of Palal, who helped repair Jerusalem's wall.

Uzal@Gen.10.27-1Ch=H0187G.brief: Son of Joktan, descendant of Shem
Uzal@Gen.10.27-1Ch=H0187G.short: Uzal, a descendant of Shem, was one of Joktan's sons.

Uzza@1Ch.8.7=H5798H.short: Uzza was a Benjamite born in Moab during the exile.

Uzza@Ezr.2.49-Neh=H5798I.brief: Ancestor of temple servants who returned from Babylon
Uzza@Ezr.2.49-Neh=H5798I.short: Uzza was an ancestor of temple servants who returned from Babylonian exile.

Caesarea_Philippi@Mat.16.13-Mrk=G2542G.short: Caesarea Philippi was the location where Peter acknowledged Jesus as the Messiah and Son of God.

Capernaum@Mat.4.13-Jhn=G2584.short: Capernaum was a fishing village on the Sea of Galilee that served as a center for Jesus' ministry in the region.

Caphtor@Deu.2.23-Tit=H3731.brief: Island home of the Philistines; visited by Paul
Caphtor@Deu.2.23-Tit=H3731.short: Caphtor, identified as the island of Crete, was the original homeland of the Philistines and a place visited by the apostle Paul.

Carchemish@2Ch.35.20-Jer=H3751.brief: Ancient city; site of Babylonian victory over Egypt

Carmel@Jos.12.22-Nam=H3760G.brief: Town in Judah; home of Nabal and Abigail

Carmel_Mount@1Ki.18.19-2Ki=H3760H.short: Mount Carmel was a mountain range in northern Israel where the prophet Elijah confronted the prophets of Baal.

Casiphia@Ezr.8.17=H3703.brief: Place where Levites were recruited for temple service
Casiphia@Ezr.8.17=H3703.short: Casiphia was a place in Babylon where Ezra sent for Levites to join the returning exiles in Jerusalem.

Cauda@Act.27.16=G2802.short: Cauda was an island where the ship carrying Paul sought shelter during a storm on his journey to Rome.

Chesalon@Jos.15.10=H3693.short: Chesalon, also known as Mount Jearim, was a landmark on the northern boundary of Judah, near Bethshemesh.

Eglath-shelishiyah@Isa.15.5-Jer=H5697B.short: Eglath-shelishiyah, a Moabite city whose destruction was prophesied by Isaiah and Jeremiah.

Ekron@Jos.13.3-Zec=H6138.short: Ekron, one of the five principal Philistine cities, located in southwestern Canaan.

Elah_Valley@1Sa.17.2-=H0425L.brief: Site of David's victory over Goliath
Elah_Valley@1Sa.17.2-=H0425L.short: The Elah Valley, where David defeated the Philistine giant Goliath.

Elam@Gen.14.1-Act=H5867A.brief: Ancient kingdom east of Babylon; ally and enemy of Israel
Elam@Gen.14.1-Act=H5867A.short: Elam, an ancient nation east of Babylon, at times an ally and at times an enemy of Israel.
