Eltekon@Jos.15.59=H0515.brief: City in the hill country of Judah
Eltekon@Jos.15.59=H0515.short: Eltekon, a city in the hill country of Judah, mentioned in the list of cities allotted to Judah.

Eltolad@Jos.15.30-=H0513.brief: A town allotted to Judah and Simeon
Eltolad@Jos.15.30-=H0513.short: Eltolad, a town allotted to the tribes of Judah and Simeon in the Negev region.

Emek-keziz@Jos.18.21=H6010J.short: Emek-keziz, a town within the territory allotted to the tribe of Benjamin.

Emmaus@Luk.24.13=G1695.brief: Emmaus, village where Jesus appeared to two disciples after resurrection
Emmaus@Luk.24.13=G1695.short: Emmaus, a village approximately seven miles from Jerusalem, where Jesus appeared to two disciples after His resurrection.

Enaim@Gen.38.14-=H5879G.brief: Enaim, place where Tamar posed as a prostitute
Enaim@Gen.38.14-=H5879G.short: Enaim, the place where Tamar sat and posed as a prostitute to deceive Judah.

Enam@Jos.15.34=H5879H.brief: Enam, town allotted to Judah in the Shephelah
Enam@Jos.15.34=H5879H.short: Enam, a town in the Shephelah region, allotted to the tribe of Judah.

En-dor@Jos.17.11-Psa=H5874.brief: Canaanite city; site of Saul's consultation with medium
En-dor@Jos.17.11-Psa=H5874.short: En-dor, a Canaanite city where Saul consulted a medium before his final battle with the Philistines.

Eneglaim@Ezk.47.10=H5882.brief: Place mentioned in Ezekiel's vision of restored Israel
Eneglaim@Ezk.47.10=H5882.short: Eneglaim, a place mentioned in Ezekiel's vision of the restored land of Israel.

En-gannim@Jos.15.34=H5873G.brief: City in the lowlands of Judah
En-gannim@Jos.15.34=H5873G.short: En-gannim, a city in the lowlands of Judah, mentioned in the list of cities allotted to Judah.

En-gannim@Jos.19.21-1Ch=H5873H.short: En-gannim (or Anem), a Levitical city in the territory of Issachar, given to the Gershonite Levites.

Engedi@Gen.14.7-Ezk=H5872.brief: Oasis in Judah; refuge for David; Chedorlaomer's victory
Engedi@Gen.14.7-Ezk=H5872.short: Engedi (or Hazazon-tamar), an oasis in Judah where David sought refuge from Saul, also the site of Chedorlaomer's victory.

En-haddah@Jos.19.21=H5876.brief: City allotted to the tribe of Issachar
En-haddah@Jos.19.21=H5876.short: En-haddah, a city allotted to the tribe of Issachar during the division of the Promised Land.

En-hakkore@Jdg.15.19=H5875.brief: Spring that appeared after Samson's victory over the Philistines
En-hakkore@Jdg.15.19=H5875.short: En-hakkore, the spring that God provided for Samson after his victory over the Philistines at Lehi.

En-hazor@Jos.19.37=H5877.brief: City allotted to the tribe of Naphtali
En-hazor@Jos.19.37=H5877.short: En-hazor, a city allotted to the tribe of Naphtali during the division of the Promised Land.

En-rogel@Jos.15.7-1Ki=H5883.brief: Spring near Jerusalem; associated with Adonijah's and David's kingships
En-rogel@Jos.15.7-1Ki=H5883.short: En-rogel, a spring near Jerusalem, was the site of Adonijah's attempt to become king and later served as a meeting place for David's supporters.

En-shemesh@Jos.15.7-=H5885.brief: Spring on the border between Judah and Benjamin
En-shemesh@Jos.15.7-=H5885.short: En-shemesh, a spring on the border between the territories of Judah and Benjamin, near Jerusalem.

Ephah@Isa.60.6=H5891J.brief: Arabian tribe; known for their camels and dromedaries
Ephah@Isa.60.6=H5891J.short: Ephah, an Arabian tribe known for their camels and dromedaries, mentioned in Isaiah's prophecy of nations coming to Jerusalem.

Ephes-dammim@1Sa.17.1-1Ch=H0658.brief: Place where the Philistines and Israelites fought; Goliath's challenge
Ephes-dammim@1Sa.17.1-1Ch=H0658.short: Ephes-dammim (or Pas-dammim), the place where the Philistines and Israelites faced each other in battle, and where Goliath challenged the Israelites.

Ephesus@Act.18.19-Rev=G2181.brief: Major city in Asia Minor; important center for early Christianity
Ephesus@Act.18.19-Rev=G2181.short: Ephesus, a major city in Asia Minor, was an important center for early Christianity and the recipient of one of Paul's epistles.

Ephraim@2Sa.13.23-Jhn=H0669L.brief: City near the Judean wilderness; Jesus withdrew there
Ephraim@2Sa.13.23-Jhn=H0669L.short: Ephraim, a city near the Judean wilderness where Jesus withdrew after the raising of Lazarus.

Ephraim_Gate@2Ki.14.13-2Ch=H0669H.brief: Gate in Jerusalem's wall, broken down by King Jehoash
Ephraim_Gate@2Ki.14.13-2Ch=H0669H.short: The Ephraim Gate, a gate in Jerusalem's wall that was broken down by King Jehoash of Israel during his conflict with King Amaziah of Judah.

Ephraim_Gate@Neh.8.16-=H0669I.brief: Gate in Jerusalem's wall, rebuilt during Nehemiah's time
Ephraim_Gate@Neh.8.16-=H0669I.short: The Ephraim Gate, a gate in Jerusalem's wall that was rebuilt during Nehemiah's time and used for public gatherings and proce∟ssions.

Ephron_Mount@Jos.15.9-=H6085H.brief: Mountain on the border between Judah and Benjamin
Ephron_Mount@Jos.15.9-=H6085H.short: Mount Ephron, a mountain on the border between the territories of Judah and Benjamin, near Kiriath-jearim.

Erech@Gen.10.10-Ezr=H0751.brief: Ancient Mesopotamian city; part of Nimrod's kingdom
Erech@Gen.10.10-Ezr=H0751.short: Erech, an ancient Mesopotamian city that was part of Nimrod's kingdom and later inhabited by people who opposed the rebuilding of the Jerusalem Temple.

Esau_Mount@Oba.1.8-=H6215I.brief: Mountainous region of Edom; judgment prophesied by Obadiah
Esau_Mount@Oba.1.8-=H6215I.short: Mount Esau, the mountainous region of Edom, against which the prophet Obadiah declared God's judgment for their hostility toward Israel.

Esek@Gen.26.20=H6230.brief: Well dug by Isaac's servants; named after quarrel
Esek@Gen.26.20=H6230.short: Esek, a well dug by Isaac's servants, named after a quarrel with local herdsmen.

Eshan@Jos.15.52=H0824.brief: City in the hill country of Judah
Eshan@Jos.15.52=H0824.short: Eshan, a city in the hill country of Judah, allotted to the tribe of Judah.

Eshcol_Valley@Num.13.23-Deu=H0812H.brief: Valley where Israelite spies obtained a large cluster of grapes
Eshcol_Valley@Num.13.23-Deu=H0812H.short: The Eshcol Valley, where the Israelite spies cut down a large cluster of grapes during their reconnaissance mission in Canaan.

Eshtaol@Jos.15.33-1Ch=H0847.brief: City allotted to Judah and Dan; associated with Samson
Eshtaol@Jos.15.33-1Ch=H0847.short: Eshtaol, a city allotted to Judah and Dan, was the hometown of Samson and the starting point of the Danite migration.

Eshtemoa@Jos.15.50-1Ch=H0851.brief: Levitical city in Judah; received spoils from David's victory
Eshtemoa@Jos.15.50-1Ch=H0851.short: Eshtemoa (or Eshtemoh), a Levitical city in Judah, was the home of several individuals and received spoils from David's victory over the Amalekites.

Etam@1Ch.4.3-=H5862H.brief: Villages associated with Simeon; home of Judahite clan
Etam@1Ch.4.3-=H5862H.short: Etam, a village associated with the tribe of Simeon and the home of a Judahite clan.

Etam@2Ch.11.6=H5862I.brief: City fortified by Rehoboam in Judah
Etam@2Ch.11.6=H5862I.short: Etam, a city in Judah fortified by King Rehoboam after the division of the kingdom.

Etam@Jdg.15.8-=H5862G.brief: Cliff where Samson hid after defeating the Philistines
Etam@Jdg.15.8-=H5862G.short: Etam, the cliff where Samson hid after defeating the Philistines, located in Judah.

Etham@Exo.13.20-Num=H0864.brief: Wilderness area where Israelites camped during the Exodus
Etham@Exo.13.20-Num=H0864.short: Etham, a wilderness area on the edge of the desert where the Israelites camped during their journey from Egypt to the Promised Land.

Ether@Jos.15.42-=H6281.brief: City allotted to Judah and Simeon
Ether@Jos.15.42-=H6281.short: Ether, a city allotted to the tribes of Judah and Simeon in the Shephelah region.

Eth-kazin@Jos.19.13=H6278.brief: Border town of Zebulun near Neah
Eth-kazin@Jos.19.13=H6278.short: Eth-kazin, a border town of Zebulun located near Neah.

Euphrates@Gen.2.14-Rev=H6578.brief: Major river in ancient Near East; boundary of Promised Land
Euphrates@Gen.2.14-Rev=H6578.short: The Euphrates, a major river in the ancient Near East, often served as a boundary marker for the Promised Land and was the site of significant events in biblical history.

Ezel_Stone@1Sa.20.19=H0237.brief: Location where David and Jonathan planned to meet
Ezel_Stone@1Sa.20.19=H0237.short: The Stone of Ezel, a location where David and Jonathan planned to meet and communicate secretly during David's flight from King Saul.

Ezem@Jos.15.29-1Ch=H6107.brief: City allotted to Judah and Simeon
Ezem@Jos.15.29-1Ch=H6107.short: Ezem, a city allotted to the tribes of Judah and Simeon in the Negev region.

Ezion-geber@Num.33.35-2Ch=H6100.brief: Israelite encampment; port city on Red Sea
Ezion-geber@Num.33.35-2Ch=H6100.short: Ezion-geber, an Israelite encampment during the Exodus and later a port city on the Red Sea, known for its maritime trade and shipbuilding.

Fair_Havens@Act.27.8=G2570H.brief: Harbor on Crete; Paul's ship stopped during journey to Rome
Fair_Havens@Act.27.8=G2570H.short: Fair Havens, a harbor on the island of Crete where Paul's ship stopped during his journey to Rome.

Fish_Gate@2Ch.33.14-Zep=H1709G.brief: Gate in Jerusalem's wall; rebuilt by Hassenaah during Nehemiah's time
Fish_Gate@2Ch.33.14-Zep=H1709G.short: The Fish Gate, a gate in Jerusalem's wall, was rebuilt by the sons of Hassenaah during Nehemiah's time and was a location of judgment and trade.

Forest_Ephraim@2Sa.18.6=H0669K.brief: Location of the battle between David's forces and Absalom's army
Forest_Ephraim@2Sa.18.6=H0669K.short: The Forest of Ephraim, where the battle between David's forces and Absalom's army took place during Absalom's rebellion.

Forum_of_Appius@Act.28.15=G0675.brief: Marketplace on Appian Way; Christians met Paul on journey to Rome
Forum_of_Appius@Act.28.15=G0675.short: The Forum of Appius, a marketplace on the Appian Way, where Christians from Rome met Paul during his journey to the city as a prisoner.

Foundation_Gate@2Ch.23.5=H3247G.brief: Gate in Jerusalem's wall; location of Levite singers during coronation
Foundation_Gate@2Ch.23.5=H3247G.short: The Foundation Gate, a gate in Jerusalem's wall, where a third of the Levite singers were positioned during the coronation of Joash.

Fountain_Gate@Neh.2.14-=H5869B.brief: Gate in Jerusalem's wall; rebuilt by Shallun during Nehemiah's time
Fountain_Gate@Neh.2.14-=H5869B.short: The Fountain Gate, a gate in Jerusalem's wall, was rebuilt by Shallun during Nehemiah's time and was a location for processions and gatherings.

Gaash@Jos.24.30-1Ch=H1608.brief: Mountain in Ephraim; burial place of Joshua
Gaash@Jos.24.30-1Ch=H1608.short: Gaash, a mountain in the region of Ephraim, was the burial place of Joshua and the homeland of two of David's mighty men.

Gabbatha@Jhn.19.13=G1042.brief: Raised stone platform in Jerusalem; location of Jesus' trial
Gabbatha@Jhn.19.13=G1042.short: Gabbatha, also known as the Stone Pavement, was the location in Jerusalem where Pontius Pilate sat in judgment over Jesus.

Galatia@Act.16.6-1Pe=G1053.brief: A region in Asia Minor, recipient of Paul's epistle.
Galatia@Act.16.6-1Pe=G1053.short: Galatia, a region in Asia Minor, was the recipient of Paul's epistle to the Galatians and was visited by Paul on his missionary journeys (Act.16.6; 18:23; 1Co.16.1; Galatians 1:2; 3:1; 6:18; 2Ti.4.10; 1Pe.1.1).

Galilee@Jos.12.23-Act=H1551.brief: Region in northern Israel; key location in Jesus' ministry
Galilee@Jos.12.23-Act=H1551.short: Galilee, a region in northern Israel, was a significant location in Jesus' life and ministry, as well as the homeland of many of his disciples.

Gallim@1Sa.25.44-Isa=H1554.brief: Town in Benjamin; home of Michal's husband Paltiel
Gallim@1Sa.25.44-Isa=H1554.short: Gallim, a town in Benjamin, was the home of Paltiel, Michal's husband, and is mentioned in a prophecy of Isaiah.

Gamad@Ezk.27.11=H1575.brief: People group; defenders of the towers of Tyre
Gamad@Ezk.27.11=H1575.short: The Gamad were a people group mentioned in Ezekiel's prophecy as defenders of the towers of Tyre.

Gareb@Jer.31.39=H1619H.short: Gareb, a hill mentioned in Jeremiah 31:39, was located near Jerusalem and was to be included within the city's future boundaries.

Gath@Jos.11.22-Mic=H1661.brief: Philistine city; home of Goliath; refuge for David
Gath@Jos.11.22-Mic=H1661.short: Gath, one of the five major Philistine cities, was the hometown of Goliath and a place of refuge for David during his flight from Saul.

Gath-hepher@Jos.19.13-2Ki=H1662.brief: Town in Zebulun; hometown of prophet Jonah
Gath-hepher@Jos.19.13-2Ki=H1662.short: Gath-hepher, a town in the territory of Zebulun, was the hometown of the prophet Jonah.

Gath-rimmon@Jos.19.45-1Ch=H1667G.brief: Levitical city in Dan and Manasseh
Gath-rimmon@Jos.19.45-1Ch=H1667G.short: Gath-rimmon, a Levitical city, was allotted to the Kohathite Levites within the territories of Dan and Manasseh.

Gaza@Gen.10.19-Act=H5804.brief: Philistine city; Samson's exploits; Philip's ministry
Gaza@Gen.10.19-Act=H5804.short: Gaza, one of the five major Philistine cities, was the site of Samson's exploits and a place visited by Philip the evangelist in the early church.

Geba@Jos.18.24-Zec=H1387G.short: Geba, a Levitical city in the territory of Benjamin, was located on the northern border of the kingdom of Judah (Joshua 18:24; 1Ki.15.22).

Gebal@Jos.13.5-Ezk=H1380.brief: Phoenician city; skilled builders; allied against Israel
Gebal@Jos.13.5-Ezk=H1380.short: Gebal, a Phoenician city known for its skilled builders, was allied against Israel and provided materials for Solomon's temple.

Gebim@Isa.10.31=H1374.brief: Town in Benjamin; mentioned in Isaiah's prophecy
Gebim@Isa.10.31=H1374.short: Gebim, a town in Benjamin, is mentioned in Isaiah's prophecy describing the advance of the Assyrian army towards Jerusalem.

Gederah@Jos.15.36-1Ch=H1449.brief: Town in Judah; home of Baal-hanan and Jozabad
Gederah@Jos.15.36-1Ch=H1449.short: Gederah, a town in Judah, was the home of Baal-hanan, one of David's overseers, and Jozabad, one of his mighty men.

Gederoth@Jos.15.41-2Ch=H1450.brief: Town in Judah; captured by Philistines during Ahaz's reign
Gederoth@Jos.15.41-2Ch=H1450.short: Gederoth, a town in Judah, was captured by the Philistines during the reign of King Ahaz.

Gederothaim@Jos.15.36=H1453.brief: Town in Judah; mentioned in list of allotted cities
Gederothaim@Jos.15.36=H1453.short: Gederothaim, a town in Judah, is mentioned in the list of cities allotted to the tribe of Judah.

Gedor@1Ch.4.39=H1446H.brief: Region where Simeonites sought pasture for their flocks
Gedor@1Ch.4.39=H1446H.short: Gedor, a region where some Simeonites went to find pasture for their flocks during the reign of King Hezekiah.

Gedor@Jos.12.13-1Ch=H1446G.brief: Town in Judah; home of Judahite clan members
Gedor@Jos.12.13-1Ch=H1446G.short: Gedor (or Geder), a town in the hill country of Judah, was the home of several members of Judahite clans.

Ge-harashim@1Ch.4.14-Neh=H2798.brief: Valley of craftsmen; inhabited by Benjamites after the exile
Ge-harashim@1Ch.4.14-Neh=H2798.short: Ge-harashim, the Valley of Craftsmen, was inhabited by some Benjamites after the return from the Babylonian exile.

Gennesaret@Mat.14.34-Luk=G1082.brief: Plain on the northwest shore of the Sea of Galilee
Gennesaret@Mat.14.34-Luk=G1082.short: Gennesaret, a fertile plain on the northwest shore of the Sea of Galilee, was the location of several events in Jesus' ministry.

Gerar@Gen.10.19-2Ch=H1642.brief: Philistine city; Abraham and Isaac's encounters with Abimelech
Gerar@Gen.10.19-2Ch=H1642.short: Gerar, a Philistine city, was the location of Abraham and Isaac's encounters with Abimelech and the site of a battle during King Asa's reign.

Gerasa@Mat.8.28-Luk=G1086G.brief: Region where Jesus healed a demon-possessed man
Gerasa@Mat.8.28-Luk=G1086G.short: Gerasa (or Gadara), a region southeast of the Sea of Galilee, was the location where Jesus healed a demon-possessed man.

Gerizim_Mount@Deu.11.29-Jdg=H1630.brief: Mountain in Samaria; site of blessings and Jotham's parable
Gerizim_Mount@Deu.11.29-Jdg=H1630.short: Mount Gerizim, a mountain in Samaria, was designated as the site for pronouncing blessings and was the location of Jotham's parable to the men of Shechem.

Geruth_Chimham@Jer.41.17=H1628.brief: Lodging place near Bethlehem; refuge for Johanan's group
Geruth_Chimham@Jer.41.17=H1628.short: Geruth Chimham, a lodging place near Bethlehem, served as a temporary refuge for Johanan and his group after the murder of Gedaliah.

Geshur@Deu.3.14-1Ch=H1650.brief: Aramean kingdom; Talmai's domain; refuge for Absalom
Geshur@Deu.3.14-1Ch=H1650.short: Geshur, an Aramean kingdom ruled by Talmai, was the homeland of David's wife Maacah and a refuge for Absalom after he murdered his half-brother Amnon.

Gethsemane@Mat.26.36-Mrk=G1068.brief: Garden near Jerusalem; site of Jesus' prayer and arrest
Gethsemane@Mat.26.36-Mrk=G1068.short: Gethsemane, a garden at the Mount of Olives, was the site where Jesus prayed and was arrested before his crucifixion.

Gezer@Jos.10.33-1Ch=H1507.brief: A Canaanite city, conquered by Joshua and later by David.
Gezer@Jos.10.33-1Ch=H1507.short: Gezer, also known as Gob, was a Canaanite city conquered by Joshua and later by David, and it was fortified by Solomon (Joshua 10:33; 12:12; 16:3, 10; 21:21; Judges 1:29; 2Sa.5.25; 21:18-19; 1Ki.9.15-17; 1Ch.6.67; 7:28; 14:16; 20:4, 10; 21:21; Judges 1:29; 2Sa.5.25; 21:18-19; 1Ki.9.15-17; 1Ch.6.67; 7:28; 14:16; 20:4).

Giah@2Sa.2.24=H1520.brief: Location near Gibeon where Joab and Abishai pursued Abner.
Giah@2Sa.2.24=H1520.short: Giah was a place near Gibeon where Joab and Abishai pursued Abner after the battle at the pool of Gibeon.

Gibbethon@Jos.19.44-1Ki=H1405.brief: A Levitical city in the territory of Dan.
Gibbethon@Jos.19.44-1Ki=H1405.short: Gibbethon, a Levitical city in the territory of Dan, was the site of conflict during the reigns of Nadab and Baasha (Joshua 19:44; 21:23; 1Ki.15.27; 16:15, 17).

Gibeah@Jos.15.57-2Ch=H1390G.brief: A town in the hill country of Judah.
Gibeah@Jos.15.57-2Ch=H1390G.short: Gibeah, a town in the hill country of Judah, was the hometown of Maacah, the mother of King Abijah (Joshua 15:57; 2Ch.13.2).

Gibeah@Jos.18.28-Hos=H1390H.brief: A city of Benjamin, associated with Saul and atrocities.
Gibeah@Jos.18.28-Hos=H1390H.short: Gibeah, a city of Benjamin, was the hometown of Saul and the site of infamous atrocities during the time of the judges (Judges 19-20; 1Sa.10.5, 10, 26; 15:34; Hosea 9:9; 10:9).

Gibeath-elohim@1Sa.10.5=H1389G.brief: A place with a garrison of Philistines, near Gibeah.
Gibeath-elohim@1Sa.10.5=H1389G.short: Gibeath-elohim, meaning "Hill of God," was a place near Gibeah where a garrison of Philistines was located (1Sa.10.5).

Gibeon@Jos.9.3-Ezk=H1391.brief: Hivite city that tricked Joshua into a peace treaty.
Gibeon@Jos.9.3-Ezk=H1391.short: Gibeon was a prominent Hivite city that deceived Joshua into making a peace treaty, and later became a Levitical city and site of worship.

Gidom@Jdg.20.45=H1440.brief: A place near Gibeah, associated with the Benjamite War.
Gidom@Jdg.20.45=H1440.short: Gidom was a place near Gibeah where the Benjamites were pursued and defeated during the Benjamite War (Judges 20:45).

Gihon@Gen.2.13-2Ch=H1521.brief: A river of Eden; a spring near Jerusalem.
Gihon@Gen.2.13-2Ch=H1521.short: Gihon refers to both a river of Eden (Genesis 2:13) and a spring near Jerusalem (1Ki.1.33, 38, 45; 2Ch.32.30; 33:14).

Gilboa@1Sa.28.4-2Sa=H1533G.brief: A mountain range where Saul and his sons died.
Gilboa@1Sa.28.4-2Sa=H1533G.short: Mount Gilboa was the site of a battle where Saul and his sons were killed by the Philistines (1Sa.28.4; 2Sa.1.21; 21:12).

Gilboa_Mount@Jdg.7.3-1Ch=H1533H.brief: A mountain range where Saul and his sons died.
Gilboa_Mount@Jdg.7.3-1Ch=H1533H.short: Mount Gilboa was the site where Saul and his sons were killed in battle against the Philistines (1Sa.31.1, 8; 2Sa.1.6; 1Ch.10.1, 8; Judges 7:3).

Gilead@Gen.31.21-Zec=H1568G.brief: Mountainous region east of Jordan; tribal territory and personal name.
Gilead@Gen.31.21-Zec=H1568G.short: Gilead refers to a mountainous region east of the Jordan River, as well as being a personal name for several individuals in the Old Testament.

Gilgal@2Ki.2.1-=H1537H.brief: A place associated with the prophets Elijah and Elisha.
Gilgal@2Ki.2.1-=H1537H.short: Gilgal, a place associated with the prophets Elijah and Elisha, was the starting point of Elijah's final journey and the location of a prophetic community (2Ki.2.1; 4:38).

Gilgal@Deu.11.30-Mic=H1537G.brief: A significant site during Israel's early history in Canaan.
Gilgal@Deu.11.30-Mic=H1537G.short: Gilgal, also known as Geliloth, Beth-gilgal, or Gibeath-haaraloth, was a significant site during Israel's early history in Canaan, serving as a base for Joshua and a place of worship (Deu.11.30; Joshua 4:19-20; 5:3,9-10; 14:6; Judges 2:1; 11:14-15; 15:12-33; Hosea 9:15).

Giloh@Jos.15.51-2Sa=H1542.brief: A city in Judah; home of Ahithophel, David's counselor.
Giloh@Jos.15.51-2Sa=H1542.short: Giloh, also known as Gilo, was a city in Judah and the hometown of Ahithophel, David's counselor who later conspired with Absalom (Joshua 15:51; 2Sa.15.12; 23:34).

Gimzo@2Ch.28.18=H1579.brief: A city in Judah captured by the Philistines.
Gimzo@2Ch.28.18=H1579.short: Gimzo was a city in the plain of Judah that was captured by the Philistines during the reign of Ahaz (2Ch.28.18).

Gittaim@2Sa.4.3-Neh=H1664.brief: Town where Beerothites fled; later inhabited by Benjamites.
Gittaim@2Sa.4.3-Neh=H1664.short: Gittaim was a town where the Beerothites fled and was later inhabited by the Benjamites after the Babylonian exile.

Goah@Jer.31.39=H1601.brief: A place near Jerusalem, mentioned in a prophetic context.
Goah@Jer.31.39=H1601.short: Goah was a place near Jerusalem, mentioned in the context of a prophetic description of the city's future restoration (Jeremiah 31:39).

Gog@Ezk.38.2-Rev=H1463H.brief: A symbolic enemy of God's people in prophetic literature.
Gog@Ezk.38.2-Rev=H1463H.short: Gog is mentioned in the prophetic books of Ezekiel and Revelation as a symbolic enemy of God's people who will be defeated in the end times (Ezk.38.2, 3, 14, 16, 18; 39:1, 11; Revelation 20:8).

Golan@Deu.4.43-1Ch=H1474.brief: A city of refuge in Bashan, allotted to Manasseh.
Golan@Deu.4.43-1Ch=H1474.short: Golan was a city of refuge in Bashan, allotted to the Levites of the family of Gershon and located in the territory of the half-tribe of Manasseh (Deu.4.43; Joshua 20:8; 21:27; 1Ch.6.71).

Golgotha@Mat.27.33-Jhn=G1115.brief: The place where Jesus was crucified, meaning "Place of a Skull."
Golgotha@Mat.27.33-Jhn=G1115.short: Golgotha, also known as the Place of a Skull, was the site outside Jerusalem where Jesus was crucified (Matthew 27:33; Mrk.15.22; Luke 23:33; Jhn.19.17).

Gomorrah@Gen.10.19-Jud=H6017.brief: Wicked city destroyed by God along with Sodom.
Gomorrah@Gen.10.19-Jud=H6017.short: Gomorrah was a wicked city in the plain of Jordan that God destroyed with sulfur and fire, along with Sodom, due to their grave sins.

Goshen@Gen.45.10-Exo=H1657G.brief: A region in Egypt where the Israelites settled and prospered.
Goshen@Gen.45.10-Exo=H1657G.short: Goshen was the region in Egypt where Jacob and his family settled during the time of Joseph, and where the Israelites lived and prospered until the Exodus (Genesis 45:10; 46:28-29, 34; 47:1, 4, 6, 27; 50:8; Exodus 8:22; 9:26).

Goshen@Jos.10.41-=H1657H.brief: A town and region in the hill country of Judah.
Goshen@Jos.10.41-=H1657H.short: Goshen was a town and region in the hill country of Judah, mentioned in the accounts of Joshua's conquests (Joshua 10:41; 11:16; 15:51).

Gozan@2Ki.17.6-Isa=H1470.brief: A region in Mesopotamia where Israelite captives were deported.
Gozan@2Ki.17.6-Isa=H1470.short: Gozan was a region in Mesopotamia where Israelite captives from the northern kingdom were deported by the Assyrians (2Ki.17.6; 18:11; 19:12; 1Ch.5.26; Isaiah 37:12).

Great_Sea@Exo.23.31-Ezk=H1419J.brief: The Mediterranean Sea, the western boundary of the Promised Land.
Great_Sea@Exo.23.31-Ezk=H1419J.short: The Great Sea, also known as the Sea of the Philistines, refers to the Mediterranean Sea, which formed the western boundary of the Promised Land (Numbers 34:6-7; Joshua 1:4; 9:1; 15:12, 47; 23:4; Ezk.47.10, 15, 19-20; 48:28; Exodus 23:31).

Greece@Isa.66.19-Act=H3120H.brief: A nation and culture, often in opposition to Israel
Greece@Isa.66.19-Act=H3120H.short: Greece (Javan), a nation and culture mentioned in both the Old and New Testaments.

Guard_Gate@Neh.12.39=H4307G.brief: A gate in Jerusalem's wall, likely the Muster Gate.
Guard_Gate@Neh.12.39=H4307G.short: The Guard Gate was a gate in Jerusalem's wall, mentioned in Nehemiah 12:39, likely the same as the Muster Gate near the Temple.

Gur@2Ki.9.27=H1483.brief: A place near Ibleam where Ahaziah was wounded.
Gur@2Ki.9.27=H1483.short: Gur was a place near Ibleam where Ahaziah, king of Judah, was wounded by Jehu's men while fleeing (2Ki.9.27).

Gurbaal@2Ch.26.7=H1485.brief: A place inhabited by Arabians, attacked by Uzziah's army.
Gurbaal@2Ch.26.7=H1485.short: Gurbaal was a place inhabited by Arabians, against whom Uzziah, king of Judah, waged war and prevailed (2Ch.26.7).

Habor@2Ki.17.6-1Ch=H2249.brief: A river in Assyria where Israelite captives were settled.
Habor@2Ki.17.6-1Ch=H2249.short: Habor was a river in Assyria along which the Israelite captives from the northern kingdom were settled by the Assyrians (2Ki.17.6; 18:11; 1Ch.5.26).

Hachilah@1Sa.23.19-=H2444.brief: A hill in the Wilderness of Ziph, near David's hideout.
Hachilah@1Sa.23.19-=H2444.short: Hachilah was a hill in the Wilderness of Ziph, where David hid from Saul and where the Ziphites revealed David's location to Saul (1Sa.23.19; 26:1, 3).

Hadad-rimmon@Zec.12.11=H1910.brief: A place near Megiddo associated with mourning for Josiah.
Hadad-rimmon@Zec.12.11=H1910.short: Hadad-rimmon was a place near Megiddo where a great lamentation was held for King Josiah, who was mortally wounded there.

Hadashah@Jos.15.37=H2322.brief: A town in the Shephelah region of Judah.
Hadashah@Jos.15.37=H2322.short: Hadashah was a town allotted to the tribe of Judah, located in the Shephelah region (Joshua 15:37).

Hadid@Ezr.2.33-Neh=H2307.brief: A town in Benjamin, resettled after the Babylonian exile.
Hadid@Ezr.2.33-Neh=H2307.short: Hadid was a town in Benjamin, whose inhabitants returned from the Babylonian exile and resettled in the town (Ezra 2:33; Nehemiah 7:37; 11:34).

Hadrach@Zec.9.1=H2317.brief: A region mentioned in a prophetic oracle of judgment.
Hadrach@Zec.9.1=H2317.short: Hadrach was a region mentioned in a prophetic oracle of judgment, possibly located in Syria (Zechariah 9:1).

Haeleph@Jos.18.28=H0507.brief: A town allotted to the tribe of Benjamin.
Haeleph@Jos.18.28=H0507.short: Haeleph was a town allotted to the tribe of Benjamin (Joshua 18:28).

Halah@2Ki.17.6-1Ch=H2477.brief: A place where Israelites were exiled by the Assyrians.
Halah@2Ki.17.6-1Ch=H2477.short: Halah was one of the places where the Assyrians settled the exiled Israelites after conquering the Northern Kingdom.

Halak_Mount@Jos.11.17-=H2510.brief: A mountain marking the southern boundary of Joshua's conquests.
Halak_Mount@Jos.11.17-=H2510.short: Mount Halak was a mountain that marked the southern boundary of the territory conquered by Joshua (Joshua 11:17; 12:7).

Halhul@Jos.15.58=H2478.brief: A town in the hill country of Judah.
Halhul@Jos.15.58=H2478.short: Halhul was a town allotted to the tribe of Judah, located in the hill country (Joshua 15:58).

Hali@Jos.19.25=H2482.brief: A town allotted to the tribe of Asher.
Hali@Jos.19.25=H2482.short: Hali was a town allotted to the tribe of Asher (Joshua 19:25).

Hall_of_Judgment@1Ki.7.7=H0197H.brief: A hall in Solomon's palace where he administered justice.
Hall_of_Judgment@1Ki.7.7=H0197H.short: The Hall of Judgment was a hall in Solomon's palace where he sat to judge and administer justice (1Ki.7.7).

Hall_of_Pillars@1Ki.7.6=H0197G.brief: A porch with pillars in Solomon's palace.
Hall_of_Pillars@1Ki.7.6=H0197G.short: The Hall of Pillars was a porch in Solomon's palace, measuring fifty cubits long and thirty cubits wide, with a portico of pillars and a canopy.

Hall_of_the_Throne@1Ki.7.7=H0197I.brief: Another name for the Hall of Judgment in Solomon's palace.
Hall_of_the_Throne@1Ki.7.7=H0197I.short: The Hall of the Throne was another name for the Hall of Judgment in Solomon's palace, where he sat to administer justice (1Ki.7.7).

Ham@Gen.14.5=H1990.brief: A place where Chedorlaomer defeated the Zuzim in battle.
Ham@Gen.14.5=H1990.short: Ham was a place where Chedorlaomer and his allies defeated the Zuzim in battle during the war of the kings (Genesis 14:5).

Hamath@Num.13.21-Zec=H2574G.brief: A major city and kingdom in Syria, often mentioned in the Bible.
Hamath@Num.13.21-Zec=H2574G.short: Hamath, also known as Hamath Rabbah or Lebo-hamath, was a significant city and kingdom in Syria, frequently mentioned in the Bible as a reference point for the northern border of Israel and in the context of political and military events (Num.13:21; Judges 3:3; 2Ki.14.25, 28; Jeremiah 39:5; 49:23; 52:9, 27).

Hammath@Jos.19.28-1Ch=H2575A.brief: A fortified city and Levitical town in Naphtali.
Hammath@Jos.19.28-1Ch=H2575A.short: Hammath, also known as Hammoth-dor or Hammon, was a fortified city in Naphtali allotted to the Levites (Joshua 19:35; 21:32; 19:28; 1Ch.6.76).

Hamonah@Ezk.39.16=H1997.brief: A city in Ezekiel's vision, meaning "multitude" or "horde."
Hamonah@Ezk.39.16=H1997.short: Hamonah is a city mentioned in Ezekiel's vision (Ezk.39.16), its name meaning "multitude" or "horde," likely referring to the burial place of Gog's army.

Hamon-gog_Valley@Ezk.39.11-=H1996.brief: A valley where Gog and his army will be buried.
Hamon-gog_Valley@Ezk.39.11-=H1996.short: The Valley of Hamon-gog is the place where Gog and his army will be buried after their defeat, as prophesied by Ezekiel (Ezk.39.11, 15).

Hanes@Isa.30.4=H2609.brief: An Egyptian city mentioned in a prophecy against Judah.
Hanes@Isa.30.4=H2609.short: Hanes was an Egyptian city to which Judah sent envoys, as mentioned in a prophecy by Isaiah (Isaiah 30:4).

Hannathon@Jos.19.14=H2615.brief: A border town in the territory of Zebulun.
Hannathon@Jos.19.14=H2615.short: Hannathon was a border town in the territory allotted to the tribe of Zebulun (Joshua 19:14).

Hara@1Ch.5.26=H2024.brief: A place where Israelite tribes were exiled by Tiglath-pileser.
Hara@1Ch.5.26=H2024.short: Hara was a place, possibly in Media, where the Reubenites, Gadites, and half-tribe of Manasseh were exiled by Tiglath-pileser, king of Assyria (1Ch.5.26).

Haradah@Num.33.24-=H2732.brief: A desert campsite during Israel's journey from Egypt.
Haradah@Num.33.24-=H2732.short: Haradah was one of the places where the Israelites camped during their journey through the wilderness after leaving Egypt.

Haran@Gen.11.31-Act=H2771A.brief: A city in Mesopotamia, associated with Abraham and his family.
Haran@Gen.11.31-Act=H2771A.short: Haran was a city in Mesopotamia where Abraham and his family settled after leaving Ur, and from where Abraham later departed for Canaan (Genesis 11:31-32; 12:4-5; 27:43; 28:10; 29:4; Act.7.2, 4).

Harmon@Amo.4.3=H2038.brief: A place mentioned in Amos's prophecy against Israel.
Harmon@Amo.4.3=H2038.short: Harmon is a place mentioned in Amos's prophecy, possibly referring to the destination of the exiled Israelites (Amo.4.3).

Harod@Jdg.7.1-1Ch=H5878.brief: A spring near where Gideon gathered his army.
Harod@Jdg.7.1-1Ch=H5878.short: Harod was a spring near the hill of Moreh, where Gideon gathered his army before battling the Midianites (Judges 7:1).

Harosheth-hagoyim@Jdg.4.2-=H2800.short: Harosheth-hagoyim was a Canaanite city that served as the base for Sisera, the commander of King Jabin's army (Judg 4:2).

Hashmonah@Num.33.29-=H2832.brief: A desert campsite during Israel's journey from Egypt.
Hashmonah@Num.33.29-=H2832.short: Hashmonah was one of the places where the Israelites camped during their wilderness wanderings after leaving Egypt.

Hauran@Ezk.47.16-=H2362.brief: Region east of the Sea of Galilee
Hauran@Ezk.47.16-=H2362.short: Hauran was a fertile region located east of the Sea of Galilee, mentioned as part of Israel's future boundaries (Ezk.47.16,18).

Havilah@Gen.2.11=H2341G.brief: Land near Eden with gold, bdellium, and onyx
Havilah@Gen.2.11=H2341G.short: Havilah was a land mentioned in the description of Eden, known for its pure gold, aromatic resin (bdellium), and onyx stone (Gen.2.11-12).

Havilah@Gen.25.18-1Sa=H2341J.brief: Region inhabited by Ishmaelites, raided by Saul
Havilah@Gen.25.18-1Sa=H2341J.short: Havilah was a region inhabited by the descendants of Ishmael (Gen.25.18), which was later raided by King Saul during his campaign against the Amalekites (1Sa.15.7).

Havvoth-jair@Num.32.41-1Ch=H2334.brief: Villages in Gilead captured by Jair
Havvoth-jair@Num.32.41-1Ch=H2334.short: Havvoth-jair were villages in Gilead captured by Jair, a leader from the tribe of Manasseh, during the Israelite conquest of the region (Num.32.41; Deut 3:14; Judg 10:4; 1Ch.2.23).

Hazar-addar@Num.34.4=H2692.brief: A town on the southern border of Canaan.
Hazar-addar@Num.34.4=H2692.short: Hazar-addar was a town on the southern border of Canaan, mentioned in the description of the land's boundaries.

Hazar-enan@Num.34.9-Ezk=H2704.brief: Town on the northern border of Israel
Hazar-enan@Num.34.9-Ezk=H2704.short: Hazar-enan was a town located on the northern border of the Promised Land (Num.34.9-10) and the future inheritance of the tribe of Dan (Ezk.48.1).

Hazar-gaddah@Jos.15.27=H2693.brief: Town allotted to the tribe of Judah
Hazar-gaddah@Jos.15.27=H2693.short: Hazar-gaddah was a town in the Negev region, allotted to the tribe of Judah during the division of the Promised Land (Josh 15:27).

Hazar-shual@Jos.15.28-Neh=H2705.brief: Town allotted to Judah and Simeon
Hazar-shual@Jos.15.28-Neh=H2705.short: Hazar-shual was a town in the Negev allotted to Judah (Josh 15:28), later given to the tribe of Simeon (Josh 19:3; 1Ch.4.28), and inhabited by Jews after the Babylonian exile (Neh.11.27).

Hazar-susah@Jos.19.5=H2701.brief: Town allotted to the tribe of Simeon
Hazar-susah@Jos.19.5=H2701.short: Hazar-susah was a town in the Negev region, allotted to the tribe of Simeon during the division of the Promised Land (Josh 19:5).

Hazar-susim@1Ch.4.31=H2702.brief: A town allotted to the tribe of Simeon.
Hazar-susim@1Ch.4.31=H2702.short: Hazar-susim was a town allotted to the tribe of Simeon, mentioned in the list of their cities in 1 Chronicles.

Hazer-hatticon@Ezk.47.16=H2694.brief: Place on the ideal border of Israel
Hazer-hatticon@Ezk.47.16=H2694.short: Hazer-hatticon, meaning "the middle village," was a place named on the ideal border of Israel in Ezekiel's vision (Ezk.47.16), likely identical to Hazar-enan.

Hazerim@Deu.2.23=H2699.short: Hazerim, meaning "villages," refers to the settlements inhabited by the Avvim, a people group dispossessed by the Caphtorim (Deut 2:23).

Hazeroth@Num.11.35-Deu=H2698.brief: Israelite encampment during the wilderness wanderings
Hazeroth@Num.11.35-Deu=H2698.short: Hazeroth was one of the places where the Israelites camped during their wilderness wanderings, mentioned in the context of Moses' leadership challenges (Num.11.35; 12:16; 33:17-18; Deut 1:1).

Hazor@Jer.49.28-=H2674K.brief: Region in Arabia, possibly Ituraea, threatened by Nebuchadnezzar
Hazor@Jer.49.28-=H2674K.short: Hazor refers to a region in Arabia, possibly Ituraea, against which Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, launched a military campaign (Jer.49.28,30,33).

Hazor@Jos.11.1-2Ki=H2674G.brief: Major Canaanite city conquered by Joshua
Hazor@Jos.11.1-2Ki=H2674G.short: Hazor was a major Canaanite city, whose king Jabin led a coalition against Israel; it was captured and destroyed by Joshua (Josh 11:1,10-11,13), later oppressing Israel before being defeated by Deborah and Barak (Judg 4:2,17).

Hazor@Jos.15.23=H2674H.brief: A town in the southland of Judah.
Hazor@Jos.15.23=H2674H.short: Hazor was a town allotted to the tribe of Judah in the Negev region.

Hazor@Jos.15.25=H2674I.brief: Town in the Negev region of Judah
Hazor@Jos.15.25=H2674I.short: Hazor was a town in the Negev region, part of the territory allotted to the tribe of Judah (Josh 15:23).

Hazor@Neh.11.33=H2674J.brief: Town resettled by Benjamites after the Babylonian exile
Hazor@Neh.11.33=H2674J.short: Hazor was a town resettled by the Benjamites after their return from the Babylonian exile (Neh.11.33).

Hazor-hadattah@Jos.15.25=H2675.brief: Town in the Negev region of Judah
Hazor-hadattah@Jos.15.25=H2675.short: Hazor-hadattah, meaning "New Hazor," was a town in the Negev region, part of the territory allotted to the tribe of Judah (Josh 15:25).

Hebron@Gen.13.18-Neh=H2275A.brief: An important city in Judah; burial place of patriarchs.
Hebron@Gen.13.18-Neh=H2275A.short: Hebron, also known as Kiriath-arba, was a significant city in Judah, associated with the patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and later became a Levitical city and a city of refuge.

Hebron_Valley@Gen.37.14=H2275H.brief: Valley near Hebron where Joseph sought his brothers
Hebron_Valley@Gen.37.14=H2275H.short: The Hebron Valley was the location where Joseph was sent by his father, Jacob, to check on his brothers who were pasturing their flocks near Shechem (Gen.37.14).

Helam@2Sa.10.16-=H2431.brief: Place where David defeated the Arameans
Helam@2Sa.10.16-=H2431.short: Helam was the location of a battle between David's forces and the Arameans, where David defeated Hadadezer, king of Zobah, and his allies (2Sa.10.16-17).

Helbah@Jdg.1.31=H2462.brief: Canaanite town not conquered by the tribe of Asher
Helbah@Jdg.1.31=H2462.short: Helbah was a Canaanite town that the tribe of Asher failed to conquer during the period of the judges (Judg 1:31).

Helbon@Ezk.27.18=H2463.brief: City known for its fine wine
Helbon@Ezk.27.18=H2463.short: Helbon was a city mentioned in Ezk.27.18 as a trading partner of Tyre, known for its fine wine.

Helech@Ezk.27.11=H2428B.brief: A place or people mentioned in Ezekiel's prophecy.
Helech@Ezk.27.11=H2428B.short: Helech was either a place, possibly in Cilicia, or a term referring to the army of Tyre, mentioned in Ezekiel's prophecy against Tyre.

Heleph@Jos.19.33=H2501.short: Heleph was a town marking the border of the territory allocated to the tribe of Naphtali (Josh 19:33).

Helkath@Jos.19.25-1Ch=H2520.brief: Levitical city in the territory of Asher
Helkath@Jos.19.25-1Ch=H2520.short: Helkath (or Hukok) was a city allocated to the Levites within the territory of the tribe of Asher (Josh 19:25; 21:31; 1Ch.6.75).

Helkath-hazzurim@2Sa.2.16=H2521.brief: Site of a battle between David's and Ish-bosheth's men
Helkath-hazzurim@2Sa.2.16=H2521.short: Helkath-hazzurim, meaning "Field of Swords," was the site of a battle between David's men and those of Ish-bosheth, resulting in Abner's defeat (2Sa.2.16).

Hena@2Ki.18.34-Isa=H2012.short: Hena was a Mesopotamian city conquered by the Assyrians before the time of Sennacherib, possibly located near Sippara (2Ki.18.34; 19:13; Isa.37.13).

Hepher@Jos.12.17-1Ki=H2660B.brief: A Canaanite city conquered by Joshua; later a Solomonic district.
Hepher@Jos.12.17-1Ki=H2660B.short: Hepher was a Canaanite city conquered by Joshua and later became part of a district under Solomon's rule.

Heres@Jdg.8.13=H2776G.brief: Place near where Gideon defeated the Midianites
Heres@Jdg.8.13=H2776G.short: Heres was a place near the site where Gideon and his men defeated the Midianites (Judg 8:13).

Hereth@1Sa.22.5=H2802.brief: Forest where David hid from Saul
Hereth@1Sa.22.5=H2802.short: The forest of Hereth was where David sought refuge when fleeing from King Saul (1Sa.22.5).

Hermon_Mount@Deu.3.8-Ezk=H2768.brief: Mountain on the northern border of Israel
Hermon_Mount@Deu.3.8-Ezk=H2768.short: Mount Hermon, also known as Baal-hermon, Baal-hamon, Baal-gad, Senir, or Sirion, was a prominent mountain on the northern border of Israel (Deut 3:8-9; 4:48; Josh 11:3,17; 12:1,5,7; 13:5,11; 1Ch.5.23; Psa.29.6; 42:6; 89:12; 133:3; Sng.4.8; 8:11; Jer.18.14; Ezk.27.5).

Heshbon@Num.21.25-Jer=H2809.brief: Amorite city conquered by Moses, allotted to Reuben
Heshbon@Num.21.25-Jer=H2809.short: Heshbon, an Amorite city conquered by Moses (Num.21.25-30), was allotted to Reuben (Num.32.37; Josh 13:17) but later given to the Levites (Josh 21:39); it was a significant city in the region (Isa.15.4; 16:8-9; Jer.48.2, 34, 45; 49:3).

Heshmon@Jos.15.27=H2829.brief: A town in the southland of Judah.
Heshmon@Jos.15.27=H2829.short: Heshmon was a town allotted to the tribe of Judah in the Negev region.

Hethlon@Ezk.47.15-=H2855.brief: Place on the northern border of Israel
Hethlon@Ezk.47.15-=H2855.short: Hethlon was a place on the northern border of Israel, mentioned in Ezekiel's vision of the restored land (Ezk.47.15; 48:1).

Hierapolis@Col.4.13=G2404.brief: City in Phrygia, home to a Christian community
Hierapolis@Col.4.13=G2404.short: Hierapolis, a city in Phrygia, was home to a Christian community mentioned by Paul in his letter to the Colossians (Col.4.13).

Hobah@Gen.14.15=H2327.brief: Place north of Damascus pursued by Abraham
Hobah@Gen.14.15=H2327.short: Hobah was a place north of Damascus where Abraham pursued the defeated army of Chedorlaomer after rescuing Lot (Gen.14.15).

Holon@Jer.48.21=H2473H.short: Holon, a city of Moab mentioned in Jeremiah's oracle against Moab.

Holon@Jos.15.51-1Ch=H2473G.brief: Levitical city in the hill country of Judah
Holon@Jos.15.51-1Ch=H2473G.short: Holon, a Levitical city in Judah's hill country, also called Hilen.

Holy_Place@Exo.26.33-Heb=H6944J.brief: The inner sanctuary of the Tabernacle and Temple
Holy_Place@Exo.26.33-Heb=H6944J.short: The Holy Place was the inner sanctuary of the Tabernacle and Temple.

Hor_Mount@Num.20.22-Deu=H2023G.brief: Mountain where Aaron died and was buried
Hor_Mount@Num.20.22-Deu=H2023G.short: Mount Hor, where Aaron died and was buried during Israel's wilderness journey.

Hor_Mount@Num.34.7-=H2023H.brief: A mountain marking Israel's northern boundary
Hor_Mount@Num.34.7-=H2023H.short: Mount Hor, a mountain at the northern extent of Israel's inheritance.

Horem@Jos.19.38=H2765.short: Horem, a fortified city in the territory of Naphtali (Joshua 19:38).

Horesh@1Sa.23.15-=H2793G.brief: A wilderness area where David hid from Saul
Horesh@1Sa.23.15-=H2793G.short: Horesh, a wilderness area in Judah where David hid from Saul.

Hor-haggidgad@Num.33.32-Deu=H2735.brief: An Israelite campsite during the wilderness wanderings
Hor-haggidgad@Num.33.32-Deu=H2735.short: Hor-haggidgad (Gudgodah), an Israelite campsite between Bene-jaakan and Jotbathah.

Horonaim@2Sa.13.34-Jer=H2773.brief: A Moabite city mentioned in prophecies of judgment
Horonaim@2Sa.13.34-Jer=H2773.short: Horonaim, a Moabite city featured in prophecies against Moab.

Horse_Gate@Neh.3.28-Jer=H5483B.brief: A gate in Jerusalem's wall near the temple
Horse_Gate@Neh.3.28-Jer=H5483B.short: The Horse Gate, a gate in Jerusalem's wall near the temple.

Hosah@Jos.19.29=H2621G.short: Hosah, a Levitical city on the border of Asher (Joshua 19:29).

House_of_the_Forest@1Ki.7.2-Isa=H1004K.brief: A building in Solomon's palace complex
House_of_the_Forest@1Ki.7.2-Isa=H1004K.short: The House of the Forest of Lebanon, a building in Solomon's palace.

Hukkok@Jos.19.34=H2712A.brief: A town on the border of Naphtali
Hukkok@Jos.19.34=H2712A.short: Hukkok, a town on the border of Naphtali (Joshua 19:34).

Humtah@Jos.15.54=H2547.brief: A town in the hill country of Judah
Humtah@Jos.15.54=H2547.short: Humtah, a town in the hill country of Judah (Joshua 15:54).

Ibleam@Jos.17.11-1Ch=H2991.short: Ibleam (Bileam, Gath-rimmon), a Levitical city in Issachar.

Iconium@Act.13.51-2Ti=G2430.brief: A city in Asia Minor visited by Paul
Iconium@Act.13.51-2Ti=G2430.short: Iconium, a city in Asia Minor where Paul preached the gospel.

Idalah@Jos.19.15=H3030.short: Idalah, a town in the territory of Zebulun (Joshua 19:15).

Idumea@Mrk.3.8=G2401.short: Idumea, a region south of Judea, inhabited by Edomites.

Iim@Jos.15.29=H5864H.brief: A town in the Negev of Judah
Iim@Jos.15.29=H5864H.short: Iim, a town in the Negev region of Judah (Joshua 15:29).

Ijon@2Sa.24.6-2Ch=H5859.brief: A town in northern Israel conquered by Assyria
Ijon@2Sa.24.6-2Ch=H5859.short: Ijon (Jaan), a town in northern Israel conquered by the Assyrians.

Illyricum@Rom.15.19=G2437.brief: A region where Paul preached the gospel
Illyricum@Rom.15.19=G2437.short: Illyricum, a region where Paul preached the gospel (Romans 15:19).

Immer@Ezr.2.59-Neh=H0564I.brief: A place from which exiles returned to Jerusalem
Immer@Ezr.2.59-Neh=H0564I.short: Immer, a place from which exiles returned to Jerusalem (Ezra 2:59; Nehemiah 7:61).

India@Est.1.1-=H1912.brief: The eastern extent of Ahasuerus' Persian Empire

Lod@1Ch.8.12-Act=H3850.brief: A city in Benjamin; home of Aeneas healed by Peter
Lod@1Ch.8.12-Act=H3850.short: Lod (Lydda), a city in the territory of Benjamin (1Ch.8.12), where Peter healed Aeneas (Act.9.32-35).

Lo-debar@Jos.13.26-Amo=H3810.brief: A town in Gilead; home of Mephibosheth
Lo-debar@Jos.13.26-Amo=H3810.short: Lo-debar (Debir), a town in Gilead where Mephibosheth, Jonathan's son, lived (2Sa.9.4-5).

Luhith@Isa.15.5-Jer=H3872.short: Luhith, a place in Moab mentioned in prophecies of Isaiah and Jeremiah (Isaiah 15:5; Jeremiah 48:5).

Luz@Jdg.1.26=H3870G.brief: A Canaanite city; a man built another city named Luz
Luz@Jdg.1.26=H3870G.short: Luz, a Canaanite city that was destroyed, and another city built by a man who had betrayed the first Luz (Judges 1:26).

Lycaonia@Act.14.6-=G3071.brief: A region in Asia Minor; Paul and Barnabas preached there
Lycaonia@Act.14.6-=G3071.short: Lycaonia, a region in Asia Minor where Paul and Barnabas preached the gospel (Act.14.6, 11).

Lycia@Act.27.5=G3073.brief: A region on the southwest coast of Asia Minor
Lycia@Act.27.5=G3073.short: Lycia, a region on the southwest coast of Asia Minor, passed by Paul on his journey to Rome (Act.27.5).

Lystra@Act.14.6-2Ti=G3082.brief: A city in Lycaonia; Paul and Barnabas preached there
Lystra@Act.14.6-2Ti=G3082.short: Lystra, a city in Lycaonia where Paul and Barnabas preached and Paul healed a lame man (Act.14.6-21).

Maacah@Deu.3.14-1Ch=H4601R.short: Maacah (Maacath), a region near Geshur (Deu.3.14; Joshua 12:5).

Maarath@Jos.15.59=H4638.brief: A town in the hill country of Judah
Maarath@Jos.15.59=H4638.short: Maarath, a town in the hill country of Judah (Joshua 15:59).

Maareh-geba@Jdg.20.33=H4629G.brief: A place near Gibeah where an ambush was set
Maareh-geba@Jdg.20.33=H4629G.short: Maareh-geba, a place near Gibeah where the Israelites set an ambush against the Benjamites (Judges 20:33).

Macedonia@Act.16.9-Tit=G3109.brief: A region in northern Greece; Paul preached there
Macedonia@Act.16.9-Tit=G3109.short: Macedonia, a region in northern Greece where Paul preached the gospel and established churches (Act.16.9-12; 20:1-3).

Machpelah@Gen.23.9-=H4375.brief: A cave near Hebron; burial place of patriarchs
Machpelah@Gen.23.9-=H4375.short: Machpelah, a cave near Hebron purchased by Abraham as a burial place for Sarah and later used for other patriarchs (Genesis 23:9, 17-19).

Madmannah@Jos.15.31-1Ch=H4089G.brief: A town in the Negev of Judah
Madmannah@Jos.15.31-1Ch=H4089G.short: Madmannah (Beth-marcaboth), a town in the Negev region of Judah (Joshua 15:31; 19:5; 1Ch.4.31).

Madmen@Jer.48.2=H4086.brief: A place in Moab threatened with destruction
Madmen@Jer.48.2=H4086.short: Madmen, a place in Moab against which Jeremiah prophesied destruction (Jeremiah 48:2).

Madmenah@Isa.10.31=H4088.short: Madmenah, a place near Jerusalem mentioned in Isaiah's prophecy (Isaiah 10:31).

Madon@Jos.11.1-=H4068.brief: A Canaanite city conquered by Joshua
Madon@Jos.11.1-=H4068.short: Madon, a Canaanite city whose king joined a coalition against Joshua but was defeated (Joshua 11:1; 12:19).

Magadan@Mat.15.39-Jhn=G3093.brief: A place on the Sea of Galilee; home of Mary Magdalene
Magadan@Mat.15.39-Jhn=G3093.short: Magadan (Dalmanutha), a place on the shore of the Sea of Galilee visited by Jesus (Matthew 15:39; Mrk.8.10), possibly the hometown of Mary Magdalene (Matthew 27:56, 61; 28:1; Mrk.15.40, 47; 16:1, 9; Luke 8:2; 24:10; Jhn.19.25; 20:1, 18).

Magbish@Ezr.2.30=H4019.brief: A place whose people returned from Babylonian exile
Magbish@Ezr.2.30=H4019.short: Magbish, a place whose people are listed among those who returned to Judah from Babylonian exile (Ezra 2:30).

Magog@Ezk.38.2-Rev=H4031H.brief: A nation that will attack Israel in the future
Magog@Ezk.38.2-Rev=H4031H.short: Magog, a nation that will join forces with Gog to attack Israel in the future, as prophesied in Ezekiel and Revelation (Ezk.38.2; 39:6; Revelation 20:8).

Mahanaim@Gen.32.2-1Ch=H4266.brief: A place east of the Jordan; David's refuge
Mahanaim@Gen.32.2-1Ch=H4266.short: Mahanaim, a place east of the Jordan River where Jacob met angels and David found refuge during Absalom's rebellion (Genesis 32:2; 2Sa.17.24, 27).

Mahaneh-dan@Jdg.13.25-=H4265.brief: A place between Zorah and Eshtaol; Samson's birthplace
Mahaneh-dan@Jdg.13.25-=H4265.short: Mahaneh-dan, a place between Zorah and Eshtaol where the Spirit of the Lord began to stir Samson (Judges 13:25; 18:12).

Makaz@1Ki.4.9=H4739.brief: A place in one of Solomon's administrative districts
Makaz@1Ki.4.9=H4739.short: Makaz, a place in one of the twelve administrative districts established by Solomon (1Ki.4.9).

Makheloth@Num.33.25-=H4722.brief: A place where the Israelites camped in the wilderness
Makheloth@Num.33.25-=H4722.short: Makheloth, a place where the Israelites camped during their wilderness journey (Numbers 33:25-26).

Makkedah@Jos.10.10-=H4719.brief: A Canaanite city conquered by Joshua
Makkedah@Jos.10.10-=H4719.short: Makkedah, a Canaanite city where Joshua defeated and executed five Amorite kings who had hidden in a cave (Joshua 10:16-28).

Malta@Act.28.1=G3194.brief: An island where Paul was shipwrecked
Malta@Act.28.1=G3194.short: Malta, an island in the Mediterranean Sea where Paul was shipwrecked on his journey to Rome (Act.28.1).

Mamre@Gen.13.18-=H4471G.brief: A place near Hebron; associated with Abraham
Mamre@Gen.13.18-=H4471G.short: Mamre, a place near Hebron where Abraham lived and built an altar to the Lord (Genesis 13:18; 18:1).

Manahath@Jdg.20.43-1Ch=H4506A.brief: A place where Benjamites lived after the exile
Manahath@Jdg.20.43-1Ch=H4506A.short: Manahath (Nohah), a place where some Benjamites lived after returning from the Babylonian exile (1Ch.8.6).

Maon@Jos.15.55-1Sa=H4584G.brief: A city in Judah; home of Nabal and Abigail
Maon@Jos.15.55-1Sa=H4584G.short: Maon, a city in the hill country of Judah (Joshua 15:55), home of Nabal and Abigail (1Sa.25.2).

Marah@Exo.15.23-Num=H4785.brief: A place with bitter water on the Exodus route
Marah@Exo.15.23-Num=H4785.short: Marah, a place where the Israelites found bitter water that Moses made drinkable by casting a tree into it (Exodus 15:23-25; Numbers 33:8-9).

Mareal@Jos.19.11=H4831.brief: A place on the border of Zebulun
Mareal@Jos.19.11=H4831.short: Mareal, a place mentioned in describing the border of the territory of Zebulun (Joshua 19:11).

Mareshah@Jos.15.44-Mic=H4762G.brief: A town in Judah; fortified by Rehoboam
Mareshah@Jos.15.44-Mic=H4762G.short: Mareshah, a town in the Shephelah of Judah (Joshua 15:44), fortified by Rehoboam (2Ch.11.8) and the site of Asa's victory over Zerah the Ethiopian (2Ch.14.9-10).

Maroth@Mic.1.12=H4796.short: Maroth, a town in Judah mentioned in Micah's prophecy (Micah 1:12).

Masrekah@Gen.36.36-1Ch=H4957.brief: The royal city of Samlah, an Edomite king
Masrekah@Gen.36.36-1Ch=H4957.short: Masrekah, the royal city of Samlah, one of the ancient kings of Edom before any Israelite king reigned (Genesis 36:36; 1Ch.1.47).

Massah@Exo.17.7-Psa=H4532.brief: A place where the Israelites tested God
Massah@Exo.17.7-Psa=H4532.short: Massah, a place in the wilderness where the Israelites tested the Lord by demanding water (Exodus 17:7; Deu.6.16; 9:22; 33:8; Psalm 95:8).

Mattanah@Num.21.18-=H4980.brief: A place where the Israelites camped during their wilderness journey
Mattanah@Num.21.18-=H4980.short: Mattanah, a place where the Israelites camped during their journey through the wilderness (Numbers 21:18-19).

Mearah@Jos.13.4=H4632.short: Mearah, a place near Sidon, mentioned in the description of the land yet to be conquered by the Israelites (Joshua 13:4).

Meconah@Neh.11.28=H4368.brief: A town inhabited by the people of Judah after the exile
Meconah@Neh.11.28=H4368.short: Meconah, a town inhabited by the people of Judah after their return from the Babylonian exile (Nehemiah 11:28).

Medeba@Num.21.30-Isa=H4311.brief: A Moabite city captured by the Israelites
Medeba@Num.21.30-Isa=H4311.short: Medeba, a city in Moab captured by the Israelites (Numbers 21:30; Joshua 13:9, 16), later a site of battle between the Ammonites and David's army (1Ch.19.7).

Media@2Ki.17.6-Act=H4074H.brief: An ancient kingdom; part of the Persian Empire
Media@2Ki.17.6-Act=H4074H.short: Media (Medes), an ancient kingdom in western Iran that, along with Persia, conquered Babylon and formed the Persian Empire (2Ki.17.6; 18:11; Esther 1:3, 14, 18; 10:2; Isaiah 21:2; Jeremiah 25:25; Dan.8.20).

Megiddo@Jos.12.21-Rev=H4023.brief: A strategic city in the Jezreel Valley
Megiddo@Jos.12.21-Rev=H4023.short: Megiddo, a strategically important city in the Jezreel Valley (Joshua 12:21; 17:11; Judges 1:27; 5:19), fortified by Solomon (1Ki.9.15), and the site of King Josiah's death (2Ki.23.29-30; 2Ch.35.22).

Me-jarkon@Jos.19.46=H4313.brief: A place in the territory of Dan
Me-jarkon@Jos.19.46=H4313.short: Me-jarkon, a place in the territory allotted to the tribe of Dan (Joshua 19:46).

Memphis@Isa.19.13-Hos=H5297.brief: An important city in ancient Egypt
Memphis@Isa.19.13-Hos=H5297.short: Memphis, an ancient Egyptian city mentioned in prophecies of judgment against Egypt (Isaiah 19:13; Jeremiah 2:16; 44:1; 46:14, 19; Ezk.30.13, 16; Hosea 9:6).

Mephaath@Jos.13.18-Jer=H4158.brief: A Levitical city in Reuben, later Moabite
Mephaath@Jos.13.18-Jer=H4158.short: Mephaath, a Levitical city in the territory of Reuben (Joshua 13:18; 21:37; 1Ch.6.79), later mentioned in a prophecy against Moab (Jeremiah 48:21).

Meribah@Exo.17.7-Psa=H4809G.brief: A place where the Israelites quarreled with Moses
Meribah@Exo.17.7-Psa=H4809G.short: Meribah, a place where the Israelites quarreled with Moses and tested the Lord, and where water came from the rock (Exodus 17:7; Deu.33.8; Psalm 95:8).

Meribah@Num.20.13-Ezk=H4809H.brief: A place where Moses disobeyed God
Meribah@Num.20.13-Ezk=H4809H.short: Meribah-kadesh, a place where Moses disobeyed God by striking the rock to bring forth water (Numbers 20:13, 24; 27:14; Deu.32.51; Psalm 81:7; 106:32; Ezk.47.19; 48:28).

Merom@Jos.11.5-=H4792.brief: A place where Joshua defeated Jabin's coalition
Merom@Jos.11.5-=H4792.short: Merom, a place near the waters of Merom where Joshua defeated a coalition of Canaanite kings led by Jabin king of Hazor (Joshua 11:5, 7).

Meronothites@1Ch.27.30-Neh=H4824.brief: A term used to describe two individuals in the Bible
Meronothites@1Ch.27.30-Neh=H4824.short: Meronothite, a term used to describe Jehdeiah, who was in charge of King David's donkeys (1Ch.27.30), and Jadon, who helped repair the wall of Jerusalem (Nehemiah 3:7).

Meroz@Jdg.5.23=H4789.brief: A place cursed for not helping against Sisera
Meroz@Jdg.5.23=H4789.short: Meroz, a place cursed by the angel of the Lord for not coming to help fight against Sisera (Judges 5:23).

Mesha@Gen.10.30=H4852.brief: A place marking the Joktanite territory
Mesha@Gen.10.30=H4852.short: Mesha, a place mentioned as the limit of the territory settled by the descendants of Joktan (Genesis 10:30).

Meshech@Psa.120.5-Ezk=H4902H.brief: A nation, descendant of Japheth; associated with Tubal
Meshech@Psa.120.5-Ezk=H4902H.short: Meshech, a nation descended from Japheth (Genesis 10:2), often mentioned together with Tubal as trading partners of Tyre (Ezk.27.13) and allies of Gog (Ezk.38.2, 3; 39:1).

Meshech-Tubal@Ezk.32.26=H4902I.brief: Two nations mentioned together; defeated by Babylon
Meshech-Tubal@Ezk.32.26=H4902I.short: Meshech-Tubal, two nations mentioned together as having been defeated by the Babylonians and lying in the grave with the uncircumcised (Ezk.32.26).

Mesopotamia@Gen.24.10-Act=H0763G.brief: The region between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers
Mesopotamia@Gen.24.10-Act=H0763G.short: Mesopotamia, the ancient region between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers, where Abraham lived before being called to Canaan (Genesis 24:10; Act.7.2) and where the Israelites were oppressed by Cushan-rishathaim (Judges 3:8, 10).

Michmash@1Sa.13.2-Isa=H4363.brief: A town in Benjamin; site of Saul's camp and Jonathan's victory
Michmash@1Sa.13.2-Isa=H4363.short: Michmash, a town in Benjamin where Saul camped (1Sa.13.2, 5, 11, 16, 23) and near which Jonathan defeated a Philistine garrison (1Sa.14.5, 31).

Michmethath@Jos.16.6-=H4366.brief: A place on the borders of Ephraim and Manasseh
Michmethath@Jos.16.6-=H4366.short: Michmethath, a place on the border between the territories of Ephraim and Manasseh (Joshua 16:6; 17:7).

Middin@Jos.15.61=H4081.brief: A town in the wilderness of Judah
Middin@Jos.15.61=H4081.short: Middin, a town in the wilderness of Judah (Joshua 15:61).

Midian@Gen.36.35-Act=H4080H.brief: A nation descended from Abraham; oppressed Israel in the time of the judges
Midian@Gen.36.35-Act=H4080H.short: Midian, a nation descended from Abraham through Keturah (Genesis 25:2), which oppressed Israel during the time of the judges (Judges 6-8) and was later defeated by Gideon (Judges 7-8).

Migdal-el@Jos.19.38=H4027.short: Migdal-el, a fortified city in the territory of Naphtali (Joshua 19:38).

Migdal-gad@Jos.15.37=H4028.brief: A town in the lowlands of Judah
Migdal-gad@Jos.15.37=H4028.short: Migdal-gad, a town in the lowlands of Judah (Joshua 15:37).

Migdol@Exo.14.2-Ezk=H4024B.brief: A place near the Red Sea where the Israelites camped
Migdol@Exo.14.2-Ezk=H4024B.short: Migdol, a place near the Red Sea where the Israelites camped during the Exodus (Exodus 14:2; Numbers 33:7), and a city in Egypt mentioned in prophecies (Jeremiah 44:1; 46:14; Ezk.29.10; 30:6).

Migron@1Sa.14.2-Isa=H4051.brief: A place near Gibeah where Saul camped
Migron@1Sa.14.2-Isa=H4051.short: Migron, a place near Gibeah where Saul camped with his troops (1Sa.14.2), and a town mentioned in Isaiah's prophecy about the Assyrian invasion (Isaiah 10:28).

Miletus@Act.20.15-2Ti=G3399.brief: A city in Asia Minor visited by Paul
Miletus@Act.20.15-2Ti=G3399.short: Miletus, a city in Asia Minor where Paul met with the elders of the Ephesian church on his way to Jerusalem (Act.20.15, 17) and where Trophimus was left ill (2Ti.4.20).

Millo@2Sa.5.9-Isa=H4407.brief: A fortification in Jerusalem built by Solomon
Millo@2Sa.5.9-Isa=H4407.short: Millo (Akra), a fortification in Jerusalem built by Solomon (1Ki.9.15, 24; 11:27) and repaired by Hezekiah (2Ch.32.5).

Minni@Jer.51.27=H4508.brief: A kingdom allied with Ararat and Ashkenaz
Minni@Jer.51.27=H4508.short: Minni, a kingdom mentioned alongside Ararat and Ashkenaz, was called to battle against Babylon.

Minnith@Jdg.11.33-Ezk=H4511.brief: An Ammonite town known for its wheat
Minnith@Jdg.11.33-Ezk=H4511.short: Minnith, an Ammonite town, was known for its wheat and was a place of defeat for the Ammonites by Jephthah.

Misgab@Jer.48.1=H4869B.short: Misgab, meaning "fortress," was a stronghold in Moab that faced judgment according to Jeremiah's prophecy.

Mishal@Jos.19.26-1Ch=H4861.short: Mishal (Mashal), a Levitical city in the territory of Asher (Joshua 19:26; 21:30; 1Ch.6.74).

Misrephoth-maim@Jos.11.8-=H4956.brief: A place near Sidon where the Canaanites fled
Misrephoth-maim@Jos.11.8-=H4956.short: Misrephoth-maim, a location near Sidon, was where the Canaanites fled after being defeated by Joshua.

Mithkah@Num.33.28-=H4989.brief: An Israelite campsite during the wilderness wanderings
Mithkah@Num.33.28-=H4989.short: Mithkah was a place where the Israelites camped during their wilderness journey, between Terah and Hashmonah.

Mitylene@Act.20.14=G3412.brief: A city on the island of Lesbos visited by Paul
Mitylene@Act.20.14=G3412.short: Mitylene, a city on the island of Lesbos where Paul's ship stopped on his way to Jerusalem (Act.20.14).

Mizar_Mount@Psa.42.6=H4706.brief: A mountain mentioned in a psalm of lament
Mizar_Mount@Psa.42.6=H4706.short: Mount Mizar, a mountain mentioned in a psalm of lament, possibly representing a place of remembrance or longing for God's presence (Psalm 42:6).

Mizpah@Jos.18.26-Jhn=H4709G.brief: A city in Benjamin; a place of gathering and judgment
Mizpah@Jos.18.26-Jhn=H4709G.short: Mizpah (Mizpeh, Ramah, Ramathaim-zophim, Arimathea), a city in Benjamin where the Israelites gathered for judgment and prayer (Judges 20:1, 3; 21:1, 5, 8; 1Sa.7.5-7, 11-12, 16; 10:17), and the hometown of Samuel (1Sa.1.19; 2:11; 7:17; 8:4; 15:34; 16:13; 19:18-23; 20:1; 25:1; 28:3) and Joseph of Arimathea (Matthew 27:57; Mrk.15.43; Luke 23:50-51; Jhn.19.38).

Mizpeh@Jos.15.38=H4708G.brief: A town in the lowlands of Judah
Mizpeh@Jos.15.38=H4708G.short: Mizpeh, a town in the lowlands (Shephelah) of Judah (Joshua 15:38).

Mizpeh_Valley@Jos.11.3-=H4709I.short: The Valley of Mizpeh (Mizpah), a region near Mount Hermon where Joshua defeated the kings of the northern Canaanite coalition (Joshua 11:3, 8).

Moab@Gen.19.37b-Zep=H4124G.brief: Ancient kingdom east of the Dead Sea in Jordan
Moab@Gen.19.37b-Zep=H4124G.short: Moab was an ancient kingdom located east of the Dead Sea in present-day Jordan, often in conflict with Israel.

Moab_Plains@Num.22.1-Jos=H4124I.brief: Region east of the Jordan River, opposite Jericho
Moab_Plains@Num.22.1-Jos=H4124I.short: The plains of Moab, located east of the Jordan River and opposite Jericho, were where the Israelites camped before entering the Promised Land (Num.22.1; 26:3, 63; 31:12; 33:48-50; 35:1; 36:13; Deut 34:1, 8; Josh 13:32).

Moladah@Jos.15.26-Neh=H4137.brief: Town in the Negev, allotted to Judah and Simeon
Moladah@Jos.15.26-Neh=H4137.short: Moladah was a town in the Negev region, allotted to the tribes of Judah and Simeon, and later inhabited by the people of Judah after the Babylonian exile (Josh 15:26; 19:2; 1Ch.4.28; Neh.11.26).

Moreh@Gen.12.6-Deu=H4176G.brief: Place near Shechem; also a hill near Gilgal
Moreh@Gen.12.6-Deu=H4176G.short: Moreh refers to two locations: a place near Shechem where Abraham built an altar (Gen.12.6) and a hill near Gilgal, associated with the blessing and cursing ceremony (Deut 11:30).

Moreh@Jdg.7.1=H4176H.brief: Place near Shechem; hill where Gideon camped
Moreh@Jdg.7.1=H4176H.short: Moreh refers to a place near Shechem associated with Abraham (Gen.12.6) and a hill where Gideon camped before attacking the Midianites (Judg 7:1).

Moresheth@Jer.26.18-Mic=H4182.brief: Hometown of the prophet Micah in Judah
Moresheth@Jer.26.18-Mic=H4182.short: Moresheth was the hometown of the prophet Micah, located in Judah.

Moriah_Mount@Gen.22.2-2Ch=H4179.brief: Site of Solomon's temple in Jerusalem
Moriah_Mount@Gen.22.2-2Ch=H4179.short: Mount Moriah was the site where Solomon built the temple in Jerusalem.

Mortar@Zep.1.11=H4389.brief: A district or valley in or near Jerusalem
Mortar@Zep.1.11=H4389.short: The Mortar was a district or valley in or near Jerusalem, mentioned in Zephaniah's prophecy.

Moserah@Deu.10.6=H4149A.brief: A place where the Israelites camped during their wilderness wanderings
Moserah@Deu.10.6=H4149A.short: Moserah was a place where the Israelites camped during their wilderness wanderings, and where Aaron died and was buried.

Moseroth@Num.33.30-=H4149B.brief: A place where the Israelites camped during their wilderness wanderings
Moseroth@Num.33.30-=H4149B.short: Moseroth was a place where the Israelites camped during their wilderness wanderings after leaving Egypt.

Most_Holy_Place@1Ki.6.16-Heb=H6944H.brief: The innermost room of the tabernacle and temple
Most_Holy_Place@1Ki.6.16-Heb=H6944H.short: The Most Holy Place was the innermost room of the tabernacle and temple, where the Ark of the Covenant was kept.

Mozah@Jos.18.26=H4681.brief: A town in the territory of Benjamin
Mozah@Jos.18.26=H4681.short: Mozah was a town allotted to the tribe of Benjamin.

Muster_Gate@Neh.3.31=H4663.brief: A gate in Jerusalem mentioned in Nehemiah's time
Muster_Gate@Neh.3.31=H4663.short: The Muster Gate, also known as the Miphkad Gate, was one of the gates of Jerusalem mentioned in Nehemiah's time.

Myra@Act.27.5=G3460.brief: A city in Lycia where Paul's ship stopped
Myra@Act.27.5=G3460.short: Myra was a city in Lycia, Asia Minor, where Paul's ship stopped on his journey to Rome as a prisoner.

Mysia@Act.16.7-=G3465.brief: A region in northwest Asia Minor visited by Paul
Mysia@Act.16.7-=G3465.short: Mysia was a region in northwest Asia Minor (modern Turkey) that Paul and his companions passed through on his second missionary journey.

Naamah@Jos.15.41=H5279B.brief: A town in the Judean lowlands
Naamah@Jos.15.41=H5279B.short: Naamah was a town in the Judean lowlands, mentioned in the tribal allotment of Judah.

Naaran@Jos.16.7-1Ch=H5295.brief: A border town between Ephraim and Benjamin
Naaran@Jos.16.7-1Ch=H5295.short: Naaran, also called Naarah, was a border town between the tribes of Ephraim and Benjamin.

Nahalol@Jos.19.15-Jdg=H5096.short: Nahalol, also called Nahalal, was a Levitical city in the territory of Zebulun.

Nain@Luk.7.11=G3484.brief: A town in Galilee where Jesus raised a widow's son
Nain@Luk.7.11=G3484.short: Nain was a town in Galilee where Jesus raised a widow's son from the dead.

Naioth@1Sa.19.18-=H5121.brief: A place near Ramah where David fled from Saul
Naioth@1Sa.19.18-=H5121.short: Naioth was a place near Ramah where David fled to escape King Saul, and where Samuel and a group of prophets lived.

Naphath@Jos.17.11=H5316G.brief: A region in Issachar with Manassite towns
Naphath@Jos.17.11=H5316G.short: Naphath was a region in Issachar that contained towns belonging to the tribe of Manasseh.

Nazareth@Mat.2.23-Act=G3478.brief: The hometown of Jesus in Galilee
Nazareth@Mat.2.23-Act=G3478.short: Nazareth was a village in Galilee where Jesus grew up, giving rise to His title "Jesus of Nazareth."

Neah@Jos.19.13-=H5272.brief: A border town of Zebulun and Asher
Neah@Jos.19.13-=H5272.short: Neah, also called Neiel, was a border town between the territories of Zebulun and Asher.

Neapolis@Act.16.11=G3496.brief: A port city in Macedonia visited by Paul
Neapolis@Act.16.11=G3496.short: Neapolis was a port city in Macedonia where Paul landed on his first journey to Europe.

Neballat@Neh.11.34=H5041.brief: A town in Benjamin inhabited by Benjamites after the exile
Neballat@Neh.11.34=H5041.short: Neballat was a town in the territory of Benjamin where some Benjamites settled after returning from the Babylonian exile.

Nebo@Ezr.2.29-Neh=H5015G.brief: A town in Judah, possibly named after a person
Nebo@Ezr.2.29-Neh=H5015G.short: Nebo was a town in Judah, possibly named after a person, whose inhabitants returned from the Babylonian exile.

Nebo@Num.32.3-Jer=H5015A.brief: A city and mountain in Moab
Nebo@Num.32.3-Jer=H5015A.short: Nebo was a city and mountain in Moab, mentioned in the Old Testament.

Nebo_Mount@Num.27.12-Jer=H5015H.brief: The mountain where Moses viewed the Promised Land
Nebo_Mount@Num.27.12-Jer=H5015H.short: Mount Nebo, also called Abarim, was the mountain from which Moses viewed the Promised Land before his death.

Negeb@Gen.12.9-Zec=H5045G.brief: The southern region of Israel, a semi-arid area
Negeb@Gen.12.9-Zec=H5045G.short: The Negeb, meaning "south," refers to the semi-arid region in the southern part of Israel.

Nephtoah@Jos.15.9-=H5318.brief: A spring on the border of Judah and Benjamin
Nephtoah@Jos.15.9-=H5318.short: Nephtoah was a spring that served as a boundary marker between the territories of Judah and Benjamin.

Netaim@1Ch.4.23=H5196.brief: A place associated with potters in Judah
Netaim@1Ch.4.23=H5196.short: Netaim was a place in Judah where potters lived and worked.

Netophah@2Sa.23.28-Jer=H5199.brief: A town in Judah, home to several notable individuals
Netophah@2Sa.23.28-Jer=H5199.short: Netophah was a town in Judah, known as the hometown of several notable individuals in the Bible.

New_Gate@Jer.26.10-=H2319G.brief: A gate in Jerusalem during Jeremiah's time
New_Gate@Jer.26.10-=H2319G.short: The New Gate was a gate in Jerusalem during the time of the prophet Jeremiah.

Nezib@Jos.15.43=H5334.brief: A town in the Judean lowlands
Nezib@Jos.15.43=H5334.short: Nezib was a town allotted to the tribe of Judah in the lowland region.

Nibshan@Jos.15.62=H5044.brief: A town in the Judean wilderness
Nibshan@Jos.15.62=H5044.short: Nibshan was a town in the wilderness of Judah, mentioned in the list of towns allotted to the tribe of Judah.

Nicopolis@Tit.3.12-=G3533.brief: A city in Epirus where Paul planned to winter
Nicopolis@Tit.3.12-=G3533.short: Nicopolis was a city in Epirus where Paul intended to spend the winter, as mentioned in his letter to Titus.

Nile@Gen.41.1-Zec=H2975G.brief: The major river of Egypt, mentioned in various contexts
Nile@Gen.41.1-Zec=H2975G.short: The Nile, the major river of Egypt, is mentioned in various contexts throughout the Bible, often in relation to the history of Israel and God's judgment on Egypt.

Nimrim@Isa.15.6-Jer=H5249.brief: A place in Moab known for its waters
Nimrim@Isa.15.6-Jer=H5249.short: Nimrim was a place in Moab known for its waters, which are mentioned in the context of God's judgment on Moab.

Nineveh@Gen.10.11-Luk=H5210.brief: The capital of Assyria, known for its wickedness and repentance
Nineveh@Gen.10.11-Luk=H5210.short: Nineveh, the capital of Assyria, is known in the Bible for its wickedness and its remarkable repentance following Jonah's preaching.

Nob@1Sa.21.1-Isa=H5011.brief: A city of priests near Jerusalem
Nob@1Sa.21.1-Isa=H5011.short: Nob was a city of priests near Jerusalem, known for a massacre ordered by King Saul and as a temporary location of the Ark of the Covenant.

Nod@Gen.4.16=H5113.brief: The land where Cain settled after killing Abel
Nod@Gen.4.16=H5113.short: Nod was the land east of Eden where Cain settled after he was banished for killing his brother Abel.

Oboth@Num.21.10-=H0088.brief: A place where the Israelites camped during the Exodus
Oboth@Num.21.10-=H0088.short: Oboth was one of the places where the Israelites camped during their journey through the wilderness after the Exodus from Egypt.

Olives_Mount@2Sa.15.30-Act=H2132G.brief: A mountain ridge east of Jerusalem
Olives_Mount@2Sa.15.30-Act=H2132G.short: The Mount of Olives is a mountain ridge east of Jerusalem, known as the site of many significant events in the Bible, particularly in the life of Jesus.

On@Gen.41.45-Ezk=H0204.brief: An ancient Egyptian city, mentioned in relation to Joseph
On@Gen.41.45-Ezk=H0204.short: On, also known as Heliopolis, was an ancient Egyptian city mentioned in the Bible in connection with Joseph's life and prophetic references to Egypt.

Ono@1Ch.8.12-Neh=H0207.brief: A town in Benjamin, near Lod
Ono@1Ch.8.12-Neh=H0207.short: Ono was a town in the territory of Benjamin, often mentioned together with Lod, and was the site of a proposed meeting between Nehemiah and his enemies.

Ophel@2Ch.27.3-Neh=H6077.short: Ophel was a fortified area in Jerusalem, located near the temple, and was inhabited by temple servants during the time of Nehemiah.

Ophir@1Ki.9.28-Isa=H0211H.brief: A region known for its gold
Ophir@1Ki.9.28-Isa=H0211H.short: Ophir was a region famous for its high-quality gold, which was imported to Israel during the reigns of David and Solomon.

Ophni@Jos.18.24=H6078.short: Ophni was a town allotted to the tribe of Benjamin during the division of the Promised Land.

Ophrah@Jos.18.23-Mic=H6084G.brief: A town in Benjamin and a place in Manasseh
Ophrah@Jos.18.23-Mic=H6084G.short: Ophrah was a town in Benjamin and a place in Manasseh, associated with Gideon and mentioned in a prophecy of Micah.

Ophrah@Jos.19.19-Jdg=H6084H.brief: Gideon's hometown in Manasseh; a town in Issachar
Ophrah@Jos.19.19-Jdg=H6084H.short: Ophrah, also known as Hapharaim, was Gideon's hometown in Manasseh and the site of important events during his time as a judge, as well as a town allotted to the tribe of Issachar.

Pacatiana@1Ti.6.21=G3818.brief: A place mentioned in some manuscripts of 1 Timothy
Pacatiana@1Ti.6.21=G3818.short: Pacatiana is a place mentioned in some manuscripts of 1Ti.6.21, but its exact location and significance are unknown.

Paddan@Gen.25.20-Hos=H6307.brief: The homeland of the patriarchs in Mesopotamia
Paddan@Gen.25.20-Hos=H6307.short: Paddan, also known as Paddan-aram or Aram, was the homeland of the patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, located in Mesopotamia.

Pamphylia@Act.2.10-=G3828.brief: A Roman province in Asia Minor
Pamphylia@Act.2.10-=G3828.short: Pamphylia was a Roman province on the southern coast of Asia Minor, visited by Paul and Barnabas during their missionary journeys.

Paphos@Act.13.6-=G3974.brief: A city on the island of Cyprus
Paphos@Act.13.6-=G3974.short: Paphos was a city on the island of Cyprus, where Paul and Barnabas encountered a sorcerer and converted the proconsul to Christianity.

Parah@Jos.18.23=H6511.short: Parah was a city allotted to the tribe of Benjamin, located between Avvim and Ophrah.

Paran@Gen.21.21-1Ki=H6290G.brief: A desert region in the Sinai Peninsula
Paran@Gen.21.21-1Ki=H6290G.short: Paran was a desert region in the Sinai Peninsula, associated with the Israelites' wanderings and the early life of Ishmael.

Paran_Mount@Deu.33.2-Hab=H6290H.brief: A mountain associated with God's appearance
Paran_Mount@Deu.33.2-Hab=H6290H.short: Mount Paran is mentioned in poetic passages as a place from which God comes or shines forth.

Parbar@1Ch.26.18=H6503.brief: A colonnade or structure in the temple complex
Parbar@1Ch.26.18=H6503.short: Parbar was a colonnade or structure located on the west side of the temple complex in Jerusalem.

Parvaim@2Ch.3.6=H6516.brief: A place from which Solomon obtained gold
Parvaim@2Ch.3.6=H6516.short: Parvaim was a place or region from which Solomon obtained gold for decorating the temple in Jerusalem.

Patara@Act.21.1=G3959.brief: A city in Lycia visited by Paul
Patara@Act.21.1=G3959.short: Patara was a coastal city in Lycia (modern-day Turkey) where Paul changed ships during his journey to Jerusalem.

Pathros@Isa.11.11-Ezk=H6624.short: Pathros was a region in Upper Egypt (southern Egypt) where some Judeans settled after the Babylonian exile.

Patmos@Rev.1.9=G3963.brief: An island where John received the Revelation
Patmos@Rev.1.9=G3963.short: Patmos is a Greek island in the Aegean Sea where the apostle John was exiled and received the visions recorded in the Book of Revelation.

Pau@Gen.36.39-1Ch=H6464.short: Pau, also known as Pai, was a city in Edom mentioned in the genealogy of Edomite kings.

Pelusium@Ezk.30.15-=H5512A.brief: An Egyptian city, also known as Sin
Pelusium@Ezk.30.15-=H5512A.short: Pelusium, also known as Sin, was an important Egyptian city mentioned in Ezekiel's prophecy against Egypt.

Peniel@Gen.32.30-1Ki=H6439G.brief: A place where Jacob wrestled with God
Peniel@Gen.32.30-1Ki=H6439G.short: Peniel, also called Penuel, was the place where Jacob wrestled with God and had his name changed to Israel.

People's_Gate@Jer.17.19=H5971H.brief: A gate in Jerusalem mentioned by Jeremiah
People's_Gate@Jer.17.19=H5971H.short: The People's Gate was one of the gates of Jerusalem, where the prophet Jeremiah was instructed to proclaim God's message.

Peor@Num.23.28-Jos=H6465.brief: A mountain in Moab associated with idolatry
Peor@Num.23.28-Jos=H6465.short: Peor was a mountain in Moab where Balak brought Balaam to curse Israel, and where the Israelites later engaged in idolatry and immorality with the Moabites.

Perazim_Mount@Isa.28.21=H6559.brief: A place where David defeated the Philistines
Perazim_Mount@Isa.28.21=H6559.short: Mount Perazim was the location where David, with God's help, defeated the Philistines, and it is used by Isaiah as an example of God's judgment.

Perez-uzza@1Ch.13.11=H6560G.brief: A place named after Uzzah's death
Perez-uzza@1Ch.13.11=H6560G.short: Perez-uzza was the name given to the place where Uzzah died after touching the Ark of the Covenant during its transport to Jerusalem.

Perga@Act.13.13-=G4011.brief: A city in Pamphylia visited by Paul
Perga@Act.13.13-=G4011.short: Perga was a city in Pamphylia (modern-day Turkey) where Paul and Barnabas preached the gospel during their first missionary journey.

Pergamum@Rev.1.11-=G4010.brief: A city in Asia Minor with a church
Pergamum@Rev.1.11-=G4010.short: Pergamum was one of the seven churches of Asia addressed in the Book of Revelation, known for its faithfulness despite living in a city associated with Satan's throne.

Persia@2Ch.36.20-Dan=H6539.brief: An empire that ruled over the exiled Jews
Persia@2Ch.36.20-Dan=H6539.short: Persia was the empire that conquered Babylon and allowed the exiled Jews to return to Jerusalem and rebuild the temple.

Pethor@Num.22.5-Deu=H6604.brief: The hometown of Balaam in Mesopotamia
Pethor@Num.22.5-Deu=H6604.short: Pethor was the hometown of Balaam, the prophet hired by Balak to curse Israel, located near the Euphrates River in Mesopotamia.

Pharpar@2Ki.5.12=H6554.short: Pharpar was one of the rivers of Damascus, mentioned by Naaman the leper when comparing them to the Jordan River in Israel.

Philadelphia@Rev.1.11-=G5359.brief: One of the seven churches in Asia Minor
Philadelphia@Rev.1.11-=G5359.short: Philadelphia was one of the seven churches in Asia Minor addressed in the Book of Revelation, known for its faithfulness and endurance.

Philippi@Act.16.12-1Th=G5375.brief: A city in Macedonia visited by Paul
Philippi@Act.16.12-1Th=G5375.short: Philippi was a city in Macedonia where Paul founded a church and experienced persecution, imprisonment, and a miraculous deliverance.

Philistia@Gen.21.32-Zec=H6429.brief: An ancient people and region in Canaan
Philistia@Gen.21.32-Zec=H6429.short: The Philistines were a powerful people who inhabited the coastal plain of Canaan and were often in conflict with the Israelites during the period of the judges and early monarchy.

Phoenicia@Act.11.19-=G5403.brief: A region and people on the Mediterranean coast
Phoenicia@Act.11.19-=G5403.short: Phoenicia was a region along the Mediterranean coast, north of Israel, known for its maritime trade and mentioned in the New Testament in connection with the spread of the gospel.

Phoenix@Act.27.12=G5405.brief: A harbor on the island of Crete
Phoenix@Act.27.12=G5405.short: Phoenix was a harbor on the island of Crete where the ship carrying Paul and other prisoners attempted to winter during their journey to Rome.

Phrygia@Act.2.10-1Ti=G5435.brief: A region in Asia Minor with early Christians
Phrygia@Act.2.10-1Ti=G5435.short: Phrygia was a region in Asia Minor where Paul traveled and preached the gospel, and some of its inhabitants were present in Jerusalem on the day of Pentecost.

Pi-beseth@Ezk.30.17=H6364.brief: An Egyptian city mentioned in Ezekiel's prophecy
Pi-beseth@Ezk.30.17=H6364.short: Pi-beseth was an Egyptian city that Ezekiel prophesied would experience God's judgment along with other cities in Egypt.

Pi-hahiroth@Exo.14.2-Num=H6367.brief: A place near the Red Sea crossing
