Pi-hahiroth@Exo.14.2-Num=H6367.short: Pi-hahiroth was a location near the Red Sea where the Israelites camped before crossing the sea during the Exodus from Egypt.

Pirathon@Jdg.12.13-1Ch=H6552.brief: A town in Ephraim, home of several notable Israelites
Pirathon@Jdg.12.13-1Ch=H6552.short: Pirathon was a town in the hill country of Ephraim, associated with the judge Abdon and two of David's mighty men, Benaiah and Hiddai.

Pisgah@Num.21.20-Jos=H6449.brief: A mountain range in Moab, east of the Jordan
Pisgah@Num.21.20-Jos=H6449.short: Pisgah, or the slopes of Pisgah, was a mountain range in Moab where Moses viewed the Promised Land before his death.

Pishon@Gen.2.11=H6376.brief: A river flowing from Eden, encircling Havilah
Pishon@Gen.2.11=H6376.short: Pishon was one of the four rivers that flowed from the river in the Garden of Eden, encircling the land of Havilah, which was known for its gold, bdellium, and onyx.

Pisidia@Act.13.14-=G4099.brief: A region in Asia Minor visited by Paul
Pisidia@Act.13.14-=G4099.short: Pisidia was a mountainous region in Asia Minor where Paul and Barnabas preached the gospel during their first missionary journey.

Pithom@Exo.1.11=H6619.brief: A store city built by the Israelites in Egypt
Pithom@Exo.1.11=H6619.short: Pithom was one of the store cities built by the Israelites during their enslavement in Egypt, along with Rameses.

Pontus@Act.2.9-1Pe=G4195.brief: A region in Asia Minor with Jewish inhabitants
Pontus@Act.2.9-1Pe=G4195.short: Pontus was a region in Asia Minor along the Black Sea coast, home to Jewish inhabitants and early Christian converts.

Potsherd_Gate@Jer.19.2=H2777.brief: A gate in Jerusalem mentioned by Jeremiah
Potsherd_Gate@Jer.19.2=H2777.short: The Potsherd Gate was a gate in Jerusalem near the Valley of Ben Hinnom, where Jeremiah was instructed to proclaim a message of judgment against Judah.

Punon@Num.33.42-=H6325.brief: A stopping place for the Israelites in the wilderness
Punon@Num.33.42-=H6325.short: Punon was one of the places where the Israelites camped during their wilderness wanderings, located between Zalmonah and Oboth.

Puteoli@Act.28.13=G4223.brief: A port city in Italy visited by Paul
Puteoli@Act.28.13=G4223.short: Puteoli was a major port city in Italy where Paul stayed for seven days on his journey to Rome as a prisoner.

Raamah@Ezk.27.22=H7484H.brief: A trading partner of Tyre, possibly in Arabia
Raamah@Ezk.27.22=H7484H.short: Raamah was a place, possibly located in Arabia, that traded with the city of Tyre, offering spices, precious stones, and gold.

Raamses@Exo.1.11=H7486H.brief: A store city built by the Israelites in Egypt
Raamses@Exo.1.11=H7486H.short: Raamses was one of the store cities built by the Israelites during their enslavement in Egypt, along with Pithom.

Rabbith@Jos.19.20=H7245.brief: A town allotted to the tribe of Issachar
Rabbith@Jos.19.20=H7245.short: Rabbith was a town in the territory of Issachar, mentioned in the list of cities and towns allocated to the tribe during the division of the Promised Land.

Rakkath@Jos.19.35-Jhn=H7557.brief: City on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee
Rakkath@Jos.19.35-Jhn=H7557.short: Tiberias (Rakkath), a city on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee, near where Jesus fed the five thousand (Josh. 19:35; Jhn.6.23).

Rakkon@Jos.19.46=H7542.brief: A town allotted to the tribe of Dan
Rakkon@Jos.19.46=H7542.short: Rakkon was a town mentioned in the description of the territory allocated to the tribe of Dan in the Promised Land.

Ramah@Jos.18.25-Mat=H7414G.brief: A town in Benjamin, near Gibeah and Jerusalem
Ramah@Jos.18.25-Mat=H7414G.short: Ramah was a town in the territory of Benjamin, often associated with significant events in Israel's history, such as the mourning of Rachel and the imprisonment of Jeremiah.

Ramah@Jos.19.29=H7414H.brief: A town on the border of Asher and Tyre
Ramah@Jos.19.29=H7414H.short: Ramah was a town located on the border between the territory of Asher and the city-state of Tyre.

Ramah@Jos.19.36=H7414I.brief: A fortified city in the territory of Naphtali
Ramah@Jos.19.36=H7414I.short: Ramah was a fortified city located in the territory of Naphtali, mentioned in the list of cities allocated to the tribe during the division of the Promised Land.

Ramath-lehi@Jdg.15.17=H7437.brief: The place where Samson killed a thousand Philistines
Ramath-lehi@Jdg.15.17=H7437.short: Ramath-lehi, meaning "hill of the jawbone," was the place where Samson killed a thousand Philistines with the jawbone of a donkey.

Rameses@Gen.47.11-Num=H7486G.brief: Egyptian city where Israelites lived before the Exodus
Rameses@Gen.47.11-Num=H7486G.short: Rameses was a city in Egypt where the Israelites lived during their enslavement before the Exodus (Gen. 47:11; Exo. 12:37).

Ramoth@Gen.31.47-Hos=H7216H.brief: City of refuge east of the Jordan
Ramoth@Gen.31.47-Hos=H7216H.short: Ramoth, also called Ramoth-gilead, was a city of refuge in Gad and a Levitical city (Deu. 4:43; Jos. 20:8; 21:38).

Recah@1Ch.4.12=H7397B.short: Recah was a descendant of Judah through Caleb (1Ch. 4:12).

Red_Sea@Exo.10.19-Heb=H5488G.brief: Sea crossed by Israelites in the Exodus
Red_Sea@Exo.10.19-Heb=H5488G.short: The Red Sea was the body of water miraculously crossed by the Israelites in their escape from Egypt (Exo. 13:18; 15:4).

Rehob@Jos.19.28=H7340G.brief: City on the border of Asher
Rehob@Jos.19.28=H7340G.short: Rehob was a city on the northern border of the territory allotted to the tribe of Asher (Jos. 19:28).

Rehob@Jos.19.30-1Ch=H7340H.short: Rehob was a Levitical city within the territory of Asher (Jos. 19:30; 21:31; 1Ch. 6:75).

Rehoboth@Gen.26.22=H7344G.short: Rehoboth was the name of a well dug by Isaac where he found room and water (Gen. 26:22).

Rehoboth@Gen.36.37-1Ch=H7344H.brief: City associated with an Edomite king
Rehoboth@Gen.36.37-1Ch=H7344H.short: Rehoboth was a city associated with Shaul, an Edomite king (Gen. 36:37; 1Ch. 1:48).

Rekem@Jos.18.27=H7552H.short: Rekem was a city allotted to the tribe of Benjamin (Jos. 18:27).

Remeth@Jos.19.21-1Ch=H7432.short: Remeth, also called Ramoth, was a Levitical city allotted to the tribe of Issachar (Jos. 19:21; 1Ch. 6:73).

Rephaim_Valley@Jos.15.8-Isa=H7497G.brief: Valley near Jerusalem, site of battles
Rephaim_Valley@Jos.15.8-Isa=H7497G.short: The Valley of Rephaim was a valley near Jerusalem where David fought the Philistines (2Sa. 5:18, 22; 23:13; 1Ch. 11:15; 14:9).

Rephidim@Exo.17.1-Num=H7508.short: Rephidim was a place where the Israelites camped during their journey from Egypt to Sinai (Exo. 17:1, 8; 19:2; Num. 33:14, 15).

Resen@Gen.10.12=H7449.brief: Ancient Assyrian city built by Nimrod
Resen@Gen.10.12=H7449.short: Resen was an ancient Assyrian city built by Nimrod between Nineveh and Calah (Gen. 10:12).

Rezeph@2Ki.19.12-Isa=H7530.short: Rezeph was a city conquered by the Assyrians, mentioned in a letter from the Assyrian king to Hezekiah (2Ki. 19:12; Isa. 37:12).

Rhegium@Act.28.13=G4484.short: Rhegium was a city in Italy where Paul's ship stopped on his journey to Rome (Act. 28:13).

Rhodes@Act.21.1=G4499.brief: Island visited by Paul on his journey
Rhodes@Act.21.1=G4499.short: Rhodes was an island where Paul stopped during his journey to Jerusalem (Act. 21:1).

Riblah@2Ki.23.33-Ezk=H7247H.brief: Babylonian headquarters during the conquest of Judah
Riblah@2Ki.23.33-Ezk=H7247H.short: Riblah was a city in Hamath where the Babylonians set up their headquarters during their campaigns against Judah (2Ki. 23:33; 25:6, 20-21; Jer. 39:5-6; 52:9-10, 26-27).

Riblah@Num.34.11=H7247G.brief: Place on the eastern border of the Promised Land
Riblah@Num.34.11=H7247G.short: Riblah was a place mentioned in the description of the eastern border of the Promised Land (Num. 34:11).

Rimmon@Jdg.20.45-=H7417C.brief: Rock where Benjamites fled after battle
Rimmon@Jdg.20.45-=H7417C.short: Rimmon was a rock where 600 Benjamite survivors fled after a battle with the other Israelite tribes (Jdg. 20:45, 47; 21:13).

Rimmon@Jos.15.32-1Ch=H7417I.brief: A town in Judah and Simeon
Rimmon@Jos.15.32-1Ch=H7417I.short: Rimmon, a town allotted to Judah and later given to Simeon, was located in the Negev region.

Rimmon-perez@Num.33.19-=H7428.short: Rimmon-perez was a place where the Israelites camped during their journey from Egypt to Canaan (Num. 33:19-20).

Rissah@Num.33.21-=H7446.short: Rissah was a place where the Israelites camped during their journey from Egypt to Canaan (Num. 33:21-22).

Rithmah@Num.33.18-=H7575.short: Rithmah was a place where the Israelites camped during their journey from Egypt to Canaan (Num. 33:18-19).

Rock_of_Escape@1Sa.23.28=H5555.brief: Place where Saul stopped pursuing David
Rock_of_Escape@1Sa.23.28=H5555.short: The Rock of Escape was a place where Saul stopped pursuing David after being called away to fight the Philistines (1Sa. 23:28).

Rogelim@2Sa.17.27-=H7274.short: Rogelim was the hometown of Barzillai the Gileadite, who provided supplies for David during Absalom's rebellion (2Sa. 17:27; 19:31).

Rome@Jhn.11.48-Phm=G4514.brief: Capital city of the Roman Empire
Rome@Jhn.11.48-Phm=G4514.short: Rome was the capital of the Roman Empire, where Paul was imprisoned and wrote several epistles (Act.28.16; Rom. 1:7).

Sahar@Ezk.27.18=H6713.brief: Unknown location mentioned in Ezekiel's prophecy
Sahar@Ezk.27.18=H6713.short: Sahar is a place mentioned in Ezekiel's prophecy, but its exact location is unknown (Ezk. 27:18).

Salamis@Act.13.5=G4529.brief: City on Cyprus visited by Paul and Barnabas
Salamis@Act.13.5=G4529.short: Salamis was a city on the island of Cyprus where Paul and Barnabas preached the gospel in the Jewish synagogues (Act.13.5).

Salecah@Deu.3.10-1Ch=H5548.brief: City in Bashan, east of the Jordan River
Salecah@Deu.3.10-1Ch=H5548.short: Salecah was a city in the region of Bashan, east of the Jordan River, associated with the kingdoms of Og and Sihon (Deut. 3:10; Josh. 12:5; 13:11; 1Chr. 5:11).

Salim@Jhn.3.23=G4530.brief: Place near Aenon where John the Baptist baptized
Salim@Jhn.3.23=G4530.short: Salim was a place near Aenon where John the Baptist was baptizing, because there was plenty of water there (Jhn.3.23).

Salmone@Act.27.7=G4534.brief: Promontory on the island of Crete
Salmone@Act.27.7=G4534.short: Salmone was a promontory on the island of Crete that Paul's ship passed on his voyage to Rome (Act.27.7).

Salt_Sea@Gen.14.3-2Ki=H4417G.brief: Another name for the Dead Sea
Salt_Sea@Gen.14.3-2Ki=H4417G.short: The Salt Sea, also known as the Sea of Arabah, is another name for the Dead Sea, located at the lowest point on Earth (Gen. 14:3; Num. 34:3, 12; Deut. 3:17; Josh. 3:16; 12:3; 15:2, 5; 18:19; Deut. 4:49; 2Ki. 14:25).

Salt_Valley@2Sa.8.13-Psa=H4417H.brief: Valley where David and his commanders defeated enemies
Salt_Valley@2Sa.8.13-Psa=H4417H.short: The Salt Valley was a location where David and his commanders defeated the Edomites and Arameans (2Sa. 8:13; 2Ki. 14:7; 1Chr. 18:12; 2Chr. 25:11; Psa. 60:1).

Samaria@1Ki.13.32-Act=H8111.brief: Capital city of the northern kingdom of Israel; Samaritan inhabitants
Samaria@1Ki.13.32-Act=H8111.short: Samaria was the capital city of the northern kingdom of Israel, and its inhabitants were known as Samaritans (1Ki. 16:24; 2Ki. 17:24; Jhn. 4:9; Act.8.5).

Samos@Act.20.15=G4544.brief: Island visited by Paul during his travels
Samos@Act.20.15=G4544.short: Samos is an island in the Aegean Sea where Paul stopped during his third missionary journey (Act.20.15).

Samothrace@Act.16.11=G4543.brief: Island visited by Paul during his second missionary journey
Samothrace@Act.16.11=G4543.short: Samothrace is an island in the Aegean Sea where Paul and his companions landed during his second missionary journey (Act.16.11).

Sansannah@Jos.15.31=H5578.brief: Town in the Negev region of Judah
Sansannah@Jos.15.31=H5578.short: Sansannah was a town allotted to the tribe of Judah in the Negev region (Josh. 15:31).

Sarid@Jos.19.10-=H8301.short: Sarid was a border town in the territory allotted to the tribe of Zebulun (Josh. 19:10, 12).

Seba@Psa.72.10-Isa=H5434H.brief: Kingdom mentioned in prophetic and poetic texts
Seba@Psa.72.10-Isa=H5434H.short: Seba was a kingdom mentioned in prophetic and poetic texts, often in the context of bringing gifts to God (Psa. 72:10; Isa. 43:3).

Sebam@Num.32.3=H7643G.brief: Town in the territory of Reuben
Sebam@Num.32.3=H7643G.short: Sebam was one of the towns in the territory of Reuben, east of the Jordan River (Num. 32:3).

Secacah@Jos.15.61=H5527.brief: Town in the wilderness of Judah
Secacah@Jos.15.61=H5527.short: Secacah was a town located in the wilderness region of Judah (Josh. 15:61).

Second_Quarter@2Ki.22.14-Zep=H4932G.brief: District in Jerusalem mentioned by Huldah and Zephaniah
Second_Quarter@2Ki.22.14-Zep=H4932G.short: The Second Quarter was a district in Jerusalem mentioned in connection with the prophetess Huldah (2Ki. 22:14; 2Chr. 34:22) and in Zephaniah's prophecy (Zeph. 1:10).

Secu@1Sa.19.22=H7906.brief: Place near Ramah visited by Saul
Secu@1Sa.19.22=H7906.short: Secu was a place near Ramah where Saul went in search of David (1Sam. 19:22).

Seir@Gen.14.6-Ezk=H8165A.brief: Region inhabited by Edomites, descendants of Esau
Seir@Gen.14.6-Ezk=H8165A.short: Seir was a mountainous region inhabited by the Edomites, the descendants of Esau (Gen. 32:3; 36:8; Num. 24:18; Deut. 2:4; Josh. 24:4).

Seir_Mount@Deu.1.2-Ezk=H8165G.brief: Mountainous region in Seir, associated with Edom
Seir_Mount@Deu.1.2-Ezk=H8165G.short: Mount Seir refers to the mountainous region within Seir, often associated with the Edomites (Deut. 1:2; 2:1, 5; 1Chr. 4:42; Ezek. 35:2, 3, 7, 15).

Seir_Mount@Jos.15.10=H8165H.brief: Landmark on the boundary of Judah
Seir_Mount@Jos.15.10=H8165H.short: Mount Seir was a landmark on the boundary of Judah, near Kiriath-jearim and Chesalon (Josh. 15:10).

Seirah@Jdg.3.26=H8167.brief: Place where Ehud escaped after killing Eglon
Seirah@Jdg.3.26=H8167.short: Seirah was the place to which Ehud escaped after killing Eglon, the king of Moab (Judg. 3:26).

Sela@Jdg.1.36-Isa=H5554.brief: Edomite stronghold captured by King Amaziah of Judah
Sela@Jdg.1.36-Isa=H5554.short: Sela, also known as rock or Joktheel, was an Edomite stronghold captured by King Amaziah of Judah (2Ki. 14:7; 2Chr. 25:12; Isa. 16:1; 42:11; Judg. 1:36).

Seleucia@Act.13.4=G4581.brief: Port city from which Paul and Barnabas sailed
Seleucia@Act.13.4=G4581.short: Seleucia was the port city from which Paul and Barnabas sailed to Cyprus on their first missionary journey (Act.13.4).

Senaah@Ezr.2.35-Neh=H5570G.brief: Town whose people returned from Babylonian exile
Senaah@Ezr.2.35-Neh=H5570G.short: Senaah was a town whose people are listed among those who returned to Judah from the Babylonian exile (Ezr. 2:35; Neh. 7:38).

Seneh@1Sa.14.4=H5573.short: Seneh was one of two rocky crags between which Jonathan and his armor-bearer passed to attack the Philistine garrison at Michmash (1Sam. 14:4).

Sephar@Gen.10.30=H5611.brief: Boundary of the territory settled by Joktan's descendants
Sephar@Gen.10.30=H5611.short: Sephar was a mountain in the east that marked the boundary of the territory settled by the descendants of Joktan (Gen. 10:30).

Sepharad@Oba.1.20-Rev=H5614.brief: City in Asia Minor; destination of exiled Jews
Sepharad@Oba.1.20-Rev=H5614.short: Sepharad, possibly referring to Sardis, was a destination of exiled Jews (Obad. 1:20) and one of the seven churches mentioned in Revelation (Rev. 1:11; 3:1, 4).

Sepharvaim@2Ki.17.24-Isa=H5617.brief: City of origin for people resettled in Samaria
Sepharvaim@2Ki.17.24-Isa=H5617.short: Sepharvaim was one of the cities from which the Assyrians brought people to resettle in Samaria after the deportation of the Israelites (2Ki. 17:24, 31; 18:34; 19:13; Isa. 36:19; 37:13).

Shaalbim@Jos.19.42-1Ch=H8169.brief: Town in Dan, home of David's mighty men
Shaalbim@Jos.19.42-1Ch=H8169.short: Shaalbim, also called Shaalabbin, was a town allotted to the tribe of Dan (Josh. 19:42; Judg. 1:35) and the hometown of some of David's mighty men (2Sam. 23:32; 1Chr. 11:33). It was also a town under Solomon's administration (1Ki. 4:9).

Shaalim@1Sa.9.4=H8171.brief: Region traversed by Saul in search of donkeys
Shaalim@1Sa.9.4=H8171.short: Shaalim was a region through which Saul passed while searching for his father's lost donkeys (1Sam. 9:4).

Shaaraim@Jos.15.36-1Sa=H8189G.brief: Town in Judah; site of Philistine retreat
Shaaraim@Jos.15.36-1Sa=H8189G.short: Shaaraim was a town in the Shephelah of Judah (Josh. 15:36) and a place the Philistines passed in their retreat from Socoh (1Sam. 17:52).

Shahazumah@Jos.19.22=H7831.short: Shahazumah was a town on the border of Issachar's territory (Josh. 19:22).

Shalishah@1Sa.9.4=H8031.brief: Region Saul passed through seeking donkeys
Shalishah@1Sa.9.4=H8031.short: Shalishah was a region Saul and his servant passed through while searching for his father's lost donkeys (1Sam. 9:4).

Shallecheth@1Ch.26.16=H7996.brief: Gate in Jerusalem assigned to Shuppim and Hosah
Shallecheth@1Ch.26.16=H7996.short: Shallecheth was a gate in Jerusalem assigned to the Levites Shuppim and Hosah for guard duty (1Chr. 26:16).

Shamir@Jdg.10.1-=H8069H.brief: Issacharite judge who led Israel for 23 years
Shamir@Jdg.10.1-=H8069H.short: Shamir, from the hill country of Ephraim, was an Issacharite who judged Israel for 23 years (Judg. 10:1-2).

Shamir@Jos.15.48=H8069G.brief: Town in the hill country of Judah
Shamir@Jos.15.48=H8069G.short: Shamir was a town in the hill country of Judah (Josh. 15:48).

Shaphir@Mic.1.11=H8208.short: Shaphir was a town mentioned in Micah's prophecy, urged to pass on in nakedness and shame (Mic. 1:11).

Sharon@1Ch.27.29-Act=H8289I.brief: Coastal plain known for its beauty and fertility
Sharon@1Ch.27.29-Act=H8289I.short: Sharon was a coastal plain known for its beauty, fertility, and pastureland (1Chr. 27:29; Sng.2.1; Isa. 33:9; 35:2; 65:10; Act.9.35).

Sharon@1Ch.5.16=H8289H.brief: Region where Gadites pastured their flocks
Sharon@1Ch.5.16=H8289H.short: Sharon was a region east of the Jordan where the Gadites pastured their flocks (1Chr. 5:16).

Sharuhen@Jos.15.32-1Ch=H8287.brief: Town allotted to Simeon within Judah's territory
Sharuhen@Jos.15.32-1Ch=H8287.short: Sharuhen, also called Shaaraim or Shilhim, was a town allotted to the tribe of Simeon within Judah's territory (Josh. 19:6; 1Chr. 4:31; Josh. 15:32).

Shaveh@Gen.14.5-=H7740.brief: Valley where Chedorlaomer defeated the Emites
Shaveh@Gen.14.5-=H7740.short: Shaveh Kiriathaim was a valley where Chedorlaomer and his allies defeated the Emites before battling the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah (Gen. 14:5, 17).

Sheba@1Ki.10.1-Luk=H7614J.brief: Kingdom known for wealth, trade, and the Queen of Sheba
Sheba@1Ki.10.1-Luk=H7614J.short: Sheba, also referred to as the South, was a kingdom known for its wealth, trade, and the visit of its queen to King Solomon (1Ki. 10:1-13; 2Chr. 9:1-12; Ps. 72:10, 15; Isa. 60:6; Jer. 6:20; Ezek. 27:22-23; 38:13; Luke 11:31).

Shebarim@Jos.7.5=H7671.brief: Place near Ai where Israelites fled
Shebarim@Jos.7.5=H7671.short: Shebarim was a place near Ai where the Israelites fled after being defeated due to Achan's sin (Josh. 7:5).

Shechem@Gen.12.6-Act=H7927G.brief: City in Canaan, later allotted to Ephraim
Shechem@Gen.12.6-Act=H7927G.short: Shechem was a prominent city in Canaan, later allotted to the tribe of Ephraim, and the site of important events in Israel's history (Gen. 12:6; 33:18-20; Josh. 20:7; 24:1, 25-26; Judg. 9; 1Ki. 12:1, 25; Ps. 60:6; 108:7; Act.7.16).

Sheep_Gate@Neh.3.1-Jhn=H6629H.brief: Gate in Jerusalem near the sheep market
Sheep_Gate@Neh.3.1-Jhn=H6629H.short: The Sheep Gate was a gate in Jerusalem's wall, likely near the sheep market, that was rebuilt during Nehemiah's time (Neh. 3:1, 32; 12:39; Jhn.5.2).

Shelah@Neh.2.14-Jhn=H7975A.short: Shelah, also called Shiloah, the King's Pool, or Siloam, was a pool in Jerusalem fed by the Gihon Spring via Hezekiah's Tunnel (Neh. 3:15; Isa. 8:6; Neh. 2:14; Luke 13:4; Jhn.9.7, 11).

Shema@Jos.15.26=H8090.brief: Town in the Negev region of Judah
Shema@Jos.15.26=H8090.short: Shema was a town in the Negev region of Judah (Josh. 15:26).

Shen@1Sa.7.12=H8129.brief: Place where Samuel set up the Ebenezer stone
Shen@1Sa.7.12=H8129.short: Shen was the place where Samuel set up the Ebenezer stone to commemorate the Israelites' victory over the Philistines (1Sam. 7:12).

Shepham@Num.34.10-=H8221.brief: Landmark on the northeastern border of the Promised Land
Shepham@Num.34.10-=H8221.short: Shepham was a landmark on the northeastern border of the Promised Land, between Hazar-enan and Riblah (Num. 34:10-11).

Shephelah@Deu.1.7-Zec=H8219.brief: Lowland region between Judean hills and coastal plain
Shephelah@Deu.1.7-Zec=H8219.short: The Shephelah was the lowland region between the Judean hills and the coastal plain, known for its fertile valleys and strategic importance (Josh. 9:1; 10:40; 2Chr. 28:18; Jer. 17:26; 32:44; 33:13).

Shepher_Mount@Num.33.23-=H8234.short: Mount Shepher was a place where the Israelites camped during their wilderness wanderings between Kehelathah and Haradah (Num. 33:23-24).

Shihor-libnath@Jos.19.26=H7884.short: Shihor-libnath was a place that marked the boundary of the territory allotted to the tribe of Asher (Josh. 19:26).

Shikkeron@Jos.15.11=H7942.brief: Town on the border of Judah
Shikkeron@Jos.15.11=H7942.short: Shikkeron was a town on the northern border of Judah's territory, near Mount Baalah (Josh. 15:11).

Shiloh@Jos.18.1-Jer=H7887.brief: Israelite sanctuary and assembly point during the judges' period
Shiloh@Jos.18.1-Jer=H7887.short: Shiloh was an important Israelite sanctuary and assembly point during the period of the judges, where the tabernacle was set up and the land was allotted to the tribes (Josh. 18:1, 8-10; 1Sam. 1:3, 9, 24; 2:14; 3:21; Jer. 7:12, 14).

Shimron@Jos.11.1-=H8110A.brief: Canaanite city conquered by Joshua, allotted to Zebulun
Shimron@Jos.11.1-=H8110A.short: Shimron, also called Shimron-meron, was a Canaanite city conquered by Joshua (Josh. 11:1; 12:20) and later allotted to the tribe of Zebulun (Josh. 19:15).

Shinar@Gen.10.10-Zec=H8152.brief: Ancient region in Mesopotamia, associated with Babylon
Shinar@Gen.10.10-Zec=H8152.short: Shinar was an ancient region in Mesopotamia, associated with the cities of Babylon and Uruk, and the site of the Tower of Babel (Gen. 10:10; 11:2; 14:1, 9; Josh. 7:21; Isa. 11:11; Dan. 1:2; Zech. 5:11).

Shion@Jos.19.19=H7866.brief: Town in the territory of Issachar
Shion@Jos.19.19=H7866.short: Shion was a town allotted to the tribe of Issachar, mentioned along with Shunem, Hapharaim, and Anaharath (Josh. 19:19).

Shittim@Num.25.1-Mic=H7851G.brief: The last Israelite campsite before crossing the Jordan.
Shittim@Num.25.1-Mic=H7851G.short: Shittim, also called Abel-shittim, the final Israelite encampment before entering Canaan.

Shittim_Valley@Jol.3.18=H7851H.short: The Shittim Valley is mentioned in Joel's prophecy as a place where water will flow when God restores Judah's fortunes (Jol.3.18).

Shoa@Ezk.23.23=H7772.brief: People group mentioned in Ezekiel's prophecy
Shoa@Ezk.23.23=H7772.short: Shoa was a people group mentioned along with the Babylonians, Chaldeans, and Assyrians in Ezekiel's prophecy against Jerusalem (Ezek. 23:23).

Shual@1Sa.13.17=H7777A.brief: Region raided by Philistines during Saul's reign
Shual@1Sa.13.17=H7777A.short: Shual was a region raided by Philistine raiders during Saul's reign, along with Ophrah and the land of Shaalim (1Sam. 13:17).

Shunem@Jos.19.18-2Ki=H7766.brief: Town in Issachar; home of the Shunammite woman
Shunem@Jos.19.18-2Ki=H7766.short: Shunem was a town allotted to the tribe of Issachar (Josh. 19:18), known for being the home of the Shunammite woman who hosted Elisha (2Ki. 4:8) and where the Philistines camped before battling Saul (1Sam. 28:4).

Shur@Gen.16.7-1Sa=H7793.brief: Wilderness area between Canaan and Egypt
Shur@Gen.16.7-1Sa=H7793.short: Shur was a wilderness area between Canaan and Egypt, mentioned in connection with Hagar (Gen. 16:7), Abraham (Gen. 20:1; 25:18), the Israelites' wanderings (Exod. 15:22), and Saul's battles (1Sam. 15:7; 27:8).

Sibmah@Num.32.38-Jer=H7643H.brief: Moabite town known for its vineyards
Sibmah@Num.32.38-Jer=H7643H.short: Sibmah was a Moabite town known for its vineyards, allotted to the tribe of Reuben (Num. 32:38; Josh. 13:19) and later mentioned in prophecies concerning Moab (Isa. 16:8-9; Jer. 48:32).

Sibraim@Ezk.47.16=H5453.brief: Landmark on the northeastern border of the Promised Land
Sibraim@Ezk.47.16=H5453.short: Sibraim was a place mentioned by Ezekiel as a landmark on the northeastern border of the Promised Land, between the territory of Damascus and that of Hamath (Ezek. 47:16).

Siddim_Valley@Gen.14.3-=H7708.brief: Valley near the Dead Sea; site of battle
Siddim_Valley@Gen.14.3-=H7708.short: The Valley of Siddim, located near the Dead Sea, was the site of a battle between the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah and the kings of Elam and their allies (Gen. 14:3, 8, 10).

Sidon@Gen.10.19-Act=H6721H.short: Sidon, also called Great Sidon, was a prominent Phoenician city known for its trade and culture, and was the hometown of Jezebel, wife of King Ahab (1Ki. 16:31). It is mentioned in various contexts throughout the Bible, including the Old Testament (Gen. 10:19; Josh. 11:8; Judg. 10:6; Isa. 23:2-4; Jer. 27:3; Ezek. 28:21-22) and the New Testament (Matt. 11:21-22; Luke 4:26; Act.27.3).

Silla@2Ki.12.20=H5538.brief: Place where King Joash was assassinated
Silla@2Ki.12.20=H5538.short: Silla was the place where King Joash of Judah was assassinated by his servants (2Ki. 12:20).

Sin@Exo.16.1-Num=H5512B.brief: Wilderness area between Elim and Sinai
Sin@Exo.16.1-Num=H5512B.short: Sin was a wilderness area between Elim and Sinai where the Israelites camped during their journey from Egypt to the Promised Land (Exod. 16:1; 17:1; Num. 33:11-12).

Sinai@Exo.3.1-Gal=H5514G.brief: Mountain where Moses received the Ten Commandments
Sinai@Exo.3.1-Gal=H5514G.short: Sinai, also called Mount Sinai, Horeb, or Mount Horeb, was the mountain where God gave Moses the Ten Commandments and other laws (Exod. 19-40; Lev. 7:38; 25:1; 26:46; 27:34; Num. 3:1; 28:6; Deut. 33:2; Judg. 5:5; Ps. 68:8, 17; Neh. 9:13; Mal. 4:4; Act.7.30, 38; Gal. 4:24-25).

Sinai_Wilderness@Exo.19.1-Num=H4057G.brief: Wilderness where Israel camped after leaving Egypt
Sinai_Wilderness@Exo.19.1-Num=H4057G.short: The Sinai Wilderness was the region where the Israelites camped after the Exodus and received the Law.

Siphmoth@1Sa.30.28=H8224.brief: Town in southern Judah that received spoils from David
Siphmoth@1Sa.30.28=H8224.short: Siphmoth was one of the towns in southern Judah that received a share of the spoils from David after he defeated the Amalekites (1Sam. 30:28).

Sirah@2Sa.3.26=H5626.brief: Place near Hebron where Abner was killed by Joab
Sirah@2Sa.3.26=H5626.short: Sirah, also called the Cistern of Sirah, was a place near Hebron where Joab killed Abner in revenge for the death of his brother Asahel (2Sam. 3:26).

Sitnah@Gen.26.21=H7856.brief: Well dug by Isaac, disputed by Philistines
Sitnah@Gen.26.21=H7856.short: Sitnah was a well dug by Isaac in the Valley of Gerar, but the Philistines disputed its ownership (Gen. 26:21).

Smyrna@Rev.1.11-=G4667.brief: One of the seven churches of Asia Minor
Smyrna@Rev.1.11-=G4667.short: Smyrna was one of the seven churches of Asia Minor addressed in the Book of Revelation, known for its persecution and poverty, yet faithful to Christ (Rev. 1:11; 2:8-11).

Socoh@Jos.15.35-2Ch=H7755G.brief: Town in Judah; site of David's battle with Goliath
Socoh@Jos.15.35-2Ch=H7755G.short: Socoh was a town in the Shephelah region of Judah (Josh. 15:35), known for being near the site of David's battle with Goliath (1Sam. 17:1) and later fortified by Rehoboam (2Chr. 11:7).

Socoh@Jos.15.48=H7755H.brief: A town in the hill country of Judah
Socoh@Jos.15.48=H7755H.short: Socoh, a town allotted to the tribe of Judah in the hill country (Jos. 15:48).

Sodom@Gen.10.19-Rev=H5467.brief: Wicked city destroyed by God for its sins
Sodom@Gen.10.19-Rev=H5467.short: Sodom, a notoriously wicked city destroyed by God along with Gomorrah for their grave sins (Gen. 19:24-25).

Solomon's_Portico@Act.3.11-=G4672H.brief: Colonnade in Jerusalem's temple where apostles taught
Solomon's_Portico@Act.3.11-=G4672H.short: Solomon's Portico, a colonnade in the Jerusalem temple where the apostles gathered to teach (Act.3.11; 5:12).

Sorek_Valley@Jdg.16.4=H7796.brief: Valley where Delilah lived, Samson's downfall occurred
Sorek_Valley@Jdg.16.4=H7796.short: Sorek Valley, the place where Delilah lived and where Samson's downfall began (Judg. 16:4).

Spain@Rom.15.24-=G4681.brief: Country Paul intended to visit to preach gospel
Spain@Rom.15.24-=G4681.short: Spain, a country Paul planned to visit to preach the gospel (Rom. 15:24, 28).

Straight@Act.9.11=G2117.brief: Street in Damascus where Saul stayed after conversion
Straight@Act.9.11=G2117.short: Straight, a street in Damascus where Saul stayed in the house of Judas after his conversion (Act.9.11).

Succoth@Exo.12.37-Num=H5523H.brief: First Israelite campsite after leaving Egypt during Exodus
Succoth@Exo.12.37-Num=H5523H.short: Succoth, the first place the Israelites camped after leaving Egypt during the Exodus (Exod. 12:37; Num. 33:5).

Succoth@Gen.33.17-Psa=H5523G.brief: City in Canaan, location of Solomon's bronze works
Succoth@Gen.33.17-Psa=H5523G.short: Succoth, a city in Canaan allocated to the tribe of Gad, later the site of Solomon's bronze works (Gen. 33:17; Josh. 13:27; 1Kgs. 7:46).

Suph@Deu.1.1=H5489.brief: Place near where Moses spoke to Israel
Suph@Deu.1.1=H5489.short: Suph, a place near the wilderness where Moses spoke to the Israelites (Deut. 1:1).

Suphah@Num.21.14=H5492B.brief: Place mentioned in the Book of the Wars of the Lord
Suphah@Num.21.14=H5492B.short: Suphah, a place mentioned in the Book of the Wars of the Lord (Num. 21:14).

Sur@2Ki.11.6=H5495.brief: Gate of the temple in Jerusalem
Sur@2Ki.11.6=H5495.short: Sur, a gate of the temple in Jerusalem, possibly referring to the Foundation Gate (2Kgs. 11:6).

Susa@Ezr.4.9-Dan=H7800.brief: Capital city of the Persian Empire
Susa@Ezr.4.9-Dan=H7800.short: Susa, the capital city of the Persian Empire, where Esther lived and the events of her book took place (Esth. 1:2; Dan. 8:2).

Sychar@Jhn.4.5=G4965.short: Sychar, a Samaritan city near Jacob's well, where Jesus spoke with a Samaritan woman (Jhn.4.5).

Syene@Isa.49.12-Ezk=H5482.brief: Southern border of Egypt, modern-day Aswan
Syene@Isa.49.12-Ezk=H5482.short: Syene, the southern border of Egypt, mentioned in prophecies about Egypt's destruction (Ezek. 29:10; 30:6).

Syracuse@Act.28.12=G4946.brief: City in Sicily where Paul's ship stopped
Syracuse@Act.28.12=G4946.short: Syracuse, a city on the island of Sicily where Paul's ship stopped for three days on his journey to Rome (Act.28.12).

Syria@Jdg.10.6-Gal=H0758I.brief: Ancient region north of Israel, often in conflict
Syria@Jdg.10.6-Gal=H0758I.short: Syria, an ancient region north of Israel, often engaged in conflicts with Israel and Judah (1Kgs. 20:1; 2Kgs. 13:3).

Syrtis@Act.27.17=G4950.brief: Dangerous shallow waters off the coast of Libya
Syrtis@Act.27.17=G4950.short: Syrtis, a dangerous area of shallow waters off the coast of Libya, feared by sailors (Act.27.17).

Taanach@Jos.12.21-1Ch=H8590.brief: Canaanite city allotted to Manasseh, later a Levitical city
Taanach@Jos.12.21-1Ch=H8590.short: Taanach, a Canaanite city allotted to the tribe of Manasseh, later designated as a Levitical city (Josh. 12:21; 17:11; 21:25).

Taanath-shiloh@Jos.16.6=H8387.brief: Landmark on the border of Ephraim's territory
Taanath-shiloh@Jos.16.6=H8387.short: Taanath-shiloh, a landmark on the eastern border of the territory allotted to the tribe of Ephraim (Josh. 16:6).

Tabbath@Jdg.7.22=H2888.brief: Place near where Midianites fled from Gideon
Tabbath@Jdg.7.22=H2888.short: Tabbath, a place near the Jordan River where the Midianites fled after being defeated by Gideon (Judg. 7:22).

Taberah@Num.11.3-Deu=H8404.brief: Israelite camp where God sent fire as judgment
Taberah@Num.11.3-Deu=H8404.short: Taberah, a place where the Israelites camped and experienced God's judgment by fire for their complaints (Num. 11:3; Deut. 9:22).

Tabor@1Sa.10.3=H8396H.brief: Oak tree near Bethel, mentioned in Samuel's prophecy
Tabor@1Sa.10.3=H8396H.short: Tabor, an oak tree near Bethel, mentioned in Samuel's prophetic message to Saul (1Sam. 10:3).

Tabor_Mount@Jos.19.22-Hos=H8396G.brief: Mountain in Israel, site of Deborah and Barak's victory
Tabor_Mount@Jos.19.22-Hos=H8396G.short: Mount Tabor, a mountain in Israel, known for the gathering of Deborah and Barak's forces and their victory over Sisera (Judg. 4:6, 12, 14).

Tadmor@1Ki.9.18-2Ch=H8412.brief: City built by Solomon in the wilderness
Tadmor@1Ki.9.18-2Ch=H8412.short: Tadmor (or Tamar), a city built by Solomon in the wilderness, possibly the later site of Palmyra (1Kgs. 9:18; 2Chr. 8:4).

Tahath@Num.33.26-=H8480G.brief: Israelite campsite during the wilderness journey
Tahath@Num.33.26-=H8480G.short: Tahath, a place where the Israelites camped during their wilderness journey (Num. 33:26-27).

Tahpanhes@Jer.2.16-Ezk=H8471.brief: Egyptian city where Jewish refugees fled after Jerusalem's destruction
Tahpanhes@Jer.2.16-Ezk=H8471.short: Tahpanhes (or Tehaphnehes), an Egyptian city where Jewish refugees, including Jeremiah, settled after the destruction of Jerusalem (Jer. 43:7-9; 44:1; 46:14; Ezek. 30:18).

Tamar@Ezk.47.18-=H8559J.brief: Landmark on the southeastern border of Israel
Tamar@Ezk.47.18-=H8559J.short: Tamar, a place mentioned as a landmark on the southeastern border of the Promised Land (Ezek. 47:18-19; 48:28).

Tappuah@Jos.12.17-=H8599B.brief: Canaanite city allotted to Ephraim and Manasseh
Tappuah@Jos.12.17-=H8599B.short: Tappuah (or En-tappuah), a Canaanite city on the border between Ephraim and Manasseh, allotted to Manasseh but with land belonging to Ephraim (Josh. 16:8; 17:7-8).

Tappuah@Jos.15.34=H8599G.short: Tappuah, a town in the Shephelah (lowlands) of Judah (Josh. 15:34).

Taralah@Jos.18.27=H8634.brief: Town allotted to the tribe of Benjamin
Taralah@Jos.18.27=H8634.short: Taralah, a town allotted to the tribe of Benjamin (Josh. 18:27).

Tarshish@1Ki.10.22-Jon=H8659H.brief: Distant maritime city known for its wealth and trade
Tarshish@1Ki.10.22-Jon=H8659H.short: Tarshish, a distant maritime city known for its ships, wealth, and trade, possibly located in southern Spain (1Kgs. 10:22; Isa. 23:1; Jonah 1:3).

Tarsus@Act.9.11-=G5019.brief: City in Cilicia, birthplace of the apostle Paul
Tarsus@Act.9.11-=G5019.short: Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, known as the birthplace and early residence of the apostle Paul (Act.9.11, 30; 21:39; 22:3).

Tekoa@2Sa.14.2-Amo=H8620.brief: Town in Judah, home of the prophet Amos
Tekoa@2Sa.14.2-Amo=H8620.short: Tekoa, a town in Judah, known as the birthplace of the prophet Amos and the home of one of David's mighty men (2Sam. 14:2; 1Chr. 11:28; Amo.1.1).

Tel-abib@Ezk.3.15=H8512.brief: Settlement of exiled Jews in Babylonia
Tel-abib@Ezk.3.15=H8512.short: Tel-abib, a settlement of exiled Jews by the Chebar River in Babylonia, where the prophet Ezekiel lived (Ezek. 3:15).

Telaim@1Sa.15.4=H2923.brief: Place where Saul gathered his army
Telaim@1Sa.15.4=H2923.short: Telaim, a place where Saul gathered his army before attacking the Amalekites (1Sam. 15:4).

Telassar@2Ki.19.12-Isa=H8515.brief: Mesopotamian city conquered by the Assyrians
Telassar@2Ki.19.12-Isa=H8515.short: Telassar, a Mesopotamian city conquered by the Assyrians, mentioned in the context of Sennacherib's boasting (2Kgs. 19:12; Isa. 37:12).

Telem@Jos.15.24=H2928G.brief: Town in the Negev region of Judah
Telem@Jos.15.24=H2928G.short: Telem, a town in the Negev region of Judah, allotted to the tribe of Judah (Josh. 15:24).

Tel-harsha@Ezr.2.59-Neh=H8521.brief: Babylonian city from which exiles returned
Tel-harsha@Ezr.2.59-Neh=H8521.short: Tel-harsha, a Babylonian city from which some Jewish exiles returned to Jerusalem, but could not prove their genealogy (Ezra 2:59; Neh. 7:61).

Tel-melah@Ezr.2.59-Neh=H8528.brief: Babylonian city from which exiles returned
Tel-melah@Ezr.2.59-Neh=H8528.short: Tel-melah, a Babylonian city from which some Jewish exiles returned to Jerusalem, but could not prove their genealogy (Ezra 2:59; Neh. 7:61).

Tema@Job.6.19-Jer=H8485H.brief: Arabian city and tribe known for trade
Tema@Job.6.19-Jer=H8485H.short: Tema, an Arabian city and tribe known for its caravans and trade, mentioned in prophetic and poetic texts (Job.6.19; Isa. 21:14; Jer. 25:23).

Teman@Jer.49.7-Hab=H8487H.brief: Region and town in Edom, known for wisdom
Teman@Jer.49.7-Hab=H8487H.short: Teman, a region and town in Edom, named after Esau's grandson, known for its wisdom (Jer. 49:7; Amo.1.12; Obad. 1:9).

Terah@Num.33.27-=H8646H.brief: Israelite campsite during the wilderness journey
Terah@Num.33.27-=H8646H.short: Terah, a place where the Israelites camped during their wilderness journey (Num. 33:27-28).

Thebes@Jer.46.25-Nam=H4996.brief: Ancient Egyptian city, known for its wealth and power
Thebes@Jer.46.25-Nam=H4996.short: Thebes, an ancient Egyptian city, known for its wealth and power, mentioned in prophecies of judgment against Egypt (Jer. 46:25; Ezek. 30:14-16; Nah. 3:8).

Thebez@Jdg.9.50-2Sa=H8405.brief: Canaanite city where Abimelech was killed
Thebez@Jdg.9.50-2Sa=H8405.short: Thebez, a Canaanite city where Abimelech was fatally wounded by a millstone thrown by a woman (Judg. 9:50-54; 2Sam. 11:21).

Thessalonica@Act.17.1-2Ti=G2332.brief: Macedonian city, site of an early Christian church
Thessalonica@Act.17.1-2Ti=G2332.short: Thessalonica, a prominent city in Macedonia, where Paul established a church and wrote two epistles to the believers (Act.17.1-9; 1Thess. 1:1; 2Thess. 1:1).

Three_Taverns@Act.28.15=G5140.brief: Staging post on the Appian Way near Rome
Three_Taverns@Act.28.15=G5140.short: Three Taverns, a staging post on the Appian Way, about 33 miles from Rome, where Paul was met by Roman Christians (Act.28.15).

Thyatira@Act.16.14-Rev=G2363.brief: City in Asia Minor, home of the prophet Lydia
Thyatira@Act.16.14-Rev=G2363.short: Thyatira, a city in Asia Minor, known for its dyeing industry and the home of Lydia, a convert of Paul (Act.16.14; Rev. 1:11; 2:18, 24).

Tibhath@1Ch.18.8=H2880.brief: City from which David took bronze for the Temple
Tibhath@1Ch.18.8=H2880.short: Tibhath, a city from which David took a large amount of bronze, used in the construction of the Temple (1Chr. 18:8).

Tigris@Gen.2.14-Dan=H2313.brief: River flowing from Eden, mentioned in Daniel's vision
Tigris@Gen.2.14-Dan=H2313.short: Tigris, one of the rivers flowing from the Garden of Eden (Gen. 2:14), and the location of Daniel's vision (Dan. 10:4).

Timnah@Gen.38.12-2Ch=H8553G.brief: Canaanite city associated with Judah and Dan
Timnah@Gen.38.12-2Ch=H8553G.short: Timnah, a Canaanite city on the border between Judah and Dan, associated with Judah's son Er and Samson (Gen. 38:12-14; Josh. 15:10; 19:43; Judg. 14:1-5).

Timnah@Jos.15.57=H8553H.brief: Town in the hill country of Judah
Timnah@Jos.15.57=H8553H.short: Timnah, a town in the hill country of Judah (Josh. 15:57).

Timnath-heres@Jos.19.50-Jdg=H8556A.brief: Town allotted to Joshua, where he was buried
Timnath-heres@Jos.19.50-Jdg=H8556A.short: Timnath-heres (or Timnath-serah), a town in the hill country of Ephraim, allotted to Joshua, where he was buried (Josh. 19:50; 24:30; Judg. 2:9).

Tiphsah@1Ki.4.24=H8607G.brief: City on the Euphrates, extent of Solomon's kingdom
Tiphsah@1Ki.4.24=H8607G.short: Tiphsah, a city on the Euphrates River, marking the extent of Solomon's kingdom (1Kgs. 4:24).

Tiphsah@2Ki.15.16=H8607H.brief: City attacked by King Menahem of Israel
Tiphsah@2Ki.15.16=H8607H.short: Tiphsah, a city attacked and brutally conquered by Menahem, king of Israel (2Kgs. 15:16).

Tirzah@Jos.12.24-Sng=H8656H.brief: Canaanite city that became the capital of Israel
Tirzah@Jos.12.24-Sng=H8656H.short: Tirzah, a Canaanite city captured by Joshua, later served as the capital of the northern kingdom of Israel before Samaria (Josh. 12:24; 1Kgs. 14:17; 15:21, 33; 16:6-23).

Tishbe@1Ki.17.1-2Ki=H8453B.short: Tishbe (or Tishbite), the hometown of the prophet Elijah, located in Gilead (1Kgs. 17:1; 21:17, 28; 2Kgs. 1:3, 8; 9:36).

Tob@Jdg.11.3-2Sa=H2897.brief: Region where Jephthah fled and recruited mercenaries
Tob@Jdg.11.3-2Sa=H2897.short: Tob (or Ish-tob), a region east of the Jordan River where Jephthah fled and later recruited mercenaries to fight the Ammonites (Judg. 11:3, 5; 2Sam. 10:6, 8).

Tochen@1Ch.4.32=H8507.brief: Town in the territory of Simeon
Tochen@1Ch.4.32=H8507.short: Tochen, a town allotted to the tribe of Simeon (1Chr. 4:32).

Tolad@1Ch.4.29=H8434.brief: Town in the territory of Simeon
Tolad@1Ch.4.29=H8434.short: Tolad, a town allotted to the tribe of Simeon (1Chr. 4:29).

Tophel@Deu.1.1=H8603.brief: A place near where Moses addressed the Israelites
Tophel@Deu.1.1=H8603.short: Tophel, a location mentioned in Moses' speech to the Israelites, possibly near modern-day et-Tafeleh, southeast of the Dead Sea (Deut. 1:1).

Topheth@Jos.15.8-Jer=H8612.brief: Site of pagan child sacrifice, south of Jerusalem
Topheth@Jos.15.8-Jer=H8612.short: Topheth, located in the Valley of Hinnom (also called the Valley of Slaughter or Baca Valley) south of Jerusalem, was a site of pagan child sacrifice that was defiled by King Josiah (2Ki.23.10; Jer.7.31-32; 19:2, 6, 11-14; 32:35; Isa.30.33).

Tower_of_Eder@Gen.35.21-Mic=H4029.brief: A tower near Bethlehem, associated with the Messiah
Tower_of_Eder@Gen.35.21-Mic=H4029.short: The Tower of Eder, a watchtower near Bethlehem, where Jacob pitched his tent and later associated with the coming of the Messiah (Gen. 35:21; Mic. 4:8).

Tower_of_Hananel@Neh.3.1-Zec=H2606.brief: A tower in Jerusalem's wall, rebuilt by Nehemiah
Tower_of_Hananel@Neh.3.1-Zec=H2606.short: The Tower of Hananel, a tower in Jerusalem's wall, rebuilt by Nehemiah and mentioned in prophetic visions of the city's restoration (Neh. 3:1; 12:39; Jer. 31:38; Zech. 14:10).

Tower_of_the_Hundred@Neh.3.1-=H4026H.brief: A tower in Jerusalem's wall, rebuilt by Nehemiah
Tower_of_the_Hundred@Neh.3.1-=H4026H.short: The Tower of the Hundred, a tower in Jerusalem's wall, rebuilt during Nehemiah's restoration of the city (Neh. 3:1; 12:39).

Tower_of_the_Ovens@Neh.3.11-=H4026I.brief: A tower in Jerusalem's wall, rebuilt by Nehemiah
Tower_of_the_Ovens@Neh.3.11-=H4026I.short: The Tower of the Ovens, a tower in Jerusalem's wall, rebuilt during Nehemiah's restoration of the city (Neh. 3:11; 12:38).

Trachonitis@Luk.3.1=G5139.brief: A rugged region northeast of the Jordan River
Trachonitis@Luk.3.1=G5139.short: Trachonitis, a rugged, rocky region northeast of the Jordan River, part of Philip's tetrarchy during the time of John the Baptist (Luke 3:1).

Travelers_Valley@Ezk.39.11=H1516O.brief: A valley where Gog's army will be buried
Travelers_Valley@Ezk.39.11=H1516O.short: The Valley of the Travelers, a location where the army of Gog will be buried after their defeat, blocking the path of travelers (Ezek. 39:11).

Troas@Act.16.8-2Ti=G5174.brief: A city in Asia Minor, visited by Paul
Troas@Act.16.8-2Ti=G5174.short: Troas, a city in Asia Minor, where Paul had a vision of a man urging him to come to Macedonia, and where he later preached and raised Eutychus from the dead (Act.16.8-11; 20:5-12; 2Cor. 2:12; 2Tim. 4:13).

Trogyllium@Act.20.15=G5175.brief: A city near Ephesus, visited by Paul
Trogyllium@Act.20.15=G5175.short: Trogyllium, a coastal town near Ephesus, where Paul's ship anchored during his journey to Jerusalem (Act.20.15).

Tubal@Isa.66.19-Ezk=H8422H.brief: A nation, descendant of Japheth, known for trading
Tubal@Isa.66.19-Ezk=H8422H.short: Tubal, a nation descended from Japheth, known for trading in slaves and bronze, and allied with Gog in the prophecy of Ezekiel (Gen. 10:2; Isa. 66:19; Ezek. 27:13; 38:2-3; 39:1).

Tyre@Jos.19.29-Act=H6865.brief: A major Phoenician port city, known for its trade
Tyre@Jos.19.29-Act=H6865.short: Tyre, a prominent Phoenician port city, known for its wealth, trade, and craftsmanship, often mentioned in the context of judgment and prophecy (Josh. 19:29; 2Sam. 5:11; 1Kgs. 5:1; Isa. 23:1-17; Ezek. 26-28; Matt. 11:21-22; Act.12.20).

Ulai@Dan.8.2-=H0195.brief: A river in Elam, near where Daniel saw a vision
Ulai@Dan.8.2-=H0195.short: Ulai, a river in Elam, near Susa, where Daniel received a vision of a ram and a goat (Dan. 8:2, 16).

Ummah@Jos.19.30=H5981.brief: A town allotted to the tribe of Asher
Ummah@Jos.19.30=H5981.short: Ummah, a town allotted to the tribe of Asher in the division of the Promised Land (Josh. 19:30).

Uphaz@Jer.10.9-Dan=H0210.brief: A place known for its fine gold
Uphaz@Jer.10.9-Dan=H0210.short: Uphaz, a place mentioned in the Bible, known for its high-quality gold (Jer. 10:9; Dan. 10:5).

Ur@Gen.11.28-Neh=H0218B.brief: The hometown of Abraham in Mesopotamia
Ur@Gen.11.28-Neh=H0218B.short: Ur of the Chaldeans, the hometown of Abraham in Mesopotamia, from where God called him to go to the land of Canaan (Gen. 11:28, 31; 15:7; Neh. 9:7).

Uz@Job.1.1-Lam=H5780J.brief: A region associated with Job, Edom, and Arabia
Uz@Job.1.1-Lam=H5780J.short: Uz, a region mentioned in the Bible as the homeland of Job, possibly located in Edom or Arabia (Job.1.1; Jer. 25:20; Lam. 4:21).

Uzal@Ezk.27.19=H0187H.brief: A place mentioned in Ezekiel's prophecy
Uzal@Ezk.27.19=H0187H.short: Uzal, a place mentioned in Ezekiel's prophecy, possibly referring to a region in Arabia known for its high-quality swords (Ezek. 27:19).

Uzza@2Ki.21.18-=H1588G.brief: A garden where Manasseh and Amon were buried
Uzza@2Ki.21.18-=H1588G.short: Uzza, a garden in Jerusalem where Manasseh and his son Amon, kings of Judah, were buried (2Kgs. 21:18, 26).

Uzzen-sheerah@1Ch.7.24=H0242.brief: A town built by Sheerah, daughter of Ephraim
Uzzen-sheerah@1Ch.7.24=H0242.short: Uzzen-sheerah, a town built by Sheerah, the daughter of Ephraim, along with the towns of Upper and Lower Beth-horon (1Chr. 7:24).

Valley_Gate@2Ch.26.9-Neh=H1516M.brief: A gate in Jerusalem's wall, rebuilt by Nehemiah
Valley_Gate@2Ch.26.9-Neh=H1516M.short: The Valley Gate, one of the gates in Jerusalem's wall, rebuilt by Nehemiah and mentioned in connection with King Uzziah's fortifications (2Chr. 26:9; Neh. 2:13, 15; 3:13).

Vedan@Ezk.27.19=H2051.brief: A place mentioned in Ezekiel's prophecy
Vedan@Ezk.27.19=H2051.short: Vedan, a place of uncertain location, mentioned in Ezekiel's prophecy as trading with Tyre (Ezek. 27:19).

Waheb@Num.21.14=H2052.brief: A place mentioned in the Book of Numbers
Waheb@Num.21.14=H2052.short: Waheb, a place mentioned in the Book of Numbers, possibly located in Moab (Num. 21:14).

Washer's_Field@2Ki.18.17-Isa=H3526G.brief: A location near Jerusalem's wall, mentioned in prophecies
Washer's_Field@2Ki.18.17-Isa=H3526G.short: The Washer's Field, a location near Jerusalem's wall, where the Assyrian officials stood and delivered messages to King Hezekiah (2Kgs. 18:17; Isa. 7:3; 36:2).

Water_Gate@Neh.3.26-=H4325H.brief: A gate in Jerusalem's wall, rebuilt by Nehemiah
Water_Gate@Neh.3.26-=H4325H.short: The Water Gate, one of the gates in Jerusalem's wall, rebuilt by Nehemiah and associated with the reading of the Law and the celebration of the Feast of Tabernacles (Neh. 3:26; 8:1, 3, 16; 12:37).

Way_of_Holiness@Isa.35.8=H1870H.brief: A prophesied highway for the redeemed in Isaiah
Way_of_Holiness@Isa.35.8=H1870H.short: The Way of Holiness, a prophesied highway in Isaiah, reserved for the redeemed and leading to Zion (Isa. 35:8).

Wildgoats_Rocks@1Sa.24.2=H3277G.brief: A place near En Gedi where David hid from Saul
Wildgoats_Rocks@1Sa.24.2=H3277G.short: Wildgoats Rocks, a rugged area near En Gedi where David hid from Saul and had the opportunity to spare the king's life (1Sam. 24:2).

Yeshanah_Gate@Neh.3.6-=H3465G.brief: A gate in Jerusalem's wall, rebuilt by Nehemiah
Yeshanah_Gate@Neh.3.6-=H3465G.short: The Yeshanah Gate, also known as the Old Gate, one of the gates in Jerusalem's wall rebuilt by Nehemiah (Neh. 3:6; 12:39).

Yiron@Jos.19.38=H3375.brief: A town allotted to the tribe of Naphtali
Yiron@Jos.19.38=H3375.short: Yiron, a town in the territory of Naphtali, mentioned in the list of cities allotted to the tribe during the division of the Promised Land (Josh. 19:38).

Zaanan@Mic.1.11=H6630.brief: A town mentioned in Micah's prophecy
Zaanan@Mic.1.11=H6630.short: Zaanan, a town mentioned in Micah's prophecy, possibly located in the Shephelah region of Judah (Mic. 1:11).

Zaanannim@Jos.19.33-Jdg=H6815.brief: A place near Kedesh in Naphtali
Zaanannim@Jos.19.33-Jdg=H6815.short: Zaanannim, a place near Kedesh in Naphtali, associated with the Kenites and mentioned in connection with the story of Deborah and Barak (Josh. 19:33; Judg. 4:11).

Zalmonah@Num.33.41-=H6758.brief: A place where the Israelites camped during their wilderness journey
Zalmonah@Num.33.41-=H6758.short: Zalmonah, a campsite of the Israelites during their wilderness journey, located between Mount Hor and Punon (Num. 33:41-42).

Zanoah@Jos.15.34-Neh=H2182G.brief: A town in the Judean lowlands allotted to Judah
Zanoah@Jos.15.34-Neh=H2182G.short: Zanoah, a town in the Judean lowlands allotted to Judah, whose inhabitants helped rebuild the Valley Gate during Nehemiah's time (Josh. 15:34; 1Chr. 4:18; Neh. 3:13; 11:30).

Zanoah@Jos.15.56=H2182H.brief: A town in the hill country of Judah
Zanoah@Jos.15.56=H2182H.short: Zanoah, a town in the hill country of Judah, mentioned in the list of cities allotted to the tribe (Josh. 15:56).

Zaphon@Jos.13.27-Isa=H6829.brief: A city in Gad and a term for the north
Zaphon@Jos.13.27-Isa=H6829.short: Zaphon, a city allotted to the tribe of Gad, also used as a term for the north or the heavenly dwelling place of God (Josh. 13:27; Judg. 12:1; Ps. 48:2; Isa. 14:13).

Zarephath@1Ki.17.9-Luk=H6886.brief: A Phoenician city where Elijah stayed with a widow
Zarephath@1Ki.17.9-Luk=H6886.short: Zarephath, a Phoenician city between Tyre and Sidon, where Elijah stayed with a widow during a famine and performed miracles (1Kgs. 17:9-10; Obad. 1:20; Luke 4:26).

Zarethan@Jos.3.16-2Ch=H6891.brief: A place near the Jordan River associated with Israel's crossing
Zarethan@Jos.3.16-2Ch=H6891.short: Zarethan, a place near Adam and the Jordan River, mentioned in connection with Israel's crossing and the casting of bronze implements for Solomon's Temple (Josh. 3:16; 1Kgs. 4:12; 7:46; 2Chr. 4:17; Judg. 7:22).

Zeboiim@Gen.10.19-Hos=H6636.brief: One of the cities of the plain destroyed with Sodom
Zeboiim@Gen.10.19-Hos=H6636.short: Zeboiim, one of the cities of the plain, along with Sodom and Gomorrah, that was destroyed by God due to its wickedness (Gen. 10:19; 14:2, 8; Deut. 29:23; Hos. 11:8).

Zeboim@Neh.11.34=H6650G.brief: A town resettled by the people of Judah after the exile
Zeboim@Neh.11.34=H6650G.short: Zeboim, a town resettled by the people of Judah after the Babylonian exile (Neh. 11:34).

Zeboim_Valley@1Sa.13.18=H6650H.brief: A valley mentioned in connection with Saul's military campaigns
Zeboim_Valley@1Sa.13.18=H6650H.short: The Valley of Zeboim, a location mentioned in the context of Saul's military campaigns against the Philistines (1Sam. 13:18).

Zedad@Num.34.8-Ezk=H6657.brief: A place on the northern border of the Promised Land
Zedad@Num.34.8-Ezk=H6657.short: Zedad, a place mentioned as part of the northern border of the Promised Land in both the Mosaic and Ezekiel's descriptions (Num. 34:8; Ezek. 47:15).

Zela@Jos.18.28-2Sa=H6762.brief: A city in Benjamin where Saul's family was buried
Zela@Jos.18.28-2Sa=H6762.short: Zela was a city in Benjamin where Saul and his family were buried.

Zelzah@1Sa.10.2=H6766.brief: A place near Rachel's tomb in Benjamin
Zelzah@1Sa.10.2=H6766.short: Zelzah was a place near Rachel's tomb in Benjamin that Samuel referenced when giving directions to Saul.

Zemaraim@Jos.18.22-2Ch=H6787.brief: A town in Benjamin; also a hill in Ephraim
Zemaraim@Jos.18.22-2Ch=H6787.short: Zemaraim was a town allotted to Benjamin (Jos.18.22). Mount Zemaraim in Ephraim was where Abijah addressed Jeroboam's army.

Zenan@Jos.15.37=H6799.brief: A town in the Judean lowlands
Zenan@Jos.15.37=H6799.short: Zenan was a town in the lowlands of Judah.

Zephath@Num.14.45-1Ch=H6857.brief: A Canaanite city captured by Judah and Simeon
Zephath@Num.14.45-1Ch=H6857.short: Zephath, later called Hormah, was a Canaanite city that Israel failed to capture but was later defeated by Judah and Simeon.

Zephathah_Valley@2Ch.14.10=H6859.brief: A valley where Asa defeated the Cushite army
Zephathah_Valley@2Ch.14.10=H6859.short: The Valley of Zephathah is where King Asa of Judah defeated Zerah the Cushite's large army.

Zer@Jos.19.35=H6863.short: Zer was a fortified city in the territory of Naphtali.

Zered@Num.21.12-Deu=H2218.brief: A brook marking the end of Israel's wilderness wanderings
Zered@Num.21.12-Deu=H2218.short: The Zered Brook marked the end of Israel's 38 years of wilderness wanderings until they crossed it to enter Moab.

Zeredah@1Ki.11.26=H6868G.brief: The hometown of Jeroboam, first king of Israel
Zeredah@1Ki.11.26=H6868G.short: Zeredah was the hometown of Jeroboam, who became the first king of the northern kingdom of Israel.

Zereth-shahar@Jos.13.19=H6890.brief: A city in Reuben's territory by the Dead Sea
Zereth-shahar@Jos.13.19=H6890.short: Zereth-shahar was a city in the territory of Reuben, located on a mountain in the plain by the Dead Sea.

Ziddim@Jos.19.35=H6661.short: Ziddim was a fortified city in the territory of Naphtali.

Ziklag@Jos.15.31-Neh=H6860.brief: A city given to David; originally Judah's, then Simeon's
Ziklag@Jos.15.31-Neh=H6860.short: Ziklag was a city allotted to Judah and Simeon that was later given to David by the Philistine king Achish.

Zimri@Jer.25.25=H2174B.brief: A nation mentioned in Jeremiah's prophecy against nations
Zimri@Jer.25.25=H2174B.short: Zimri was a nation mentioned in Jeremiah's prophecy of God's judgment against various nations.

Zin@Num.13.21-Jos=H6790.brief: A desert and wilderness region south of Judah
Zin@Num.13.21-Jos=H6790.short: The Wilderness of Zin was a desert region south of Judah where the Israelites encamped during their wilderness wanderings.

Zior@Jos.15.54=H6730.brief: A town in the hill country of Judah
Zior@Jos.15.54=H6730.short: Zior was a town in the hill country of Judah.

Ziph@Jos.15.24=H2128G.brief: A town in the Negev of Judah
Ziph@Jos.15.24=H2128G.short: Ziph was a town in the Negev region of Judah.

Ziph@Jos.15.55-Psa=H2128H.brief: A town in Judah where David hid from Saul
Ziph@Jos.15.55-Psa=H2128H.short: Ziph was a town in the hill country of Judah where David hid from Saul in the nearby wilderness.

Ziphron@Num.34.9=H2202.brief: A place on the northern border of the Promised Land
Ziphron@Num.34.9=H2202.short: Ziphron was a place on the northern border of the Promised Land.

Ziz@2Ch.20.16=H6732.brief: A pass where Jehoshaphat defeated Moab and Ammon
Ziz@2Ch.20.16=H6732.short: The Ascent of Ziz was a pass where Jehoshaphat defeated the armies of Moab and Ammon.

Zoan@Num.13.22-Ezk=H6814.brief: An ancient Egyptian city, probably Tanis
Zoan@Num.13.22-Ezk=H6814.short: Zoan was an ancient Egyptian city where God performed miracles through Moses; it is probably to be identified with Tanis.

Zoar@Gen.13.10-Jer=H6820.brief: A city near Sodom, spared from destruction
Zoar@Gen.13.10-Jer=H6820.short: Zoar, also known as Bela, was a small city near Sodom where Lot fled when God destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah.

Zobah@1Sa.14.47-2Ch=H6678G.brief: An Aramean kingdom, enemy of Israel during David's reign
Zobah@1Sa.14.47-2Ch=H6678G.short: Zobah was an Aramean kingdom northeast of Israel, conquered by David and later a source of opposition to Solomon.

Zophim@Num.23.14=H6839.brief: A place in Moab where Balaam blessed Israel
Zophim@Num.23.14=H6839.short: The field of Zophim was a place on the top of Pisgah in Moab where Balaam blessed Israel.

Zorah@Jos.15.33-Neh=H6881.brief: A town in the Shephelah, home of Samson
Zorah@Jos.15.33-Neh=H6881.short: Zorah was a town in the Shephelah region, originally allotted to Judah and later to Dan, and was the hometown of Samson.

Zuph@1Sa.9.5=H6689H.brief: A land where Saul searched for his father's donkeys
Zuph@1Sa.9.5=H6689H.short: The land of Zuph was a region in Ephraim where Saul and his servant searched for his father's lost donkeys.

Abaddon@Job.26.6=H0011.brief: The angel of the bottomless pit, meaning "destruction"
Abaddon@Job.26.6=H0011.short: Abaddon (Hebrew) or Apollyon (Greek), meaning "destruction" or "destroyer," is the name of the angel of the bottomless pit.

Abib@Exo.13.4-Est=H0024G.brief: The first month of the Hebrew religious calendar
Abib@Exo.13.4-Est=H0024G.short: Abib, later known as Nisan, was the first month of the Hebrew religious calendar, in which the Passover was celebrated.

Adar@Ezr.6.15-Est=H0143.brief: The twelfth month of the Hebrew religious calendar
Adar@Ezr.6.15-Est=H0143.short: Adar was the twelfth month of the Hebrew religious calendar, in which the feast of Purim was celebrated.

Alamoth@1Ch.15.20-Psa=H5961.brief: A musical term, possibly referring to a high pitch
Alamoth@1Ch.15.20-Psa=H5961.short: Alamoth is a musical term used in the superscriptions of some Psalms, possibly referring to a high pitch or a musical instrument.

Alpha@Rev.1.8-=G0001G.brief: A title of Jesus, signifying His eternal nature
Alpha@Rev.1.8-=G0001G.short: In Revelation 1:8, 21:6; 22:13, Jesus is referred to as "the Alpha and the Omega," a title that emphasizes His eternal nature and His role as the beginning and the end of all things.

Al-taschith@Psa.57.1-=H0516.brief: Musical or literary term in Psalms, meaning "Do Not Destroy"
Al-taschith@Psa.57.1-=H0516.short: Al-taschith, meaning "Do Not Destroy," appears in the titles of Psalms 57, 58, 59, and 75, possibly indicating a musical or literary term.

Amon@Jer.46.25-Nam=H0528.brief: Egyptian god; city in Nahum, probably Thebes
Amon@Jer.46.25-Nam=H0528.short: Amon, mentioned in Jeremiah 46:25; Nam.3.8, refers to the Egyptian god Amon and the city of Thebes, respectively.

Apharasthchite@Ezr.4.9-=H0671A.brief: Apharsathchites: A group opposing the rebuilding of Jerusalem's temple
Apharasthchite@Ezr.4.9-=H0671A.short: The Apharsathchites were a group that opposed the rebuilding of the temple in Jerusalem during the time of Ezra (Ezra 4:9; 5:6; 6:6).

Artemis@Act.19.24-=G0735.brief: Greek goddess worshipped in Ephesus, associated with fertility
Artemis@Act.19.24-=G0735.short: Artemis, a Greek goddess worshipped in Ephesus, was the focus of a major controversy during Paul's ministry in the city (Act.19.24, 27, 28, 34, 35).

Asherah@Exo.34.13-Mic=H0842.brief: Canaanite goddess; associated with wooden poles, idolatry
Asherah@Exo.34.13-Mic=H0842.short: Asherah, a Canaanite goddess, was worshipped by the Israelites through wooden poles or images, often leading them into idolatry.

Ashima@2Ki.17.30=H0807.brief: Deity worshipped by the people of Hamath
Ashima@2Ki.17.30=H0807.short: Ashima was a deity worshipped by the people of Hamath who were resettled in Samaria by the Assyrian king (2Ki.17.30).

Ashtaroth@Jdg.2.13-1Sa=H6252G.brief: A Canaanite goddess of fertility and war
Ashtaroth@Jdg.2.13-1Sa=H6252G.short: Ashtaroth was a Canaanite goddess of fertility and war whose worship was condemned in the Bible.

Ashtoreth@1Ki.11.5-2Ki=H6253.brief: A Syrian goddess of fertility and war
Ashtoreth@1Ki.11.5-2Ki=H6253.short: Ashtoreth, was a Sidonian goddess of fertility and war whose worship was condemned in the Bible.

Azazel@Lev.16.8-=H5799.brief: Mysterious figure connected to the Day of Atonement
Azazel@Lev.16.8-=H5799.short: Azazel, mentioned in Leviticus 16, is a mysterious figure connected to the scapegoat ritual on the Day of Atonement.

Baal@Num.25.3-Rom=H1168A.short: Baal-berith or El-berith, meaning "Lord of the Covenant" or "God of the Covenant," was a Canaanite deity worshipped by the Israelites in Shechem during the time of the judges (Judges 8:33; 9:4, 46).

Baal-berith@Jdg.8.33-=H1170.brief: Canaanite god of fertility and weather
Baal-berith@Jdg.8.33-=H1170.short: Baal, a Canaanite god of fertility and weather, and Peor, a Moabite god, were worshipped by the Israelites, leading them into idolatry and disobedience to the Lord.

Bear@Job.9.9-=H5906.brief: Constellation mentioned in God's discourse with Job
Bear@Job.9.9-=H5906.short: The Bear is a constellation referred to in God's speeches to Job, showcasing God's power and wisdom in creation.

Behemoth@Job.40.15=H0930.brief: A powerful, majestic creature described in the Bible
Behemoth@Job.40.15=H0930.short: Behemoth, mentioned in Job.40.15, is a powerful and majestic creature that God uses to illustrate His creative power and sovereignty.

Bel@Isa.46.1-Jer=H1078.short: Bel, a Babylonian god mentioned in Isaiah 46:1 and Jeremiah 50:2; 51:44), is associated with the god Marduk and is depicted as bowing down and being humiliated by the Lord.

Boaz@1Ki.7.21-2Ch=H1162H.brief: One of two bronze pillars in Solomon's Temple
Boaz@1Ki.7.21-2Ch=H1162H.short: Boaz was the name given to one of the two bronze pillars that stood at the entrance of Solomon's Temple (1Ki.7.21; 2Ch.3.17).

Booths_Festival@Jhn.7.2=G4634.brief: Jewish festival commemorating the Israelites' wilderness wanderings
Booths_Festival@Jhn.7.2=G4634.short: The Booths_Festival, also known as the Feast of Tabernacles or Sukkot, was a Jewish festival commemorating the Israelites' wilderness wanderings and God's provision (Jhn.7.2).

Bul@1Ki.6.38=H0945.brief: The eighth month in the ancient Hebrew calendar
Bul@1Ki.6.38=H0945.short: Bul, mentioned in 1Ki.6.38, is the eighth month in the ancient Hebrew calendar, corresponding to October-November in the modern calendar.

Chemosh@Num.21.29-Jer=H3645.brief: Moabite god, worshipped by Solomon and others
Chemosh@Num.21.29-Jer=H3645.short: Chemosh, the god of the Moabites, was worshipped by Solomon and the Israelites, leading them into idolatry.

Chislev@Neh.1.1-Zec=H3691.brief: The ninth month in the ancient Hebrew calendar
Chislev@Neh.1.1-Zec=H3691.short: Chislev, mentioned in Nehemiah 1:1 and Zechariah 7:1, is the ninth month in the ancient Hebrew calendar, corresponding to November-December in the modern calendar.

Chronicles@1Ki.14.19-Est=H1697O.brief: Historical records of the kings of Israel and Judah
Chronicles@1Ki.14.19-Est=H1697O.short: The Chronicles, mentioned throughout the books of Kings and Chronicles, were historical records of the reigns of the kings of Israel and Judah.

Dagon@Jdg.16.23-1Ch=H1712.brief: Philistine god whose temple was destroyed by Samson
Dagon@Jdg.16.23-1Ch=H1712.short: Dagon was the chief deity of the Philistines, with temples at Gaza and Ashdod.

Dedication_Festival@Jhn.10.22=G1456.brief: Jewish festival commemorating the rededication of the Temple
Dedication_Festival@Jhn.10.22=G1456.short: The Dedication_Festival, also known as Hanukkah, was a Jewish festival that commemorated the rededication of the Temple in Jerusalem (Jhn.10.22).

Destiny@Isa.65.11=H4507.brief: A pagan deity mentioned in the Book of Isaiah
Destiny@Isa.65.11=H4507.short: Destiny, mentioned in Isaiah 65:11, is a pagan deity associated with fate or fortune, which some Israelites worshipped, forsaking the Lord.

Elul@Neh.6.15=H0435.brief: The sixth month in the ancient Hebrew calendar
Elul@Neh.6.15=H0435.short: Elul, mentioned in Nehemiah 6:15, is the sixth month in the ancient Hebrew calendar, corresponding to August-September in the modern calendar.

Epicurean@Act.17.18=G1946.brief: A philosophical school in ancient Greece, mentioned in Acts
Epicurean@Act.17.18=G1946.short: Epicureans, mentioned in Act.17.18, were adherents of a philosophical school in ancient Greece that emphasized the pursuit of pleasure and the avoidance of pain.

Ethanim@1Ki.8.2=H0388.brief: The seventh month in the ancient Hebrew calendar
Ethanim@1Ki.8.2=H0388.short: Ethanim, mentioned in 1Ki.8.2, is the seventh month in the ancient Hebrew calendar, corresponding to September-October in the modern calendar.

Fortune@Isa.65.11=H1408.brief: A pagan deity associated with luck and prosperity
Fortune@Isa.65.11=H1408.short: Fortune, mentioned in Isaiah 65:11, is a pagan deity associated with luck and prosperity, which some Israelites worshipped, forsaking the Lord.

Freedmen@Act.6.9=G3032.brief: Former slaves who had been granted freedom
Freedmen@Act.6.9=G3032.short: The Freedmen, mentioned in Act.6.9, were likely former Jewish slaves who had been granted freedom and had their own synagogue in Jerusalem.

Gabriel@Dan.8.16-Luk=H1403.brief: An angel who delivers messages from God
Gabriel@Dan.8.16-Luk=H1403.short: Gabriel is an angel who appears in the Bible to deliver important messages from God, such as interpreting visions for Daniel (Dan.8.16; 9:21) and announcing the births of John the Baptist and Jesus (Luke 1:19, 26).

Gittith@Psa.8.1-=H1665.brief: A musical term in the superscriptions of Psalms
Gittith@Psa.8.1-=H1665.short: Gittith, mentioned in the superscriptions of Psalms 8, 81, and 84, is a musical term of uncertain meaning, possibly referring to a musical instrument, a tune, or a style associated with the city of Gath.

Hermes@Act.14.12=G2060G.brief: Greek god, associated with Paul and Barnabas
Hermes@Act.14.12=G2060G.short: In Act.14.12, the people of Lystra identified Paul as Hermes, the Greek god of messages and eloquence, because he was the chief speaker.

Herodian@Mat.22.16-Mrk=G2265.brief: A Jewish political party supporting the Herodian dynasty
Herodian@Mat.22.16-Mrk=G2265.short: The Herodians, mentioned in Matthew 22:16; Mrk.3.6; 12.13, were a Jewish political party that supported the rule of the Herodian dynasty and collaborated with the Pharisees in their opposition to Jesus.

Higgaion@Psa.9.16=H1902G.brief: A musical or literary term in the Psalms
Higgaion@Psa.9.16=H1902G.short: Higgaion, mentioned in Psalm 9:16, is a musical or literary term of uncertain meaning, possibly indicating a pause for meditation or reflection.

Hosanna@Mat.21.9-Jhn=G5614.brief: A Hebrew expression meaning "save now" or "save, please"
Hosanna@Mat.21.9-Jhn=G5614.short: Hosanna, a Hebrew expression meaning "save now" or "save, please," was shouted by the crowds during Jesus' triumphal entry into Jerusalem, acknowledging Him as the Messiah (Matthew 21:9, 15; Mrk.11.9-10; Jhn.12.13).

Jachin@1Ki.7.21-2Ch=H3199H.brief: One of two bronze pillars in Solomon's Temple
Jachin@1Ki.7.21-2Ch=H3199H.short: Jachin was the name given to one of the two bronze pillars that stood at the entrance of Solomon's Temple (1Ki.7.21; 2Ch.3.17).

Jonath-elem-rechokim@Psa.56.1=H3128.brief: A musical term in the superscription of Psalm 56
Jonath-elem-rechokim@Psa.56.1=H3128.short: Jonath-elem-rechokim, meaning "Dove on Far-off Terebinths," is a musical term or phrase found in the superscription of Psalm 56, possibly indicating the melody or musical setting to which the psalm was to be sung.

Judaism@Gal.1.13-=G2454.brief: The monotheistic religion of the Jewish people
Judaism@Gal.1.13-=G2454.short: In Galatians 1:13-14, Paul refers to his former way of life in Judaism, emphasizing his zealous adherence to the traditions of his ancestors before his conversion to Christianity.

Kiyyun@Amo.5.26=H3594.brief: Astral deity worshiped by Israelites, provoking God's judgment
Kiyyun@Amo.5.26=H3594.short: Kiyyun was an astral deity that the Israelites worshiped, leading to God's judgment and their exile.

Legion@Mrk.5.9-Luk=G3003.brief: Name of a demon or group of demons
Legion@Mrk.5.9-Luk=G3003.short: In the New Testament, Legion is the name given to a demon or group of demons that possessed a man in the region of the Gerasenes (Mrk.5.9; Luke 8:30).

Leviathan@Job.3.8-Isa=H3882.brief: A large sea creature mentioned in the Bible
Leviathan@Job.3.8-Isa=H3882.short: Leviathan is a large sea creature mentioned in several Old Testament passages, often associated with chaos, evil, or God's power over creation (Job.3.8; 41:1; Psalm 74:14; 104:26; Isaiah 27:1).

LORD@Gen.1.1-Rev=H3068G.brief: Names or title used to refer to God
LORD@Gen.1.1-Rev=H3068G.short: Throughout the Bible, God is referred to by various names and titles, each revealing different aspects of His character, nature, and relationship with His people.

Lucifer@Isa.14.12=H1966.brief: Symbolic name referring to the king of Babylon's fall
Lucifer@Isa.14.12=H1966.short: Isaiah poetically describes the king of Babylon as Lucifer, portraying his fall from power.

Mahalath@Psa.53.1-=H4257.brief: A musical or literary term in the Psalms
Mahalath@Psa.53.1-=H4257.short: Mahalath, mentioned in the superscriptions of Psalms 53 and 88, is a musical or literary term of uncertain meaning.

Maranatha@1Co.16.22=G3134.brief: An Aramaic expression meaning "Our Lord, come!"
Maranatha@1Co.16.22=G3134.short: Maranatha is an Aramaic expression that means "Our Lord, come!" and is used in 1Co.16.22 as a prayer for the Lord's return.

Maskil@Psa.32.1-=H4905.brief: A musical or literary term in the Psalms
Maskil@Psa.32.1-=H4905.short: Maskil is a term found in the superscriptions of several psalms, possibly indicating a contemplative or instructive psalm or a specific musical style.

Mazzaroth@Job.38.32=H4216.brief: A term related to astronomy or constellations
Mazzaroth@Job.38.32=H4216.short: Mazzaroth, mentioned in Job.38.32, is a term of uncertain meaning, possibly referring to constellations or the zodiac.

Merodach@Jer.50.2=H4781.short: Merodach, also known as Bel, was the chief god of the Babylonian pantheon.

Messiah@Jhn.1.41-=G3323.brief: The anointed one, a title for Jesus Christ.
Messiah@Jhn.1.41-=G3323.short: Messiah, meaning "anointed one," is a title used for Jesus Christ.

Miktam@Psa.16.1-=H4387.brief: A musical or literary term used in Psalm titles.
Miktam@Psa.16.1-=H4387.short: Miktam is a musical or literary term of uncertain meaning used in Psalm titles.

Molech@Lev.18.21-Act=H4432.brief: Canaanite deity associated with child sacrifice.
Molech@Lev.18.21-Act=H4432.short: Molech (or Milcom or Moloch) was a Canaanite deity associated with child sacrifice.

Muth-labben@Psa.9.1=H4192.brief: Musical term or tune in a psalm title
Muth-labben@Psa.9.1=H4192.short: Muth-labben, a phrase of uncertain meaning, appears in the title of Psalm 9.

Nazirites@Num.6.2-Amo=H5139.brief: Person who took a special vow of dedication
Nazirites@Num.6.2-Amo=H5139.short: A Nazirite was an individual who took a special vow of dedication to God, abstaining from wine, cutting hair, and avoiding corpses.

Nebo@Isa.46.1=H5015B.brief: A Babylonian god and a mountain in Moab
Nebo@Isa.46.1=H5015B.short: Nebo, mentioned in Isaiah 46:1, is a Babylonian god of wisdom and writing, and also the name of a mountain in Moab where Moses viewed the Promised Land before his death (Deu.32.49; 34:1).

Nehushtan@2Ki.18.4=H5180.brief: The bronze serpent made by Moses in the wilderness
Nehushtan@2Ki.18.4=H5180.short: Nehushtan, mentioned in 2Ki.18.4, was the name given to the bronze serpent that Moses made in the wilderness (Numbers 21:8-9), which had become an object of idolatrous worship by the time of King Hezekiah.

Nergal@2Ki.17.30=H5370.brief: A Mesopotamian god worshipped by the Assyrians
Nergal@2Ki.17.30=H5370.short: Nergal, mentioned in 2Ki.17.30, was a Mesopotamian god of war, pestilence, and the underworld, worshipped by the men of Cuth who were brought to Samaria by the Assyrians.

New_Moon@Col.2.16=G3561.brief: New Moon: A religious observance marking the beginning of months
New_Moon@Col.2.16=G3561.short: The New Moon, mentioned in Col.2.16, was a religious observance marking the beginning of each month in the Hebrew calendar, often celebrated with special sacrifices and feasts.

Nibhaz@2Ki.17.31=H5026.brief: Idol god worshiped by the Avvites in Samaria
Nibhaz@2Ki.17.31=H5026.short: Nibhaz was a deity worshiped by the Avvite people who settled in Samaria.

Nicolaitans@Rev.2.6-=G3531.brief: A group whose practices were condemned by Jesus
Nicolaitans@Rev.2.6-=G3531.short: The Nicolaitans, mentioned in Revelation 2:6; 2:15, were a group whose practices were hated by Jesus and condemned by the early church.

Nisroch@2Ki.19.37-Isa=H5268.brief: An Assyrian deity, possibly associated with agriculture
Nisroch@2Ki.19.37-Isa=H5268.short: Nisroch, mentioned in 2Ki.19.37; Isaiah 37:38, was an Assyrian deity in whose temple King Sennacherib was worshipping when he was assassinated by his sons.

Omega@Rev.1.8-=G5598.brief: A title of Jesus, signifying His eternal nature
Omega@Rev.1.8-=G5598.short: In Revelation 1:8, 21:6; 22:13, Jesus is referred to as "the Alpha and the Omega," a title that emphasizes His eternal nature and His role as the beginning and the end of all things.

Orion@Job.9.9-Amo=H3685G.brief: A prominent constellation mentioned in the Bible
Orion@Job.9.9-Amo=H3685G.short: Orion, a prominent constellation, is mentioned in Job.9.9, 38:31; Amo.5.8 as a display of God's power and creative work in the heavens.

Passover@Exo.12.11-Heb=H6453.brief: An annual Jewish feast commemorating the Exodus
Passover@Exo.12.11-Heb=H6453.short: The Passover is an annual Jewish feast that commemorates the deliverance of the Israelites from slavery in Egypt, as described in Exodus 12, and is celebrated with specific rituals and offerings as prescribed in the Old Testament and observed in the New Testament.

Pharisee@Mat.3.7-Php=G5330.brief: A strict Jewish sect known for legalism and hypocrisy
Pharisee@Mat.3.7-Php=G5330.short: The Pharisees were a Jewish sect known for their strict observance of the law and oral traditions, often clashing with Jesus over matters of ritual purity, Sabbath regulations, and His claims to divine authority (Matthew 23; Luke 11:37-54).

Pleiades@Job.9.9-Amo=H3598.brief: A star cluster mentioned as a display of God's power
Pleiades@Job.9.9-Amo=H3598.short: The Pleiades are a star cluster mentioned in Job.9.9; 38:31 as a display of God's creative power and in Amo.5.8 as evidence of God's control over the natural world.

Preparation_Festival@Mat.27.62-Jhn=G3904.brief: The day before the Sabbath or Passover
Preparation_Festival@Mat.27.62-Jhn=G3904.short: The day of Preparation was the day before the Sabbath (Mrk.15.42; Luke 23:54) or the day before the Passover (Jhn.19.14, 31, 42).

Purim@Est.3.7-=H6332.brief: Jewish festival commemorating the events in the book of Esther
Purim@Est.3.7-=H6332.short: Purim is the Jewish festival celebrating the deliverance of the Jews from Haman's plot to destroy them, as recorded in the book of Esther (Esther 9:26-32).

Raca@Mat.5.22=G4469.brief: An Aramaic term of contempt meaning "empty-headed"
Raca@Mat.5.22=G4469.short: Raca is an Aramaic term of contempt, meaning "empty-headed" or "foolish," which Jesus warned against using to insult others, equating it with murder (Matthew 5:22).

Rahab@Job.9.13-Isa=H7294.brief: A poetic name for Egypt, representing a mythical sea monster
Rahab@Job.9.13-Isa=H7294.short: Rahab is a poetic name for Egypt, often represented as a mythical sea monster that God defeated, symbolizing His power over the nations (Psalm 89:10; Isaiah 51:9).

Rephan@Act.7.43=G4481.brief: A pagan deity worshipped by the Israelites in the wilderness
Rephan@Act.7.43=G4481.short: Rephan was a pagan deity worshipped by the Israelites in the wilderness, for which God allowed them to be carried into exile (Act.7.43).

Rimmon@2Ki.5.18=H7417A.brief: A Syrian deity worshipped by Naaman
Rimmon@2Ki.5.18=H7417A.short: Rimmon was a Syrian deity worshipped by Naaman, who asked for God's pardon for bowing down in Rimmon's temple (2Ki.5.18).

Sabbath@Exo.16.23-Heb=H7676.brief: The seventh day of the week, set apart for rest and worship
Sabbath@Exo.16.23-Heb=H7676.short: The Sabbath, meaning "rest," was the seventh day of the week, set apart by God as a holy day for rest and worship (Exodus 20:8-11; Leviticus 23:3).

Sadducee@Mat.3.7-Act=G4523.brief: A Jewish sect that denied the resurrection and spirits
Sadducee@Mat.3.7-Act=G4523.short: The Sadducees were a Jewish sect that denied the resurrection, angels, and spirits, and often clashed with Jesus and the early church (Matthew 22:23; Act.23.6-8).

Satan@Deu.13.13-Rev=H7854.brief: The adversary, the devil, the tempter of humanity
Satan@Deu.13.13-Rev=H7854.short: Satan, meaning "adversary" or "accuser," is the devil, the chief enemy of God and tempter of humanity, who seeks to hinder God's purposes and lead people into sin (Job.1.6-12; Matthew 4:1-11; Revelation 12:9).

Selah@Psa.3.2-Hab=H5542.brief: A musical or liturgical term of uncertain meaning
Selah@Psa.3.2-Hab=H5542.short: Selah is a term frequently used in the Psalms and Habakkuk, likely a musical or liturgical direction, though its precise meaning is uncertain (Psalm 3:2, 4, 8; Habakkuk 3:3, 9, 13).

Shebat@Zec.1.7=H7627.brief: The eleventh month of the Jewish calendar
Shebat@Zec.1.7=H7627.short: Shebat is the eleventh month of the Jewish calendar, mentioned in Zechariah 1:7 as the date of one of the prophet's visions.

Sheminith@1Ch.15.21-Psa=H8067.brief: A musical term of uncertain meaning
Sheminith@1Ch.15.21-Psa=H8067.short: Sheminith is a musical term that appears in the titles of Psalms 6; 12; 1Ch.15.21, possibly referring to a musical instrument, a part in music, or a melody.

Shibboleth@Jdg.12.6=H7641H.brief: A Hebrew word used to identify Ephraimites
Shibboleth@Jdg.12.6=H7641H.short: Shibboleth was a Hebrew word used by the Gileadites to identify Ephraimites, who could not pronounce it correctly, resulting in the death of 42,000 Ephraimites (Judges 12:6).

Shiggaion@Psa.7.1=H7692G.brief: A musical term in the title of Psalm 7
Shiggaion@Psa.7.1=H7692G.short: Shiggaion is a musical term that appears in the title of Psalm 7, possibly indicating a specific style or genre of music.

Shigionoth@Hab.3.1=H7692H.brief: A musical term in the title of Habakkuk's prayer
Shigionoth@Hab.3.1=H7692H.short: Shigionoth is a musical term that appears in the title of Habakkuk's prayer in Habakkuk 3:1, possibly indicating a specific style or genre of music.

Shimeathite@1Ch.2.55=H8101.brief: A Kenite clan skilled in scribal arts
Shimeathite@1Ch.2.55=H8101.short: The Shimeathites were a Kenite clan known for their scribal skills, mentioned in 1Ch.2.55 among the descendants of Salma.

Shushan_Eduth@Psa.60.1=H7802.brief: A musical term or tune in the title of Psalm 60
Shushan_Eduth@Psa.60.1=H7802.short: Shushan Eduth, meaning "Lily of the Testimony," is a musical term or tune mentioned in the title of Psalm 60, possibly referring to a specific melody or musical setting.

Sikkuth@Amo.5.26=H5522.brief: A pagan deity worshipped by the Israelites
Sikkuth@Amo.5.26=H5522.short: Sikkuth, possibly an Assyrian deity, was one of the pagan gods worshipped by the Israelites, for which they were condemned to exile (Amo.5.26).

Sivan@Est.8.9=H5510.brief: The third month of the Jewish calendar
Sivan@Est.8.9=H5510.short: Sivan is the third month of the Jewish calendar, mentioned in Esther 8:9 as the month in which Mordecai's decree was written and sent to the provinces.

Stoic@Act.17.18=G4770.brief: A Greek philosophical school encountered by Paul in Athens
Stoic@Act.17.18=G4770.short: The Stoics were a Greek philosophical school that emphasized reason, self-control, and the acceptance of fate, some of whom debated with Paul in Athens (Act.17.18).

Sucathite@1Ch.2.55=H7756.brief: A Kenite clan skilled in scribal arts
Sucathite@1Ch.2.55=H7756.short: The Sucathites were a Kenite clan known for their scribal skills, mentioned in 1Ch.2.55 among the descendants of Salma.
