Succoth-benoth@2Ki.17.30=H5524.brief: A Babylonian deity worshipped by the Sepharvites
Succoth-benoth@2Ki.17.30=H5524.short: Succoth-benoth was a Babylonian deity worshipped by the Sepharvites, one of the peoples settled in Samaria by the Assyrian king (2Ki.17.30).

Tammuz@Ezk.8.14=H8542.brief: A Mesopotamian deity mourned by women in Jerusalem
Tammuz@Ezk.8.14=H8542.short: Tammuz, a Mesopotamian deity, was mourned by women at the north gate of the Jerusalem temple, a practice condemned by Ezekiel (Ezk.8.14).

Tarpelite@Ezr.4.9=H2967.brief: A group of officials in the Persian Empire
Tarpelite@Ezr.4.9=H2967.short: The Tarpelites were a group of officials in the Persian Empire who opposed the rebuilding of Jerusalem during the time of Ezra (Ezra 4:9).

Tartak@2Ki.17.31=H8662.brief: An Avvite deity worshipped in Samaria
Tartak@2Ki.17.31=H8662.short: Tartak was a deity worshipped by the Avvites, one of the peoples settled in Samaria by the Assyrian king (2Ki.17.31).

Tebeth@Est.2.16=H2887.brief: The tenth month of the Jewish calendar
Tebeth@Est.2.16=H2887.short: Tebeth is the tenth month of the Jewish calendar, mentioned in Esther 2:16 as the month in which Esther was taken to King Ahasuerus.

Thummim@Exo.28.30-Neh=H8550.brief: Objects used with the Urim for divine guidance
Thummim@Exo.28.30-Neh=H8550.short: The Thummim, along with the Urim, were objects carried in the breastpiece of the high priest's ephod and used to seek divine guidance (Exodus 28:30; Numbers 27:21).

Tirathite@1Ch.2.55=H8654.brief: A Kenite clan skilled in scribal arts
Tirathite@1Ch.2.55=H8654.short: The Tirathites were a Kenite clan known for their scribal skills, mentioned in 1Ch.2.55 among the descendants of Salma.

Urim@Exo.28.30-Neh=H0224.brief: Objects used with the Thummim for divine guidance
Urim@Exo.28.30-Neh=H0224.short: The Urim, along with the Thummim, were objects carried in the breastpiece of the high priest's ephod and used to seek divine guidance (Exodus 28:30; Numbers 27:21).

Weeks@Exo.34.22-1Co=H7620G.brief: A Jewish agricultural festival celebrated 50 days after Passover
Weeks@Exo.34.22-1Co=H7620G.short: The Feast of Weeks, also known as Pentecost, was a Jewish agricultural festival celebrated fifty days after Passover, commemorating the wheat harvest and the giving of the Law at Sinai.

Zealot@Mat.10.4-Mrk=G2581.brief: A member of a Jewish political faction
Zealot@Mat.10.4-Mrk=G2581.short: The Zealots were a Jewish political faction known for their fierce opposition to Roman rule and their advocacy for armed resistance (Matthew 10:4; Mrk.3.18).

Zeus@Act.14.12-=G2203.brief: The chief god in Greek mythology
Zeus@Act.14.12-=G2203.short: Zeus, the chief god in Greek mythology, was identified with the Roman god Jupiter and was worshipped in Lystra (Act.14.12-13).

Ziv@1Ki.6.1-=H2099.brief: The second month in the ancient Hebrew calendar
Ziv@1Ki.6.1-=H2099.short: Ziv, the second month in the ancient Hebrew calendar, is mentioned in connection with the construction of Solomon's Temple (1Ki.6.1, 37).

Latin@Luk.23.38-Jhn=G4515.brief: Language used in the inscription on Jesus' cross
Latin@Luk.23.38-Jhn=G4515.short: Latin, along with Greek and Hebrew, was one of the languages used in the inscription placed above Jesus' cross during His crucifixion (Luke 23:38; Jhn.19.20).

Aramaic@2Ki.18.26-Rev=H0762.brief: Semitic languages used in the Bible and ancient Near East
Aramaic@2Ki.18.26-Rev=H0762.short: Aramaic and Hebrew are Semitic languages used in various passages of the Bible, with Hebrew being the primary language of the Old Testament and Aramaic appearing in some later texts.

Greek@Isa.66.19-Rev=G1673.brief: A language used in the New Testament
Greek@Isa.66.19-Rev=G1673.short: Greek, one of the original languages of the New Testament, is mentioned in Luke 23:38, Jhn.19.20, Act.21.37; Revelation 9:11, highlighting its widespread use in the Roman Empire during the time of Jesus and the early church.

Hebrew@2Ki.18.26-Isa=H3066.short: Hebrew was the language spoken by the Jews, as evidenced by its use in communication and writings (2Ki.18.26; 2Ch.32.18; Neh.13.24; Isa.36.11, 13).

Gentiles@Gen.10.5-Rev=H1471G.brief: A non-Jewish person; someone from the nations
Gentiles@Gen.10.5-Rev=H1471G.short: In the Bible, the term "Gentile" refers to non-Jewish people or those from the nations, and their relationship with God and the Jewish people is a significant theme throughout Scripture.

Asiarch@Act.19.31=G0775.brief: High-ranking officials in the Roman province of Asia
Asiarch@Act.19.31=G0775.short: The Asiarchs, mentioned in Act.19.31, were high-ranking officials in the Roman province of Asia who had a friendly relationship with Paul.

Candace@Act.8.27=G2582.brief: Queen of Ethiopia, her eunuch met Philip
Candace@Act.8.27=G2582.short: Candacé, the queen of Ethiopia, is mentioned in Act.8.27 in connection with her eunuch, who was baptized by Philip.

Rabbi@Mat.23.7-Jhn=G4461.brief: A Jewish title of respect for a teacher
Rabbi@Mat.23.7-Jhn=G4461.short: Rabbi, meaning "my teacher," was a title of respect used by Jews to address their religious teachers and leaders (Matthew 23:7-8; Jhn.1.38, 49).

Seraph@Isa.6.2-=H8314B.brief: Angelic beings that attend to God's throne
Seraph@Isa.6.2-=H8314B.short: Seraphim are angelic beings that surround God's throne, each having six wings and praising His holiness (Isaiah 6:2-6).

Teraphim@Gen.31.19-Zec=H8655.brief: Household gods or idols used for divination and worship
Teraphim@Gen.31.19-Zec=H8655.short: Teraphim were household gods or idols used for divination and worship, often associated with pagan practices and condemned in the Bible (Genesis 31:19; 2Ki.23.24; Ezk.21.21).

Abaddon@Job.26.6-Pro=H0011.brief: A Hebrew term for the realm of the dead
Abaddon@Job.26.6-Pro=H0011.short: Abaddon is a Hebrew term used in the Old Testament to refer to the realm of the dead or the place of destruction.

Sheol@Gen.37.35-Rev=H7585.brief: The underworld; the abode of the dead in the Bible
Sheol@Gen.37.35-Rev=H7585.short: Sheol, also referred to as the Pit, Gehenna, Tartarus, or Hades, is the biblical concept of the underworld or the abode of the dead, often associated with darkness, stillness, and separation from God.

H5983: – after "@":     the first instance where that person/place occurs, unless the identity is uncertain and there is another that is certain. EG most common name is used for Abraham@Gen.11.26 where he is actually called Abram; the certain form is used for Ammon@Deu.2.19-Zep=H5983
